Getty Images
鈴木誠也 最新情報
　シカゴ・カブスに所属する32歳の鈴木誠也外野手に対し、同球団が1年総額2315万ドル（約36億6000万円）のクオリファイング・オファー（QO）を提示した。同選手はこのオファーを拒否する見通しだと、米メディア『NBCスポーツ』が報じている。
QOは、フリーエージェント（FA）となる選手に球団が提示する1年契約のオファーである。
選手が拒否して他球団と契約した場合、元の球団はドラフト指名権の補償を受けられる仕組みだ。
同メディアのジョージ・ビッセル記者は、鈴木について「今オフのFA市場において、おそらく最高の野手」と評価している。
ただ、2012年にQO制度が始まって以降、提示を受けた157人のうち「受諾したのはわずか18人」にとどまるようだ。
2026年シーズンの鈴木は、545打席で打率.270、出塁率.368、長打率.473、26本塁打、86打点、96得点を記録。
2022年にカブスへ加入してから5シーズンのうち4シーズンで20本塁打以上をマークしており、同メディアは安定した長打力の持ち主として鈴木を評している。
 
一方、カブスはイアン・ハップ外野手とマシュー・ボイド投手にはQOを提示しなかった。
同メディアはこの判断について「注目に値する」と伝えている。
鈴木の評価は他のメディアでも高い。
米公式サイト『MLB.com』のマーク・フェインサンド記者が選んだFA選手トップ30では、鈴木は全体5位にランクインしている。
ただし、打球の質には陰りも見える。
同メディアは、鈴木のハードヒット率が2023〜2025年の48.6％から、2026年は38.9％に低下したと指摘している。
8月に32歳を迎えた鈴木が、今オフの野手市場の目玉として、どの球団と契約を結ぶのか注目が集まりそうだ。

A
item.content:encoded:
Según un informe reciente de Andy Kostka de The Baltimore Banner, los Baltimore Orioles estarían dispuestos a escuchar ofertas por “la mayoría” de los jugadores de su roster.
Como era de esperar, el único jugador “intocable” del roster es Pete Alonso.
Darragh McDonald de MLBTR.com reaccionó enseguida a la noticia y escribió:
Conviene subrayar que no es lo mismo intentar cambiar jugadores de forma activa que estar dispuesto a escuchar ofertas, una distinción que Kostka deja clara en su informe. Aun así, llama la atención que la directiva de Baltimore llegue a la temporada baja dispuesta a considerar cambios profundos. Esa postura se entiende: los Orioles pasaron de 2018 a 2021 entre los peores equipos del béisbol en una estrategia de reconstrucción para acumular talento joven.
Cabe recordar que los Orioles cambiaron a Adley Rustchman a principios de esta temporada, lo que pudo ser una primera señal de que se avecinaba una venta masiva de jugadores.
Como los Atlanta Braves necesitan con urgencia un campocorto titular, veamos qué podrían ofrecerles a los Orioles a cambio de Gunnar Henderson.
Más sobre MLB en Heavy: Exjugador de New York Yankees durante siete años sigue como agente libre tras quedar fuera de la organización
¿Qué podrían ofrecer los Braves a los Orioles por Gunnar Henderson?
Gunnar Henderson es uno de los campocortos con más proyección de poder en toda la MLB.
En sus cinco años de carrera en la MLB, Henderson ganó el premio al Novato del Año de la Liga Americana, fue elegido para el Juego de Estrellas y conectó 110 jonrones en 655 partidos.
Si los Orioles de verdad están escuchando ofertas por Henderson, los Atlanta Braves deberían interesarse sin duda.
Este paquete de cambio podría beneficiar a ambos equipos:
- Los Orioles reciben: al abridor JR Ritchie, al jardinero Brewer Hicklen y a los prospectos Alex Lodise y Owen Murphy
- Los Braves reciben: al campocorto Gunnar Henderson
Hay que tener en cuenta que Gunnar Henderson aún no firma una extensión de contrato y no será agente libre hasta 2029, lo que eleva su valor en un posible cambio.
Más sobre MLB en Heavy: New York Yankees reciben un mensaje sobre Anthony Volpe ante una decisión sobre Jazz Chisholm Jr.
Por qué tiene sentido que Gunnar Henderson llegue a los Braves
La llegada de Gunnar Henderson a los Braves tiene sentido porque Atlanta ha tenido serios problemas en el campocorto durante los últimos dos años. Mauricio Dubon puede cubrir esa posición en su papel de jugador versátil, pero quizá la mayor necesidad del equipo esta temporada baja sea un campocorto.
Y si Atlanta no quiere gastar una fortuna en un agente libre de primer nivel —además, hay pocos disponibles—, adquirir a Henderson mediante un cambio tiene mucho sentido. Incluso algunos aficionados de los Braves ya han planteado la idea.
Parece imposible que Ha-Seong Kim regrese a Atlanta, y Dubon también es agente libre. Sin embargo, es probable que Dubon firme un contrato de varios años con Atlanta. Según cómo juegue Mike Yastrzemski, quizá le convenga más al equipo usarlo como jardinero izquierdo con bastante tiempo de juego.
En 2026, Gunnar Henderson bateó para .226 con 24 jonrones, 27 dobles y un OPS+ de 102.

Still, it’s notab
item.content:encoded:
According to a recent report by Andy Kostka of The Baltimore Banner, the Baltimore Orioles are reportedly open to trading ‘a majority’ of the players on their roster.
As one would imagine, the only ‘untouchable’ on their roster is Pete Alonso.
MLBTR.com’s Darragh McDonald quickly hit the recent news and wrote:
It’s worth emphasizing that there’s a difference between actively trying to trade players and being open to offers, a distinction that Kostka clearly makes in his report. Still, it’s notable that the Baltimore front office is going into the offseason with the willingness to consider sweeping changes. The openness is certainly understandable. The Orioles did a big tank job from 2018 to 2021, placing themselves as one of the worst clubs in baseball for that stretch in order to stockpile young talent.
Worth noting, the Orioles traded Adley Rustchman earlier this season, which could have been an early sign of a fire sale.
With the Atlanta Braves in desperate need of an everyday shortstop, let’s take a quick look at what a trade package could look like between the Orioles and Braves for Gunnar Henderson.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees 7-Year Player Still a Free Agent After Release From Organization
What Could Braves-Orioles Deal Look Like for Gunnar Henderson?
Gunnar Henderson is one of the most promising shortstops in all of MLB from a power standpoint.
In his 5-year MLB career, Henderson has won the AL Rookie of the Year, been named an All-Star, and has clubbed 110 home runs in 655 total games played.
If the Orioles are actually taking offers on a potential trade, the Atlanta Braves should absolutely be interested.
Here’s a trade package that could benefit both parties in this instance:
- Orioles receive: SP JR Ritchie, OF Brewer Hicklen, prospects Alex Lodise and Owen Murphy
- Braves receive: SS Gunnar Henderson
It’s important to note that Gunnar Henderson has yet to sign a contract extension and isn’t a free agent until 2029, which certainly drives the price up a bit on his trade status.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Dealt Anthony Volpe Message Amid Jazz Chisholm Jr. Decision
Why Gunnar Henderson to the Braves Makes Sense
Gunnar Henderson to the Braves makes sense because Atlanta has dealt with major issues at the shortstop position for the last two years. Sure, Mauricio Dubon can slot in as the team’s shortstop in a utility role, but perhaps the Braves’ biggest need this offseason is a SS.
And if Atlanta doesn’t want to spend the big bucks in free agency for a top-of-the-market option (there aren’t many, anyway), trading for Henderson makes a lot of sense, and even some of the Braves faithful have already tried to float the idea.
There’s no way that Ha-Seong Kim is being brought back to Atlanta, and even Dubon is a free agent. However, it feels likely that Dubon will ink a multi-year deal with Atlanta, but he could be better suited for the team as a semi-everyday left fielder, depending on how Mike Yastrzemski is playing.
In 2026, Gunnar Henderson batted .226 with 24 home runs, 27 doubles, and logged an OPS+ of 102.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Tarik Skubal Reunion With Tigers Comes With One Big Catch
item.dc:creator: Michael Whitaker
item.description: The Tarik Skubal era with the Detroit Tigers came to a close in early August when he was traded to the then-defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers in exchange for a package that included a trio of prospects. Skubal helped the Dodgers win their division and advance to the National League Championship Series, but they were stunningly swept by the Milwaukee Brewers, who went on to win their first World Series title over the Tampa Bay Rays. Now, the offseason is here, and Skubal is in l
item.content:encoded:
The Tarik Skubal era with the Detroit Tigers came to a close in early August when he was traded to the then-defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers in exchange for a package that included a trio of prospects.
Skubal helped the Dodgers win their division and advance to the National League Championship Series, but they were stunningly swept by the Milwaukee Brewers, who went on to win their first World Series title over the Tampa Bay Rays.
Now, the offseason is here, and Skubal is in line to potentially land the richest contract ever given to an MLB pitcher, which would surpass the records set by former Tigers Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer.
The question on the minds of Tigers fans everywhere is whether a reunion with the two-time Cy Young Award winner is possible. According to an ESPN analyst, it is, but there's a catch that could significantly hamper those chances.
The Detroit Tigers Are Reportedly Monitoring Tark Skubal's Free Agency
Skubal is now officially an unrestricted free agent, and has the chance to cash in potentially as the highest-paid MLB pitcher in history.
According to ESPN's Kiley McDaniel, there is a chance that he could return to the Tigers, who are reportedly monitoring his free agency period, but that he would have to accept a discount to come back.
"As covered in that panel piece, the usual suspects are believed to be at the front of the line for Skubal: The Dodgers and Mets are the primary bidders, the Tigers are monitoring for a discount, the Yankees are thinking about it (and then trading from their pitching stockpile if they land Skubal), and the Angels, White Sox, and Padres are the sleepers with ownership changes behind the interest," McDaniel wrote on ESPN.
The fact that Skubal and the Tigers were not able to come to an agreement on a new contract before he was traded, combined with the report that he'd allegedly have to accept a discount to return to Detroit, doesn't exactly bode well for the chances of a reunion.
Tarik Skubal Did Say That He'd Welcome A Return To The Tigers
Not long after he was traded to the Dodgers, Skubal explained that he would welcome a return to the Tigers, though he didn't go into any detail regarding any financial stipulations.
"I would love to play my whole career in Detroit," Skubal said during an appearance on the "Pardon My Take" podcast. "I would love to. And hopefully those negotiations pick back up in November once the playoffs are done. And we'll see where that goes.
"Hopefully they're involved with everything; I would love to return. I've got nothing but good things to say about the City of Detroit and the manager, the coaching, the staff, the trainers, the teammates; it's tough.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Tarik Skubal Reunion With Tigers Comes With One Big Catch appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers Should Target King as Skubal Alternative
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Solano
item.description: Tarik Skubal is the unquestioned top player available in free agency, with a legitimate opportunity to establish new contract records for a pitcher. His market could dictate the pace of the entire offseason. Teams interested in other starting pitchers may wait for Skubal to sign before committing their money elsewhere, while his eventual contract could also influence negotiations involving several of the leading free agents. The Los Angeles Dodgers would have a significant opening to address in
item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal is the unquestioned top player available in free agency, with a legitimate opportunity to establish new contract records for a pitcher.
His market could dictate the pace of the entire offseason.
Teams interested in other starting pitchers may wait for Skubal to sign before committing their money elsewhere, while his eventual contract could also influence negotiations involving several of the leading free agents.
The Los Angeles Dodgers would have a significant opening to address in their rotation should they fail to re-sign Skubal.
Right-hander Michael King represents a familiar alternative who could join Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Shohei Ohtani and Roki Sasaki in the starting rotation.
How King fits with Dodgers
King was easily the San Diego Padres' ace last season, going 12-10 with a 3.21 ERA and 1.18 WHIP in 185 innings over 32 starts.
The right-hander raised his performance during the postseason. King allowed only one run on five hits in 14 innings over three appearances (two starts), recording an 0.64 ERA and 0.71 WHIP with 15 strikeouts and one save.
That combination of effectiveness and availability would make King an appealing fit for Los Angeles.
He will turn 32 in May, meaning this offseason could represent his final opportunity to secure a long-term contract worth nine figures.
King is arguably the second-best starting pitcher available behind Skubal and should receive the substantial agreement he is seeking.
King's upside
Los Angeles would not be acquiring King to reproduce everything Skubal provides. Instead, the Dodgers would be adding another established starter capable of handling a significant workload and taking the ball in important games.
His presence could help distribute innings throughout a rotation filled with accomplished pitchers who have also dealt with availability concerns.
King's experience in different assignments would offer the Dodgers additional flexibility.
He has demonstrated that he can work as a traditional starter, appear in another capacity during the postseason and remain effective when the circumstances surrounding his role change.
That adaptability becomes particularly useful during October, when teams often abandon regular-season pitching patterns.
His postseason performance also showed that the pressure surrounding meaningful games does not prevent him from executing. Los Angeles needs pitchers who can handle the expectations attached to a roster built to contend for the World Series every year.
King would also provide an alternative that prevents the Dodgers from treating Skubal as their only acceptable outcome.
Skubal deserves to command an enormous contract, but Los Angeles must remain prepared to redirect its resources should another team present an offer it is unwilling to match.
Signing King would still require a considerable investment. However, his durability, adaptability and ability to perform in the postseason would make him a sensible replacement option rather than merely a consolation prize.

item.content:encoded:
The San Diego Padres have a well-known need at the top of their starting rotation.
If everyone from the group of Michael King, Casey Mize, Walker Buehler, Nick Pivetta, Robbie Ray and Griffin Canning sign elsewhere in free agency, the middle and back of the rotation could use help, too.
To that end, FanSided's Robert Murray dropped the names of both top-of-the-rotation starters in the 2026-27 free agent class as possible Padres targets: Freddy Peralta and Tarik Skubal.
Both pitchers would help a paper-thin Padres rotation in 2027 and beyond. Peralta, 30, was recently named MVP of the American League Championship Series. After a rocky start to the regular season with the New York Mets, the right-hander went 2-1 with a 2.95 ERA in five postseason games with the AL champion Rays.
And then there's Skubal. The two-time Cy Young Award winner reportedly has interest in returning to Los Angeles after going from the Detroit Tigers to the Dodgers in a blockbuster midseason trade.
The left-hander is the obvious crown jewel of the free agent class, and is being predicted to sign the most lucrative contract ever for a pitcher. That immediately positions the Dodgers and New York Mets — owner Steve Cohen already doled out the largest contract ever for a position player — as the favorites within the industry to sign the 29-year-old left-hander.
Speaking on The Baseball Insiders on Monday, Murray said the Padres "might end up being the sleeper team for Tarik Skubal."
"That new ownership group there, they got a taste of what winning was like," Murray said. "They got to see how competitive that baseball team was. They got to see how [Petco Park] just absolutely rocks. They have a GM in AJ Preller who will explore anything. And I could see, very easily, the San Diego Padres exploring the waters for Tarik Skubal."
Murray noted that Preller already gave one Scott Boras client, shortstop Xander Bogaerts, the long-term contract (11 years, $280 million) he was seeking. He also speculated that Skubal could be looking for a $400 million deal.
"We're still figuring out this new ownership group, but you have to imagine if AJ Preller wants someone of that caliber, he's going to pitch every idea he can to that new ownership group," Murray said.
For now, the link between the Padres and Skubal is just conjecture. But Murray just offered a couple reasons not to rule it out.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on Facebook and X/Twitter for the latest news.
J.P. Hoornstra is an On SI Contributor. A veteran of 20 years of sports coverage for daily newspapers in California, J.P. covered MLB, the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Los Angeles Angels (occasionally of Anaheim) from 2012-23 for the Southern California News Group. His first book, The 50 Greatest Dodgers Games of All-Time, published in 2015. In 2016, he won an Associated Press Sports Editors award for breaking news coverage. He once recorded a keyboard solo on the same album as two of the original Doors.

item.content:encoded:
大物FAがひしめく今オフのMLB市場で、日本人選手が補強の切り札として脚光を浴びている。中でも阪神からポスティングシステムでメジャー移籍を目指す佐藤輝明内野手（27）をめぐっては、名門同士の宿敵対決が勃発する可能性がありそうだ。
米有力紙「ニューヨーク・タイムズ」傘下のスポーツ専門サイト「ジ・アスレチック」は3日（現地時間）、レッズとナショナルズでGMを務めたジム・ボウデン氏による全30球団の今冬の補強課題を特集。同氏が各球団のフロントに聞き取りを行い、日本人選手を補強候補とみる球団の顔ぶれを分析した。
まず佐藤だ。今季打率3割6厘、39本塁打、106打点で3冠王に輝いた左の大砲には複数の需要がある。レッドソックスは打線の強化を最優先課題に掲げ、三塁を守れる佐藤が補強ポイントに合致するとみている。ヤンキースについても、ボウデン氏は内野陣の再編に絡めて獲得を提言。打線の中軸を担う新たな強打者として期待を寄せる。右打ちの長距離砲を探すマリナーズも、左打ちの佐藤を候補の一人に挙げた。東西の人気球団が争奪戦を演じても不思議ではない。
一方、カブスからFAとなった鈴木誠也外野手（32）は、2日（同3日）に古巣からクオリファイング・オファー（QO）を提示されたが、他球団からも熱視線を浴びそうだ。今季26本塁打、86打点をマークした右の強打者に対し、外野強化が急務のオリオールズには適任と評価。フィリーズも最優先補強ポイントの外野で、鈴木とマリナーズからFAとなったランディ・アロザレーナを有力な選択肢に据える。打線の立て直しを図るブルージェイズも獲得に動くと予測され、マリナーズも候補に加わる。4球団の思惑が交錯する構図だ。
同じくカブスからFAとなった今永昇太投手（33）には、先発陣の強化を急ぐブレーブスが浮上した。今季11勝を挙げた左腕は、大物先発のトレード獲得が実現しない場合、マイケル・キングやソニー・グレイらと並んで獲得を検討する候補という。
12月1日（同2日）の労使協定失効とロックアウトの懸念が迫る中、日本人選手をめぐる争奪戦も時間との勝負になりそうだ。

item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Free Agency class faces a difficult proposition ahead of what could very well be a league-wide lockout that begins at 9 p.m. PT on Tuesday, Dec. 1.
According to Jeff Passan of ESPN, Tarik Skubal is expected to sign with a team before the current collective bargaining agreement (CBA) expires.
Skubal is far and away the best player in this class, and the expectation is he will sign before the Dec. 1 lockout.
All MLB free agents are incentivized to sign free-market contracts before the possible lockout because of the uncertainty surrounding what may happen with the new CBA.
There will be a suspension of all negations and signings until a new CBA is agreed upon. Most importantly, players could be looking at a scenario where their earning potential is lowered if ownership gets its way and implements a salary cap in the new CBA.
As the top free-agent target in the Majors, Skubal’s best opportunity to secure the biggest possible payday may very well be before the Dec. 1 deadline of sorts. The adoption of a salary cap in MLB is not guaranteed, but the possibility still presents a threat to Skubal and the remainder of free agents this season.
This scenario could also be the Los Angeles Dodgers’ best chance to re-sign Skubal. If the owners are successful in their push for a salary cap — or more punitive penalties on spending — it is highly unlikely that the Dodgers will have the wherewithal to get a deal done.
There is a possibility that a salary cap will not be included in the new CBA, but signing Skubal before the deadline is the only way for the Dodgers to ensure they have the opportunity to offer him a contract.
Blake Snell recruiting Tarik Skubal
Skubal quickly endeared himself to his new Dodgers teammates this past season and expressed on multiple occasions how much he enjoyed his time with the organization.
He grew especially close to fellow left-hander Blake Snell, and they both often jokingly referred to the other as his “little brother.”
The feeling was mutual for Snell, who has said he will do his part to recruit Skubal back to the Dodgers.
After the Dodgers were eliminated by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, Skubal declined to answer any questions about his impending free agency.

item.content:encoded:
Phillies' Luis Arraez gets $54M contract projection from ESPN amid 'plenty of demand' originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Philadelphia Phillies acquired second baseman Luis Arraez at the MLB trade deadline from the San Francisco Giants, and while it wasn't a very successful tenure, he still had a productive 2026 season as a whole.
His defense was vastly improved, and his offensive production was still in line with his normal contact-first approach. Now a free agent, it will be interesting to see where his new deal falls.
ESPN's Kiley McDaniel is projecting that Arraez, with "plenty of demand" predicted, will get a $54 million contract this offseason that would make plenty of sense after a solid rebound season.
Luis Arraez gets $54M contract projection with 'plenty of demand' expected
"12. Luis Arraez, 2B... Projected contract/QO: three years, $54 million (18 AAV), not eligible for QO," McDaniel projects. "... Some teams might be skeptical of his defensive improvement and/or not prioritizing this extreme type of hitter, but I think there will be plenty of demand."
While modern baseball has shifted more towards players who can hit home runs, Arraez's style of play is still something that plenty of teams around baseball value.
The Milwaukee Brewers just won the World Series with a team that wasn't designed to hit a lot of homers. Their opponent, the Tampa Bay Rays, was built in a similar way.
After a mediocre stint with the Phillies, it wouldn't be a surprise if Arraez left the Phillies this offseason for a new club. If he does, there will likely be plenty of teams interested in his services.
Thanks to not having the qualifying offer eligible for him, he should draw even more interest than some of the other free agents who would cost a team draft capital if they were to sign them.
Arraez might not land top-of-the-market money, but as a 29-year-old second baseman with quality defense and elite contact ability, there will be teams interested, and a $54 million contract over three years is very much in play for the Phillies free agent.
McDaniel is projecting that, amid "plenty of interest" from teams around MLB, Arraez will land a $54 million contract with an AAV of $18 million this offseason. Whether it's with the Phillies or not is still way too early to tell.

item.content:encoded:
Mike Trout is an American professional baseball player who has won multiple Silver Slugger Awards and was unanimously named AL Rookie of the Year in 2012 as well as AL MVP honors. In 2019, Trout signed a record-breaking contract with the Los Angeles Angels; at the time, it was the largest contract in sports history. He appeared in a commercial during the 2013 Super Bowl. Trout is known to lead a private lifestyle that revolves around luxury real estate.
What is Mike Trout’s Net Worth in 2026?
Trout's net worth in 2026 is approximately $220 million. He is widely regarded as one of the best baseball players. He represented the Angels in the 2013 Major League Baseball All-Star Game. In 2014, Trout signed a six-year $144.5 million contract extension with the Los Angeles Angels.
After the completion of his six-year deal, he signed a new contract of $426.5 million with the Angels; this added 10 years to his existing deal, making it 12 years total with a signing bonus of $20 million. That makes his average annual salary approximately $ 35.5 million. In 2026, Trout will earn a base salary of $35.45 million annually.
Upon the fulfillment of the contract, he will have earned more than $500 million in salary, making it the largest contract in sports history at the time.
Between 2017 and June 2018, he made $27 million from salary and endorsements.
In a statement released by the Angels, Trout said, “This is where I wanted to be all along. I have enjoyed my time as an Angel and look forward to representing the organisation, my teammates and our fans for years to come.”
Mike Trout's Endorsements and More
Other than his baseball salary, Trout earns $10-20 million per year from endorsements.
He appeared in a Subway commercial during the 2013 Super Bowl broadcast, which was his first major endorsement deal.
In 2014, Trout became the first MLB player to get his own signature shoe from Nike since Ken Griffey Jr. He serves as a primary baseball face and icon for the brand and is seen wearing and promoting his custom footwear and gear.
In 2012, Trout signed an endorsement deal with sports drink BodyArmor; he frequently drank and promoted BodyArmor, introducing them to the Major League players. He secured a sizeable payout from his equity stake in BodyArmor when Coca-Cola bought the sports drink brand in fall 2021.
Mike Trout’s Luxury Lifestyle
The Los Angeles Angels superstar purchased a $9.15 million luxury mansion in Newport Beach, California, in 2019. Trout leads a private lifestyle that revolves around his luxury real estate, high-profile endorsements, and a grounded life with his wife, Jessica Cox, and their two sons, Beckham and Jordy.
During the MLB season, Mike Trout and his family live together in their Southern California mansion that is close to the Angels' stadium.

item.title: [NBC New York] 8 MLB players received qualifying offers. What does that mean for free agency?
item.dc:creator: Ronald Blum; The Associated Press
item.description: New York Yankees closer David Bednar, Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki and Seattle Mariners outfielder Randy Arozarena were among eight players who received $23.15 million qualifying offers from their teams Monday. Milwaukee Brewers first baseman/outfielder Jake Bauers and Baltimore Orioles left-hander Trevor Rogers also received the offers, along with Minnesota Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers, Pittsburgh Pirates second baseman Brandon Lowe and San Diego Padres left-hander Adrian Morejon. Players
item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees closer David Bednar, Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki and Seattle Mariners outfielder Randy Arozarena were among eight players who received $23.15 million qualifying offers from their teams Monday.
Milwaukee Brewers first baseman/outfielder Jake Bauers and Baltimore Orioles left-hander Trevor Rogers also received the offers, along with Minnesota Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers, Pittsburgh Pirates second baseman Brandon Lowe and San Diego Padres left-hander Adrian Morejon.
Players have until Nov. 17 to accept.
Qualifying offers began after the 2012 season, and only 18 of 157 prior offers have been accepted. The figure is determined by the average of the top 125 major league contracts this year.
A free agent can be made a qualifying offer only if he has been with the same team continuously since opening day and has never received a qualifying offer before.
If a team makes a qualifying offer to a player who signs a major league contract with another club before the next amateur draft, his former club receives draft pick compensation at the end of the first round or at the end of competitive balance round B. The placement depends on the amount of the new contract and the revenue-sharing and luxury tax status of the team losing the player.
Among those not receiving an offer was Philadelphia Phillies third baseman Alex Bohm.
Twenty-eight more players became free agents, raising the total to 183. Players could start negotiating terms with all teams at 5 p.m. ET on Monday.
Major League Baseball is expected to impose a lockout when the collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, likely creating a signing frenzy in the run-up.
Option and opt-out decisions
Baltimore declined a $7.5 million option on first baseman Ryan Mountcastle, limited to eight games this year by a broken left foot sustained when he stumbled while on the basepaths on April 8. The Orioles turned down a $3.5 million option on left-hander Dietrich Enns, which called for a $125,000 buyout.
Corbin Burnes decided not to opt out of the final four seasons of his $210 million, six-year contract with the Arizona Diamondbacks. The deal calls for $35 million annual salaries, including $11 million deferred each year. The 32-year-old right-hander returned to the major leagues on Sept. 8 after a 15-month recovery from Tommy John surgery, made three starts and went back on the injured list because of shoulder inflammation.
Toronto Blue Jays right-hander José Berríos decided not to opt out of the final two seasons of his $131 million, seven-year contract, which call for salaries of $24 million per season. The 32-year-old did not pitch this year and is recovering from Tommy John surgery on May 20.
Athletics right-hander Luis Severino exercised a $22 million player option for 2027, the last season of a $67 million, three-year contract agreed to in December 2025. The 32-year-old was 2-6 with a 4.16 ERA in 12 starts, not pitching after May 29 because of a strained right shoulder.
Baltimore reliever Ryan Helsley did not opt out of his $14 million salary next season, part of a $28 million, two-year contract. The 32-year-old right-hander was 0-4 with a 4.11 ERA and eight saves in 17 relief appearances. He didn’t pitch for the Orioles between April 28 and June 17 because of right elbow inflammation, returned for five outings and then went back on the IL with elbow discomfort. He did not pitch again this season.
Houston Astros right-hander Tatsuya Imai did not opt out of the final two seasons of a $54 million, three-year contract, which calls for salaries of $18 million in 2027 and 2028. Imai also has the right to opt out after next season. The 28-year-old was 6-4 with a 4.93 ERA in 15 starts and eight relief appearances.
Cubs right-handers Clay Holmes, Hunter Harvey and Colin Rea became free agents along with left-hander Caleb Thielbar after their 2027 options were declined, while righty Jacob Webb agreed to a $2.5 million, one-year contract.
Arizona right-hander Michael Soroka declined his $10 million mutual option for 2027, triggering a $1 million buyout. Soroka, 29, was 9-5 with a 3.41 ERA in 21 starts and one relief appearance after signing a one-year contract that guaranteed $7.5 million. He earned $1.35 million in performance bonuses. He was sidelined between June 19 and Aug. 10 by a left glute strain.
Cleveland declined right-hander Shawn Armstrong’s $8 million mutual option in favor of a $1.5 million buyout. The 36-year-old had a one-year deal guaranteeing $5.5 million and went 2-1 with a 4.58 ERA in 41 relief appearances. He was out between July 24 and Sept. 23 because of a strained left calf.
World Series champion Milwaukee declined an $8.5 million mutual option on catcher Gary Sánchez, who gets a $250,000 buyout as part of a one-year contract guaranteeing $1.75 million. The Brewers also turned down a $14 million option on right-hander Antonio Senzatela, part of a $50.5 million, five-year contract he agreed to with Colorado.
Detroit declined a $12 million option on reliever Kenley Jansen. The 39-year-old right-hander, third on the career list with 498 saves, gets a $2 million buyout as part of an $11 million, one-year contract. The Tigers exercised a $10 million option on right-hander Drew Anderson, who had a $7 million salary this year.
Toronto declined an $8 million option on outfielder Myles Straw, who gets a $1.75 million buyout that completes a $25 million, five-year contract he signed with Cleveland.
St. Louis declined a $6 million option on right-hander Ryne Stanek, who gets a $1 million buyout as part of a contract guaranteeing $3.5 million.
Tampa Bay’s Yandy Díaz’s option vested at $13 million after the Rays deemed him healthy for 2027. Díaz reached the 500 plate appearances needed for the option to become guaranteed and had to meet the second provision.
Arbitration-eligible players
Among players who would have been eligible for arbitration if their options had been declined, Milwaukee exercised catcher William Contreras, the World Series MVP, at $14.5 million; Tampa Bay exercised Gold Glove shortstop Taylor Walls at $3.1 million; and Houston exercised infielder Isaac Paredes at $13.35 million.
San Francisco declined an $800,000 option on right-hander Rowan Wick, who gets a $100,000 buyout. If tendered a 2027 contract, he would be eligible for arbitration.
Detroit agreed to a $1.3 million, one-year contract with right-hander Jacob Waguespack, who can earn $300,000 in performance bonuses based on innings; $25,000 each for 45 and 50, and $50,000 apiece for 55, 60 and 65.
Once-touted prospect on the market
Baltimore outfielder Heston Kjerstad became a minor league free agent after clearing waivers. Kjerstad was the No. 2 pick in the 2020 draft and has played 117 games across four seasons in the majors.
Baltimore outfielder Leody Taveras cleared waivers and elected free agency.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Junior Caminero Makes Rays History as American League MVP Finalist
item.dc:creator: Christian Rauh
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays Third baseman Junior Caminero has officially been named one of three finalists for the American League Most Valuable Player Award, joining Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez and Kansas City Royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. And while Caminero faces some impressive competition, his nomination has already secured him a place in franchise history. The 23-year-old is guaranteed to finish among the top three in American League MVP voting, becoming the highest-finishing p
item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays Third baseman Junior Caminero has officially been named one of three finalists for the American League Most Valuable Player Award, joining Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez and Kansas City Royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr.
And while Caminero faces some impressive competition, his nomination has already secured him a place in franchise history.
The 23-year-old is guaranteed to finish among the top three in American League MVP voting, becoming the highest-finishing player in Rays history.
Previously, Evan Longoria and Yandy Díaz shared the organization's highest finish, with both placing sixth in MVP voting.
And considering some of the talented players who have represented Tampa Bay throughout its history, Caminero's accomplishment is particularly impressive.
However, his recognition certainly isn't surprising considering what he accomplished throughout the 2026 season.
Caminero appeared in all 162 games, finishing the regular season batting .276 with 42 home runs, 101 RBIs, and 100 runs scored.
He also recorded a .360 on-base percentage and .884 OPS while earning his second consecutive All-Star selection.
Those numbers helped Tampa Bay finish with a 98-64 record, capturing the American League East title and securing the league's top postseason seed.
And while Caminero's power has consistently been one of his biggest strengths, perhaps his most impressive improvement came with his approach at the plate.
After recording a .311 on-base percentage during the 2025 season, Caminero improved that number to .360 in 2026.
He also demonstrated better plate discipline while continuing to provide Tampa Bay with significant power in the middle of its lineup.
That's particularly encouraging considering Caminero actually hit fewer home runs than the 45 he recorded in 2025.
However, his overall offensive production improved, demonstrating that he's becoming a more complete hitter.
And while his offensive contributions were certainly impressive, Caminero also showed improvement defensively at third base.
Those developments helped establish him as one of the American League's most valuable players.
Of course, winning the award won't be easy, and probably won't happen.
Alvarez finished the regular season batting .316 with 42 home runs, 106 RBIs, and a 1.033 OPS, providing Houston with one of baseball's most productive offensive players.
Meanwhile, Witt contributed offensively, defensively and on the basepaths, finishing the season with 45 stolen bases.
However, Caminero has an interesting argument considering his individual production and Tampa Bay's success throughout the regular season.
The Rays finished with the best record in the American League, and Caminero played an important role in helping the organization reach the postseason.
And while the MVP award is based on regular-season performance, his contributions eventually helped Tampa Bay reach its third World Series in franchise history.
The winner will officially be announced November 12.
However, regardless of whether Caminero takes home the award, his recognition represents another important accomplishment for the organization.
Especially considering he's only 23 years old.
And while the Rays have several important decisions to make this offseason, Caminero has already demonstrated why he's expected to remain one of the organization's most important players moving forward.
His first MVP finalist recognition is another indication of just how much he's developed and why Tampa Bay needs to ensure he stays in a Rays uniform for his entire career.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Three Teams Emerge In Red Sox's Sonny Gray Free Agency Sweepstakes
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: The offseason has really begun now and free agents can start to sign deals with clubs around the league. For the Boston Red Sox, they surely will be on the hunt. item.content:encoded:
The offseason has really begun now and free agents can start to sign deals with clubs around the league.
For the Boston Red Sox, they surely will be on the hunt. The offense needs some work, specifically in the power department. Boston also could very well end up neeing another starting pitcher, especially if Sonny Gray ends up leaving in free agency. Gray was excellent in 2026, but his mutual option was declined and now he's out there in the open market trying to find a new home.
In October, MLB.com's Mark Feinsand wrote that he expects Boston to be among the "primary" suitors for Gray. But it's not guaranteed that Gray will return, especially with heavy competition. On Tuesday, The Athletic's Jim Bowden dropped a column discussing needs for each team across the league. In the process, Bowden mentioned the Atlanta Braves, Toronto Blue Jays and the San Diego Padres as potential fits for Gray.
Atlanta Braves
"I expect them to have some interest in free agents such as Michael King, Sonny Gray, Freddy Peralta and Shota Imanaga, if they can’t trade for a top starter," Bowden said of the Braves.
If a team is going to poach Gray from the Red Sox, the Braves absolutely make the most sense. Atlanta has been connected to Gray for years at this point, even back when he was a member of the St. Louis Cardinals. The Braves are a contender in the National League and they just so happen to be the closest team in baseball to his home state of Tennessee. In October, the Braves were floated once again for Gray. Now, it's the case again. Back during the summer, the Braves were mentioned as a fit before the trade deadline. The idea of the Braves going after Gray makes too much sense.
San Diego Padres
"Will they try to bring back [Michael King] and [Adrian Morejon]? Will they go after Gray and [Freddu Peralta], too? We know how aggressive president of baseball operations A.J. Preller is, but what we don’t know yet is what he’s armed with from a financial standpoint," Bowden said of the Padres.
The Padres are the Padres. Preller has shown that he isn't afraid to make any splash. Gray is among the top hurlers in the open market. Right now, the Padres need pitching and Gray is out there for the taking.
Toronto Blue Jays
"They’re expected to be in play for some of the big free agents, including starting pitchers Skubal, Peralta, King and Gray, as well as one of the top outfield free agents in Suzuki," Bowden said of the Blue Jays.
The Blue Jays are a team that is never afraid to make a splash. Last year, the Blue Jays went out and signed Dylan Cease and Cody Ponce. Gray would be a major get this winter, and would be the worst-case scenario for Boston as the Blue Jays are in the American League East.

item.content:encoded:
ESPN reveals free agent contract projection for Mariners All-Star Randy Arozarena originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Only five players in Major League history have recorded six consecutive 20-20 seasons.
Randy Arozarena, who hit 26 home runs and had 26 stolen bases this past season with the Seattle Mariners, is one of those five.
He joined Barry Bonds, Bobby Bonds, Bobby Abreu, and Willie Mays in the exclusive group.
Arozarena is now a free agent, and the Mariners extended him the $23.15 million qualifying offer on Monday, which he will likely decline.
ESPN's Kiley McDaniel projects Arozarena's contract at four years, $90 million. Next year will be the two-time All-Star's age 32 season.
"Arozarena burst onto the national stage in the 2020 playoffs, hitting 10 homers in 20 postseason games for the Rays, fewer than 100 games into his big league career at that point.
"He has put up 20.0 WAR over six seasons since that iconic run, and his 5.5 WAR season in 2026 was a career year across the board. He well outpaced his xwOBA and career norms, but he has also had six straight seasons of at least 20 homers and 20 steals, so he has always been an offensive threat," McDaniel wrote.
The best thing for Arozarena's offensive output may be to sign with a team that plays at a more hitter-friendly ballpark than T-Mobile Park in Seattle.
Teams in need of more power and a corner outfielder, like the Toronto Blue Jays and Philadelphia Phillies, make a ton of sense as landing spots for Arozarena.
Expect to see Arozarena decline the Mariners' qualifying offer in the next few days.

Prevén que los Chicago Cubs ficharán a Sonny Gray Los Cubs adquirieron a Kevin Gausman antes de la fecha límite de cambio
item.content:encoded:
Los Chicago Cubs deberían ser uno de los equipos más activos esta temporada baja para reforzar su roster.
Chicago está en posición de ganar ahora: los Cubs figuran entre los mejores equipos de la Liga Nacional. Una de sus principales necesidades es reforzar la rotación de abridores, que les dio muchos problemas.
Chicago cayó ante los San Diego Padres en la ronda de comodines.
Prevén que los Chicago Cubs ficharán a Sonny Gray
Los Cubs adquirieron a Kevin Gausman antes de la fecha límite de cambios, pero es probable que firme con otro equipo o se retire esta temporada baja.
Por eso, Chicago debería buscar uno o dos abridores esta temporada baja. Ante la apertura del mercado de agentes libres, el analista de la MLB Darragh McDonald, de MLBTradeRumors, pronosticó que los Cubs ficharán a Sonny Gray por dos años y 55 millones de dólares.
“Gray resurgió en su primera temporada en Boston”, señaló el artículo. “Tras dos temporadas en St. Louis con una efectividad apenas superior a 4.00, el exseleccionado con el turno 18 del draft, subcampeón en la votación del premio Cy Young y elegido tres veces al Juego de Estrellas, registró una efectividad de 2.72 en 169 excelentes entradas con los BoSox. …
“Gray tiene fama de responder en los partidos importantes, y casi cualquier club de las Grandes Ligas lo consideraría un abridor viable para los playoffs, incluso una opción para el partido 1. Su edad limitará cualquier contrato a dos años. También es posible que acepte uno de un año —o de dos con una cláusula de salida—, pues desde que terminó la temporada ha hablado abiertamente de la posibilidad de retirarse para pasar más tiempo con su familia y sus hijos pequeños. Gray ha dicho que planea lanzar en 2027, pero no se ha comprometido a seguir después de ese año. La elección de Darragh: Cubs”.
Es probable que el contrato de Gray incluya una cláusula de salida tras el primer año, por lo que su paso por Chicago podría durar solo una temporada. Aun así, el lanzador elegido tres veces al Juego de Estrellas ocuparía un lugar destacado en la rotación de los Cubs.
Pese a sus 37 años, Gray sigue siendo un abridor de primer nivel y reforzaría la rotación de los Cubs. Terminó con marca de 18-5 y efectividad de 2.72 en 29 aperturas con los Red Sox, cifras que elevarán su valor en el mercado.
Chicago necesita reforzar su cuerpo de lanzadores
Los Cubs tropezaron la temporada pasada, en gran parte por las deficiencias de su cuerpo de lanzadores.
La rotación de Chicago tuvo problemas y, de cara a la temporada baja, el presidente de operaciones de béisbol de los Cubs, Jed Hoyer, dijo que deben reforzar su cuerpo de lanzadores.
“La calidad general de nuestro cuerpo de lanzadores tiene que mejorar”, dijo Hoyer. “Cuando pienso en esta temporada baja y en las próximas temporadas, ese debe ser el objetivo: llevar nuestra estructura de desarrollo de lanzadores y la calidad de nuestro pitcheo al nivel de nuestros jugadores de posición”.
Por suerte, los Cubs tienen varias opciones de abridores de impacto en el mercado de agentes libres.

item.title: [Revista Mercado] Caminero, Cristopher Sánchez y Johan Durán, finalistas de los premios MLB: cuándo se anuncian

item.content:encoded:
Caminero, Cristopher Sánchez y Johan Durán, finalistas de los premios MLB: cuándo se anuncian
La temporada 2026 de las Grandes Ligas dejó a tres peloteros dominicanos entre los protagonistas de los principales reconocimientos individuales de la Major League Baseball (MLB). Junior Caminero, Cristopher Sánchez y Jhoan Durán figuran entre los finalistas de sus respectivas categorías, una presencia que vuelve a destacar el talento dominicano en el béisbol profesional.
Foto: El dominicano Junior Caminero, de los Tampa Bay Rays, figura entre los tres finalistas al premio de Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana de la temporada 2026. También fueron seleccionados sus compatriotas Cristopher Sánchez, de los Filis de Filadelfia, para el Cy Young de la Liga Nacional, y Jhoan Durán, para el premio al Relevista del Año del mismo circuito. Los ganadores de los premios Cy Young y Relevista del Año se anunciarán el 11 de noviembre, mientras que los MVP se darán a conocer el 12 de noviembre.
Los tres fueron seleccionados por su rendimiento durante la campaña regular. Caminero compite por el premio al Jugador Más Valioso (MVP) de la Liga Americana, Sánchez aspira al Cy Young de la Liga Nacional y Durán busca quedarse con el galardón al Relevista del Año del mismo circuito.
Te puede interesar: El Banco Mundial prevé una caída del 7 % en su índice de materias primas en 2027, pero una canasta de tres insumos importados por RD subiría un 9 % ¿Dónde queda el alivio?
La MLB anunció los finalistas el lunes 2 de noviembre, en una edición que también introduce una novedad en el calendario de reconocimientos de la Asociación de Escritores de Béisbol de Estados Unidos (BBWAA), con la incorporación oficial del premio al Relevista del Año para cada liga.
Junior Caminero, en la carrera por el MVP de la Liga Americana
Con apenas 22 años, Junior Caminero logró situarse entre los tres aspirantes al premio de Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana, tras convertirse en una de las principales referencias ofensivas de los Tampa Bay Rays.
El antesalista dominicano comparte la terna con Yordan Álvarez, de los Astros de Houston, y Bobby Witt Jr., de los Reales de Kansas City. Esta nominación representa un importante reconocimiento a su desempeño y confirma el protagonismo que ha ganado entre las nuevas figuras de las Grandes Ligas.
Uno de los aspectos que marcó su campaña fue la regularidad. Caminero disputó los 162 encuentros de la temporada regular, reflejo de su disponibilidad y continuidad a lo largo del calendario. Su rendimiento contribuyó a una destacada actuación colectiva de Tampa Bay y reforzó su candidatura en una de las categorías más importantes de los premios individuales.
Cristopher Sánchez busca el Cy Young de la Liga Nacional
En el grupo de lanzadores, Cristopher Sánchez también consiguió un lugar entre los finalistas al premio Cy Young de la Liga Nacional, distinción que reconoce al pitcher más sobresaliente de cada circuito.
El zurdo de los Filis de Filadelfia competirá por el galardón con Jacob Misiorowski, de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee, y Chris Sale, de los Bravos de Atlanta.
Sánchez concluyó la campaña con 18 victorias y siete derrotas, una efectividad de 2.91 y 231 ponches en 207 entradas de labor. A estos registros se suma un WHIP de 1.20, además de haber encabezado las Grandes Ligas entre los lanzadores en WAR, con 8.1.
Entre sus actuaciones más destacadas sobresale una racha de 50 entradas y dos tercios sin permitir carreras, una muestra de la consistencia que mantuvo durante buena parte del calendario. Su aporte lo convirtió en una pieza fundamental de la rotación de Filadelfia y respalda su candidatura a uno de los reconocimientos más prestigiosos del pitcheo.
Te puede interesar: Serie Mundial 2026: ¿Cuánto dinero gana el campeón y cuánto paga MLB a los que caen en cada ronda?
Jhoan Durán, entre los candidatos a Relevista del Año
La representación dominicana en las nominaciones se completa con Jhoan Durán, cerrador de los Filis de Filadelfia, quien figura entre los aspirantes al premio Relevista del Año de la Liga Nacional.
El derecho comparte la terna con Trevor Megill, de Milwaukee, y Mason Miller, de San Diego. Su inclusión llega después de una campaña en la que asumió una responsabilidad importante en el bullpen de Filadelfia, especialmente en los momentos decisivos de cada encuentro.
Durante la temporada regular convirtió 33 de sus 35 oportunidades de salvamento, registró una efectividad de 1.82 y sumó 84 ponches en 59 entradas y un tercio. Estas estadísticas reflejan su capacidad para responder bajo presión y la confianza que depositó en él el cuerpo técnico para asegurar las victorias del equipo.
Su candidatura también coincide con un cambio en la historia de estos reconocimientos. La edición de 2026 será la primera en la que la BBWAA entregue oficialmente el premio Relevista del Año para cada liga. Aunque MLB ya distinguía a los mejores cerradores mediante los galardones Mariano Rivera y Trevor Hoffman, esta nueva categoría pasa a formar parte de los premios seleccionados por los periodistas especializados.
¿Cuándo se anuncian los ganadores de los premios MLB 2026?
Los ganadores de las distintas categorías se darán a conocer entre el 9 y el 12 de noviembre, mediante transmisiones programadas por MLB Network a las 7:00 de la noche, hora del Este de Estados Unidos. En República Dominicana, los anuncios podrán seguirse a partir de las 8:00 de la noche. El calendario de premiaciones quedó organizado de la siguiente manera:
- 9 de noviembre — Premios al Novato del Año de la Liga Americana y la Liga Nacional
- 10 de noviembre — Premios al Mánager del Año de ambos circuitos
- 11 de noviembre — Premios Cy Young y Relevista del Año de la Liga Americana y la Liga Nacional
- 12 de noviembre — Premios al Jugador Más Valioso (MVP) de ambas ligas
De acuerdo con esta programación, Cristopher Sánchez y Jhoan Durán conocerán el resultado de sus respectivas candidaturas el miércoles 11 de noviembre, mientras que Junior Caminero tendrá que esperar hasta el jueves 12.
Te puede interesar: Dominicanos en la postemporada de MLB 2026: Quiénes juegan los playoffs y en qué equipos
Cabe señalar que las votaciones se completaron antes del inicio de la postemporada. Por tanto, las actuaciones de los jugadores durante los playoffs no alteran los resultados, ya que los reconocimientos toman en consideración exclusivamente el desempeño registrado en la temporada regular.
La presencia de Caminero, Sánchez y Durán entre los finalistas representa un nuevo motivo de orgullo para el béisbol dominicano. Además de reconocer sus actuaciones individuales, estas nominaciones mantienen la atención sobre el protagonismo que siguen teniendo los peloteros del país en las Grandes Ligas.

Good morning! Catch up on the latest contract news and Mariners roster updates as the free agency period heats up. Eight players received a league-record $23.15 million qualifying offer yesterday, while the overall free-agent pool expanded to 183 players.
In Mariners news…
- The Mariners have extended a Qualifying Offer to Randy Arozarena, which is the average salary of MLB's 125 highest-paid players and valued at $23.15 million this year. Players have until a Nov. 17 deadline to decide whether to accept, and Arozarena is expected to decline the QO in search of a multiyear deal elsewhere.

item.content:encoded:
Blue Jays predicted to sign Yankees' two-time Gold Glove winner to replace George Springer originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Toronto Blue Jays have several offseason needs they must address before they can take the next step. If the Blue Jays want to get back to the World Series, they will need to make some significant moves this offseason.
Toronto struggled to stay on track amid numerous injuries in 2026. One of the biggest needs this offseason is finding a replacement for George Springer, especially with comments hinting retirement could happen this offseason.
"Very, very grateful to our fans, this team, this organization. Obviously this is not the way that we all wanted it to end. But if it is, I'm going to do my best to embrace being back home for one last time and making sure that I do anything I can to reciprocate to the fans," Springer said before his last home series.
Now, it is up to the Blue Jays to find another All-Star-caliber outfielder who can replace what Springer brought to the team in center field.
"It's been a long time since the Blue Jays developed an All-Star-caliber outfielder. You're stuck reaching for Kevin Pillar's peak seasons, then even further for Vernon Wells, who last played for the Blue Jays in 2010. Essentially, the Blue Jays need to find their next George Springer," MLB.com's Keegan Matheson wrote.
Sports Illustrated's Yirsandy Rodriguez believes two-time Gold Glove winner Trent Grisham could be a good replacement for Springer.
"Overall, Grisham finished in the 13th percentile in baserunning and the 19th in fielding, which will undoubtedly reduce his impact on the free-agent market. That said, if we focus on the role Grisham could play in Toronto, his contribution would be very different from Taylor's and Thomas', but he could be the full-time center fielder and, if he finds his best offensive version, there is no doubt that he should be a strong candidate to lead off in the lineup," Rodriguez wrote.
Grisham has been a rival of Toronto for the last few years, so joining the Blue Jays would be a different experience for him. However, the organization would likely welcome him with open arms if he is the player chosen to replace Springer.
Grisham played on a $22 million contract with the Yankees this past season. After a down year, he will likely be looking to bounce back, potentially taking over as Toronto's everyday center fielder.

item.content:encoded:
Christian Yelich has spent plenty of time delivering for the Milwaukee Brewers. On Monday, he was delivering chicken fingers.
Fresh off Milwaukee's first World Series championship, Yelich traded his baseball uniform for a Raising Cane's shirt, working a celebratory "shift" at the restaurant's Greendale location. Fans began lining up as early as 11 p.m. Sunday for a chance to see the Brewers star, who spent the morning serving meals, working the drive-thru and interacting with fans outside.
"It's kind of crazy," Yelich said when told how long fans had been waiting. "It's an honor that people are excited about the team, excited that I'm here. We appreciate everyone that comes out."
And when it comes to ordering from Raising Cane's himself, Yelich keeps things simple. His go-to is the Box Combo, although whether he includes coleslaw depends on the day.
Yelich Reflects on Whirlwind World Series Celebration
The Raising Cane's appearance was the latest stop in a busy stretch for Yelich. Between traveling from Tampa, celebrating with fans at the championship parade and making an appearance on Saturday Night Live, Yelich has barely had time to process what the Brewers accomplished.
"I think it kind of still is [settling in]," Yelich said. "We've been bouncing around a lot the last few days. ...I slept for the first time for a few hours, I think, yesterday. So, I feel a lot better going into today."
Despite the crazy schedule, Yelich has embraced the opportunities that have come with winning a championship.
"I actually wasn't that nervous for SNL, because I figured this is probably the only time I'm ever going to be here in my life," Yelich said. "So whether we nail it or bomb, it's going to be a great story."
Yelich said he focused on enjoying the moment rather than worrying about the performance. "I was just taking it all in and enjoying the experience," Yelich said. "It's a really cool opportunity to do SNL, and I got to share it with Brice and Murph."
The appearance also served as a reminder of how far Milwaukee's championship run reached beyond Wisconsin.
"I think we forget how many people watch baseball," Yelich said. " Lorne talked about it, Steven Spielberg and Tom Hanks, a lot of people talked about it and how much [they] enjoyed watching the World Series. It's just a reminder of how big the game of baseball really is."
What's Next for Yelich This Offseason?
After a championship run and several days of nonstop celebrations, Yelich is looking forward to finally having some time to enjoy the moment and recover physically.
"Just experiencing everything that comes with this," Yelich said. "Obviously rest up a little bit and get your body feeling a little bit better, which actually I feel pretty good right now. But yeah, it's going to be an awesome offseason, and it's cool that this team gets to stay together forever."
For Yelich, the championship represents more than the franchise's first World Series title. It's also a bond with the teammates who helped make it happen.
"Every year is never the same team, right?" Yelich said. "So, just really excited that that group of guys will be around together forever."
Yelich, who has been with Milwaukee since 2018, is under contract with the Brewers through the 2028 season, with a $20 million mutual option for 2029. When the 34-year-old signed his contract extension in 2020, he made it clear what he hoped to accomplish during his time in Milwaukee.
"I just really enjoy playing in the city of Milwaukee, the state of Wisconsin," Yelich said at the time. "The fan base embraced me from Day One. For me, it's just a really special place to play. Our goal here is to eventually bring a World Series to Milwaukee and to the Brewers' organization."
Six years later, Yelich accomplished exactly what he set out to do.
More MLB: The Secret Behind Pat Murphy's Push for a Third Straight NL Manager of the Year
Alyssa Polczynski (paul-zin-ski) is a sports journalist based in Scottsdale, Arizona, who currently writes for Fastball On SI and Heavy.com. She previously worked as an editorial producer for mlb.com and contributed to the Society of American Baseball Research. Polczynski earned a bachelor's degree in sports journalism and master's degree in mass communication from Arizona State University. She is also the author of the children's book Winny the Guinea's Spectacular Tea Party. A Southeast Michigan native and lifelong Detroit sports fan, Polczynski spends her free time playing golf, running, volunteering at animal shelters, and snacking on spicy dill pickle chips.
Follow alyssa_polc

item.content:encoded:
HOUSTON – Not that the gaudy numbers put up this season by Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez weren’t enough to make him the front-runner for the American League Most Valuable Player Award, but an endorsement from a former MVP certainly doesn’t hurt his case.
“No doubt, he’s hands down the best player right now in the league,” said Astros second baseman Jose Altuve, the 2017 AL MVP, earlier this year.
The numbers prove it. And now it’s up to the voting members of the Baseball Writers’ Association of America to decide if Alvarez’s monster 2026 season was enough for him to win his first MVP. Alvarez is one of three finalists for the AL MVP, along with Junior Caminero of the Rays and Bobby Witt Jr. of the Royals.
The winner will be announced from 6-7 p.m. CT Nov. 12 on MLB Network.
Alvarez won the batting title in the AL with a .316 batting average and led the league in on-base percentage (.432), slugging percentage (.601), OPS (1.033), offensive WAR (7.2), total bases (341), walks (109) and extra-base hits (77), while finishing second in RBIs (106) and tying for second in home runs (42), both of which were career highs.
“It’s crazy, everything he’s doing,” Altuve said. “He does it over and over. We know he’s going to hit a lot of homers, but when he hits them, we’re still surprised. He’s amazing. He deserves everything that happens to him.”
Alvarez is the third player since 1970 to win the AL batting title while hitting at least 40 homers, joining Aaron Judge (2025) and Miguel Cabrera (2012-13).
“That’s something that I’ve always wanted to do,” he said of the batting title. “I feel very proud to be able to do that. In fact, I even told [my teammates] that even though I hit 40 home runs, I think the batting title was something I always wanted and I feel very proud to be able to do that.”
Alvarez was named AL Player of the Month in March/April and July and led the Majors in batting average, OBP and slugging, becoming the first player to lead MLB in all three of those categories since Judge in 2025, Cabrera in 2013 and Barry Bonds in 2002. All three were named MVP in their respective leagues.
He was so feared as a hitter he drew 33 intentional walks, breaking Jeff Bagwell’s club record of 27 in 1997. The only player in AL history to have more intentional walks in a season was Judge with 33 last year.
According to Baseball Savant, he ranked in the 99th percentile in xwOBA (.443), xBA (.319) and xSLG (.640) and exit velocity (94.4 average).
When it came to big moments during games, Alvarez was front and center for the Astros. He hit a two-run homer and a grand slam in a nine-run first inning June 12 in Kansas City, driving in a franchise-record six runs in an inning.
He provided early fireworks on July 4 at Daikin Park by hitting two homers, including a two-run, walk-off homer to straightaway center in a come-from-behind win over the eventual AL champion Rays. On Aug. 2, he went 4-for-5 to complete a sweep of the first-place Rangers for Houston’s sixth consecutive win.
Alvarez is looking to join Bagwell (1994 in the National League) and Altuve as the only MVP winners in Astros history.

item.title: [MLB.com] Cease, Varland named finalists for AL Cy Young, Reliever of the Year Awards
item.dc:creator: Keegan Matheson
item.description: Dylan Cease is one of three finalists for the American League Cy Young Award, joining Cam Schlittler of the Yankees and Parker Messick of the Guardians, while Louis Varland has earned a spot among the finalists for the AL’s Reliever of the Year Award with the Rays’ Bryan Baker and the Guardians’ Cade Smith. The Cy Young Award will be announced on MLB Network on Nov. 11 at 7 p.m. ET, with the Reliever of the Year Award scheduled for the same night on the same show. Just one year into his seven-ye
item.content:encoded:
Dylan Cease is one of three finalists for the American League Cy Young Award, joining Cam Schlittler of the Yankees and Parker Messick of the Guardians, while Louis Varland has earned a spot among the finalists for the AL’s Reliever of the Year Award with the Rays’ Bryan Baker and the Guardians’ Cade Smith.
The Cy Young Award will be announced on MLB Network on Nov. 11 at 7 p.m. ET, with the Reliever of the Year Award scheduled for the same night on the same show.
Just one year into his seven-year, $210 million deal, Cease has already exceeded the Blue Jays’ early expectations with a dominant debut. The 30-year-old posted a 2.40 ERA with a whopping 239 strikeouts over 169 innings, good for a rate of 12.7 per nine innings.
Cease hit double-digit strikeouts in nine of his 29 outings this season, giving the Blue Jays a rare combination of swing-and-miss stuff with an ability to work deep into games. It’s the highest strikeouts-per-nine rate from a Blue Jays starter in franchise history and his 239 K’s rank him fourth all-time behind only Robbie Ray in 2021 (248) and Roger Clemens in ’97-98 (292, 271). All three of those seasons between Ray and Clemens ended in an AL Cy Young Award.
For much of the season, this felt like a two-horse race between Cease and Schlittler, but the Yankees’ ace likely pulled away down the stretch when he posted a 1.95 ERA over 193 2/3 innings. Cease also hit the IL late in the year with inflammation in his right shoulder, which came after some noticeable dips in velocity, but the Blue Jays didn’t sound worried about that coming out of September.
“Dylan was remarkable this year,” said GM Ross Atkins. “We were really impressed by his buy-in, his open-mindedness. That level of humility for someone at that level is very impressive. We’re very encouraged. We know he didn’t finish with the same power that he had, but we have no concerns. That was more bad timing than anything else.”
The Blue Jays have their ace now, no questions asked. Cease’s athleticism helps to project him as a pitcher who will carry his elite stuff well into his 30s, and he gives the Blue Jays a true centerpiece to build around. Entering 2027, he’s expected to have José Soriano and Trey Yesavage pitching behind him while the Blue Jays work to build out the rest of their rotation, which is expected to include Cody Ponce as he returns from right knee surgery.
Out of the bullpen, it won’t surprise anyone to see Varland’s name among the three finalists.
The joke amongst Blue Jays fans is to call Varland “The Committee,” a nod to when John Schneider said the closer’s role would be a committee approach after Jeff Hoffman was removed from the role in late April. It was immediately apparent, though, that Varland was the guy.
Varland put together one of the greatest bullpen seasons in Blue Jays history, right up there with the best we’ve seen from traditional back-end relievers like Tom Henke and Duane Ward. He posted a 1.27 ERA with 97 strikeouts over 78 innings while racking up 35 saves.
Only one closer in Blue Jays history has saved 40-plus games in a season -- Ward’s 45 in 1993 -- but Varland could have taken a run at that number if he’d been in the role all season and will have another shot in 2027.
Everything about Varland screams “closer,” such as a unique mix of personalities with his calm demeanor off the mound and around the clubhouse, but his incredible intensity when the ninth inning rolls around. His true breakout came during the Blue Jays’ 2025 run to the World Series, where Varland pitched 15 times, but the ‘26 season established him as one of the game’s truly elite closers.
It’s a stacked field in that category, with all three worthy. Cleveland’s Smith saved 41 games with a 1.95 ERA while Tampa Bay’s Baker matched those 41 saves with a 1.44 ERA. There’s no wrong answer here, but Blue Jays fans -- and Schneider -- wouldn’t trade Varland for anyone in the ninth inning.

item.content:encoded:
La temporada baja de MLB ya está en marcha. Ocho jugadores elegibles recibieron ofertas calificadas de sus respectivos equipos y tienen hasta el 17 de noviembre para aceptarlas o rechazarlas.
Los Angeles Dodgers, sin embargo, no presentaron ofertas calificadas a ninguno de sus jugadores. Así, Kiké Hernández, Alex Vesia, Blake Treinen, Evan Phillips y Brusdar Graterol quedan en la agencia libre.
Su principal agente libre pendiente, Tarik Skubal, no es elegible para recibir una oferta porque llegó a mitad de temporada en un canje procedente de los Detroit Tigers.
Aunque no pueden asegurar ahora la permanencia de Skubal para la temporada 2027 de MLB, los Dodgers planean dar pelea por el zurdo de 240 libras.
Según MLB Trade Rumors, se espera que los Dodgers compitan de tú a tú con los New York Mets cuando llegue el plazo decisivo.
New York Mets o Los Angeles Dodgers ofrecerían a Tarik Skubal un contrato de nueve años y 425 millones de dólares
Según Steve Adams, de MLB Trade Rumors, se espera que el ganador del Cy Young de la Liga Americana en 2025 rompa las marcas de contratos para lanzadores esta temporada baja. Adams prevé que Skubal firme por nueve años y 425 millones de dólares.
Se espera que Los Angeles Dodgers mantengan su estrategia habitual esta temporada baja, lo que los coloca entre los principales favoritos en la puja. Sin embargo, los Mets tuvieron la nómina más alta la temporada pasada y se prevé que hagan una contratación de impacto en la agencia libre tras un año decepcionante.
Adams señala que todos los equipos del béisbol están interesados en Skubal, pero pocos están dispuestos a desembolsar una fortuna por él.
“Todos los equipos querrán a Skubal, pero la realidad es que pocos se sentirán cómodos con un contrato superior a 300 millones de dólares, y quizá incluso a 400 millones”, escribió Adams. “Los Dodgers, su equipo actual, estarán en la pelea, pero ya cuentan con muchos brazos para la rotación. Eso no significa que no intentarán retener a Skubal, aunque la profundidad de su plantilla reduce un poco la urgencia y quizá abra la puerta a otros equipos… Los Mets tienen los recursos para competir de tú a tú con los Dodgers y necesitan refuerzos para su rotación con mucha más urgencia”.
En el artículo de Adams, él y sus coautores eligen al equipo en el que creen que terminará Skubal. Tanto Adams como Darragh McDonald apuestan por los Mets, mientras que Anthony Franco elige a los Dodgers.
El periodista especializado en MLB Jeff Passan refuerza esa idea al afirmar que los Mets y los Dodgers son los “pretendientes más evidentes”.
En 10 partidos con los Dodgers esta temporada, Skubal sumó 70 ponches, una efectividad de 2.61 y una marca de 5-2. Aunque la puja sigue abierta, parece poco probable que los Dodgers la pierdan si deciden ir con todo por Skubal.
Los Dodgers buscarían retener a Alex Vesia y Evan Phillips
Aunque buena parte de la atención se centra en la posible puja entre New York Mets y Los Angeles Dodgers por Skubal, Los Angeles también tiene a otros dos lanzadores en el mercado esta temporada baja.
Los relevistas Alex Vesia y Evan Phillips.
Se prevé que ambos reciban contratos de dos años por más de 20 millones de dólares para seguir con los Dodgers. No recibieron ofertas calificadas hoy por su costo: la oferta calificada para 2026-2027 asciende a 23.15 millones de dólares, una cifra algo elevada para estos relevistas.

item.content:encoded:
Isaac Paredes News: Option picked up by Houston
The Astros exercised Paredes' $13.35 club option for the 2027 season Monday, Chandler Rome of The Athletic reports.
Paredes appeared in a career-high 155 regular-season games in 2026 and slashed .262/.360/.447 with 25 home runs, 94 RBI, 69 runs scored and 71:88 BB:K across 659 plate appearances. Paredes entered spring training last February as the projected odd man out in the Astros' infield, but Carlos Correa ended up missing most of the season with an ankle injury that required surgery, opening up the hot corner for Paredes.

item.title: [MLB.com] Astros exercise option on Paredes, outright OF Meyers
item.dc:creator: Brian McTaggart
item.description: HOUSTON -- The Astros on Monday exercised the $13.35 million club option for next season for third baseman Isaac Paredes, who finished second on the team behind American League Most Valuable Player finalist Yordan Alvarez in bWAR last season. The option will become a mutual option if Paredes finishes in the Top 10 in AL MVP voting, which will be announced next week. Either way, Paredes is under contract for the Astros in ‘27 after he hit .262 with 25 homers, 94 RBIs and an .807 OPS in 155 games
item.content:encoded:
HOUSTON -- The Astros on Monday exercised the $13.35 million club option for next season for third baseman Isaac Paredes, who finished second on the team behind American League Most Valuable Player finalist Yordan Alvarez in bWAR last season.
The option will become a mutual option if Paredes finishes in the Top 10 in AL MVP voting, which will be announced next week. Either way, Paredes is under contract for the Astros in ‘27 after he hit .262 with 25 homers, 94 RBIs and an .807 OPS in 155 games this year.
The Astros tried to trade Paredes last offseason to clear up their infield logjam, which was resolved when Carlos Correa injured his ankle in May and missed the remainder of the season. Houston faces the same dilemma entering this offseason with Correa set to return healthy in 2027.
Last week, the Astros chose not to pick up the $5 million option of right-hander Ryan Weiss and will instead pay him a $500,000 buyout. Weiss, who pitched the previous two seasons in Korea, had a 7.62 ERA in 26 innings with Houston in ’26 and was designated for assignment in June.
Meanwhile, right-hander Tatsuya Imai, who signed a three-year, $54 million deal in January, opted into his contract for ‘27 -- worth $18 million -- last week. He pitched in 23 games (15 starts) for the Astros last season and was 6-4 with a 4.93 ERA.
Meyers opts for free agency
Jake Meyers, whose 494 games in center field for the Astros since the start of the 2021 season are more than twice as many as any other player, elected free agency Monday after the Astros outrighted him from the 40-man roster.
That was among a flurry of moves announced by new general manager Randy Flores, including right-hander Roddery Muñoz and catcher César Salazar being selected to the 40-man roster and the acquisition of right-handed pitcher Evan Reifert from the Rays in exchange for cash.
Reifort was also added to the 40-man roster, which is at 39 players.
Reifert, 27, pitched his entire 2026 season at Triple-A Durham in the Rays organization, posting a 2.48 ERA in 46 appearances, including three starts. He had 81 strikeouts in his 58 innings pitched last season, while posting a .180 opponents’ batting average.
Meyers hit .213 with three homers in 57 games for the Astros last season, missing more than a month with a right oblique strain. He spent most of the season at Triple-A Sugar Land before a knee fracture ended his season in mid-September.
Meyers has started in center field on Opening Day for the Astros in each of the last four seasons and enjoyed his best season in 2025, hitting .292 in 104 games.

item.title: [Toronto Star] Blue Jays Dylan Cease and Louis Varland crack MLB award shortlists
item.dc:creator: Gregor Chisholm
item.description: Blue Jays right-handers Dylan Cease and Louis Varland did more than their fair share of heavy lifting this year to prop up Major League Baseball's worst offence, and now they're in the mix for a pair of major pitching awards because of it. Cease was announced Monday evening as one of three finalists for the American League Cy Young Award, which is voted on by members of the Baseball Writers’ Association of America, while Varland is among the top three for the inaugural reliever of the year award
item.content:encoded:
Blue Jays right-handers Dylan Cease and Louis Varland did more than their fair share of heavy lifting this year to prop up Major League Baseball's worst offence, and now they're in the mix for a pair of major pitching awards because of it.
Cease was announced Monday evening as one of three finalists for the American League Cy Young Award, which is voted on by members of the Baseball Writers’ Association of America, while Varland is among the top three for the inaugural reliever of the year award.
Votes for MLB’s major individual awards were submitted before the playoffs. These aren’t true finalists because the winners have already been determined, to be announced Nov. 9.
New York Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler and Cleveland Guardians lefty Parker Messick are also in the running for the Cy Young. Schlittler is considered the front-runner after he posted an AL-best 1.95 ERA while ranking second in walks/hits per inning pitched (0.92) and innings (193 2/3). He also finished tied with Cease for second in strikeouts with 239.
Cleveland Guardians right-hander Cade Smith, who was born in British Columbia, and Tampa Bay Rays righty Bryan Baker are the other top relievers. Varland, whose main competition is Smith, has a strong case with a lower ERA (1.27 vs. 1.95) and more innings (78 vs. 74). Smith finished with more saves (41 vs. 35) and struck out more batters (107 vs. 97).
