item.title: [Chicago Tribune] Cubs CF Pete Crow-Armstrong is an MVP finalist — and White Sox’s Will Venable gets Manager of the Year nod
item.dc:creator: LaMond Pope
item.description: Pete Crow-Armstrong displayed his all-around talents daily for the Chicago Cubs. And on the South Side, manager Will Venable guided the White Sox through a remarkable turnaround. Both were announced as finalists for Baseball Writers’ Association of America awards on Monday. Fresh off winning a Gold Glove Award on Sunday, Crow-Armstrong was revealed as one of the finalists for National League Most Valuable Player. Shohei Ohtani of the Los Angeles Dodgers and Brice Turang of the Milwaukee Brewers
item.content:encoded:
Pete Crow-Armstrong displayed his all-around talents daily for the Chicago Cubs. And on the South Side, manager Will Venable guided the White Sox through a remarkable turnaround.
Both were announced as finalists for Baseball Writers’ Association of America awards on Monday.
Fresh off winning a Gold Glove Award on Sunday, Crow-Armstrong was revealed as one of the finalists for National League Most Valuable Player. Shohei Ohtani of the Los Angeles Dodgers and Brice Turang of the Milwaukee Brewers are also in the running.
Venable is a finalist for American League Manager of the Year — along with Kevin Cash of the Tampa Bay Rays and Chad Tracy of the Boston Red Sox — after the White Sox made a 24-game improvement and made the playoffs for the first time since 2021.
Crow-Armstrong became just the seventh player in major-league history to have a season with at least 40 home runs (45) and 40 stolen bases (41) — the first Cub to achieve the feat.
Offensively, he led the majors in fWAR (10.6), bWAR (9.8), runs (119) and extra-base hits (84) and was tied for first in home runs (45). He also topped the NL with a .943 OPS and a .570 slugging percentage. Overall, he slashed .280/.372/.570 with 31 doubles, 45 home runs, 107 RBIs and 41 stolen bases in 162 games.
Defensively, Crow-Armstrong led MLB outfielders with 26 outs above average (OAA) and a 26 fielding run value (FRV) on the way to earning his second consecutive NL Gold Glove Award.
“The thing that I keep saying is I was actually able to appreciate the year as it was going on, which was the first time I’ve been able to do that in my life just because there was a lot of good this year, and more good than bad when it comes to baseball expectations,” Crow-Armstrong said on Sunday.
The good times were plentiful for the Sox this year under Venable. The skipper was named the Sporting News AL Manager of the Year last month after the team went from a 60-102 record in 2025 to an 84-78 mark and a postseason appearance in 2026.
The Sox battled for the AL Central title all the way to the final series of the season, finishing one game behind the division-winning Cleveland Guardians.
It was the second straight season the Sox made at least a 19-game improvement, going from 41 wins in 2024 under Pedro Grifol and interim manager Grady Sizemore to 60 victories in 2025 during Venable’s first year and 84 this season.
According to Stats Perform, he is just the third major-league manager since 1901 to improve by 19-plus wins in back-to-back seasons (excluding the pandemic-shortened season and strikes), joining Hall of Famers Miller Huggins of the 1925-27 New York Yankees (69 to 91 to 110) and John McGraw of the 1902-04 New York Giants (48 to 84 to 106).
“Will’s the man,” Sox shortstop Colson Montgomery said ahead of the AL wild-card series against the Houston Astros. “From the belief, from the confidence, and everything, it’s started with him and it kind of trickled down to all of us young guys.
“I feel like once you have a guy that is so confident and so positive and ready, it’s just how can you not want to try to be exactly like that.”
The award winners will be announced next week — Manager of the Year on Nov. 10 and MVP on Nov. 12.
— Chicago Tribune’s Meghan Montemurro contributed to this report.

item.title: [CBS Sports] Pete Crow-Armstrong, Jacob Misiorowski, more named finalists for MVP, Cy Young and Rookie of the Year awards
item.dc:creator: Matt Snyder
item.description: Major League Baseball, in conjunction with the Baseball Writers Association of America (BBWAA), has announced the finalists for the 2026 major awards: Most Valuable Player, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year, Reliever of the Year and Manager of the Year. As a reminder, the voting was completed before the playoffs even started. In fact, ballots were due before the first pitch of the playoffs. That means these are regular-season awards. Further, there's no voting after finalists are announced or anythin
item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball, in conjunction with the Baseball Writers Association of America (BBWAA), has announced the finalists for the 2026 major awards: Most Valuable Player, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year, Reliever of the Year and Manager of the Year.
As a reminder, the voting was completed before the playoffs even started. In fact, ballots were due before the first pitch of the playoffs. That means these are regular-season awards. Further, there's no voting after finalists are announced or anything like that. The word "finalists" is kind of misleading, too. The ballots have already been tabulated and the league office is simply revealing the top three vote-getters for each award to create a buzz before the winners are announced.
Take note that the BBWAA has added a new award this season: Relief Pitcher of the Year for each league. MLB has been naming the Mariano Rivera American League Reliever of the Year and Trevor Hoffman National League Reliever of the Year, but this is the first time the BBWAA has added an award for a relief pitcher.
The announcement schedule is as follows.
Monday, Nov. 9: Jackie Robinson Rookie of the Year Awards
Tuesday, Nov. 10: Manager of the Year Awards
Wednesday, Nov. 11: Cy Young Awards
Wednesday, Nov. 11: Relief Pitcher of the Year Awards
Thursday, Nov. 12: Most Valuable Player Awards
Onto the finalists.
American League MVP
Yordan Alvarez, Astros: He stayed healthy for a full season and was every bit as good as we all thought he'd be. In 158 games, Alvarez had 34 doubles, 42 homers, 106 RBI, 105 runs and led the majors in all three slashes: .316/.432/.601 (190 OPS+). He also led the majors in walks and intentional walks.
Junior Caminero, Rays: At age 22, he played all 162 games, leading the Rays to the best AL record. He hit .276/.360/.524 (144 OPS+) with 42 home runs, 101 RBI and 100 runs, posting a 5.7 WAR. He's already made history, too, as the Rays had previously never had a player finish in the top five of MVP voting.
Bobby Witt Jr., Royals: This is now Witt's fourth straight season in the top seven and third straight season in the top four. He finished second in 2024. This season, he hit .281/.359/.441 (125 OPS+) with 33 doubles, 18 homers, 54 RBI, 94 runs, 45 steals and 6.7 WAR.
American League Cy Young
Dylan Cease, Blue Jays: In his first season after signing a big deal with the Jays, Cease was one of the few bright spots for the disappointing ballclub. He went 11-6 with a 2.40 ERA (184 ERA+), 1.10 WHIP and 239 strikeouts in 169 innings, finishing with 5.5 WAR. He was the All-Star Game starter.
Parker Messick, Guardians: In 32 starts, Messick was 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA, 1.06 WHIP and 193 strikeouts in 186 ⅓ innings, helping the Guardians win the AL Central for the third straight season. Fun fact: Eight pitchers in history have won the Rookie of the Year and Cy Young. Fernando Valenzuela in 1981 is the only one to win both in the same year.
Cam Schlittler, Yankees: Fresh off a great half season and playoffs in 2025, Schlittler just kept impressing. In his age-25 season, he was 14-6 with a 1.95 ERA, 0.92 WHIP and 239 strikeouts in 193 ⅔ innings, holding the Yankees rotation together despite several key injuries. He led the AL in WAR and ERA.
American League Rookie of the Year
Kevin McGonigle, Tigers: A first-round pick out of high school in 2023, McGonigle made the Tigers out of spring training and took the league by storm. He returned home to Philadelphia for the All-Star Game and finished with an AL-best 7.1 WAR. In 707 plate appearances, he hit .278/.376/.420 (126 OPS+) with 28 doubles, five triples, 18 home runs, 72 RBI, 97 runs and 12 steals, all the while playing good defense at both shortstop and third base.
Parker Messick, Guardians: The southpaw got his feet wet in 2025, but the workload was low enough that he maintained rookie status for 2026, during which he excelled. In 32 starts, Messick was 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA, 1.06 WHIP and 193 strikeouts in 186 ⅓ innings, helping the Guardians win the AL Central for the third straight season.
Payton Tolle, Red Sox: The 6-foot-6 lefty was a second-round pick in 2024 and debuted last season, though he didn't even work 20 innings and struggled. This time around, he was ready. In 26 starts, he was 9-6 with a 3.03 ERA (135 ERA+), 1.10 WHIP and 171 strikeouts in 148 2/3 innings.
American League Relief Pitcher of the Year
Bryan Baker, Rays: After dabbling in relative obscurity for parts of five seasons, Baker broke out at age 31 this year. He led the majors with 41 saves while pitching to a 1.44 ERA and 0.91 WHIP with 63 strikeouts in his 62 ⅓ innings for the best team in the AL.
Cade Smith, Guardians: Tied with Baker for the MLB lead in saves with 41, Smith was nails in his first full season as closer. He had a 1.95 ERA, 0.96 WHIP and 107 strikeouts in 74 innings for a playoff team.
Louis Varland, Blue Jays: In his fifth MLB season, Varland really found something and finished with a 1.27 ERA, 1.00 WHIP and 97 strikeouts in 78 innings. By late April, he was the Jays' closer, finishing 35 of 37 save chances.
American League Manager of the Year
Kevin Cash, Rays: The Rays missed the playoffs in 2024 and 2025 and returned to the Trop after hurricane damage left them without a home in '25. They went out and won 98 games and took one of the toughest divisions in baseball, finishing as the best team in the AL.
Chad Tracy, Red Sox: Tracy took over as manager after the Red Sox got off to a 10-17 start. He went 77-58, making the playoffs. The turnaround featured an absurd stretch during which the Red Sox won 32 of 37 games.
Will Venable, White Sox: Venable became a first-time manager for the 2025 season, taking over a team that lost a modern MLB-record 121 games the previous year. They lost 102 in 2025, but this season improved by 24 games and made the playoffs. This wasn't based much on huge free agency additions or trades for a lot of outside help. It was mostly internal improvement.
National League MVP
Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs: We'd seen flashes of the upside before, but PCA put everything together in 2026. He finished a .280/.372/.570 (156 OPS+) hitter with 31 doubles, five triples, 45 home runs, 107 RBI, 119 runs and 9.8 WAR. He led the majors in WAR, runs, home runs and led the NL in slugging percentage, OPS and OPS+. He became the seventh player ever to join the 40-40 club, too.
Shohei Ohtani, Dodgers: The four-time MVP looked like he was going to win a fifth for the first half of the season, but injuries caught up to him late. Still, at the plate, Ohtani hit .275/.377/.512 with 26 doubles, four triples, 30 home runs, 81 RBI, 89 runs, 11 steals and 3.2 WAR. On the mound, he was 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and 95 strikeouts in 85 ⅔ innings with 3.2 WAR.
Brice Turang, Brewers: Nationally underrated, Turang still hasn't made an All-Star Game, though he did start 2026 as a member of Team USA in the World Baseball Classic. In the regular season, Turang hit .268/.366/.450 (124 OPS+) with 37 doubles, three triples, 21 home runs, 100 RBI, 102 runs and 7.3 WAR, rating out as one of the best defenders in baseball.
National League Cy Young
Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers: There was upside to dream on here entering the season and it became a . In 30 starts, Miz posted a 1.80 ERA, 0.80 WHIP and 252 strikeouts in 174 ⅔ innings. He went 16-5 for the team with the best record in baseball and led the majors in ERA, WHIP and strikeouts, among other things.
Chris Sale, Braves: The spindly left-hander won his first Cy Young at age 35 in 2024. He was only able to make 27 starts this season, but he was better in a few rate stats. Overall, he was 14-9 with a 2.16 ERA, 0.98 WHIP and 200 strikeouts against only 31 walks in 162 ⅔ innings.
Cristopher Sánchez, Phillies: Early in the season, Sánchez moved to the front of the line after a scoreless streak of 50 ⅔ innings. At midseason, he started the All-Star Game in Philly. He finished the season 18-7 with a 2.91 ERA, 1.20 WHIP and 231 strikeouts in 207 innings. He led the majors in pitcher WAR at 8.1.
National League Rookie of the Year
Carson Benge, Mets: The 2024 first-rounder made the team out of spring training and hit .282/.346/.430 with 20 home runs, 22 steals and 4.3 WAR.
Sal Stewart, Reds: It's a fight of Old School vs. New School. Stewart only posted 1.8 WAR, but he had 32 home runs and 111 RBI, putting him in rarefied air for a rookie. He's one of just 15 rookies ever with at least 30 homers and 100 RBI. The last eight players to do so won Rookie of the Year. The only ones who didn't win came before there was an award or someone else did it in the same season (two rookies in 1950 got to 30-100).
JJ Wetherholt, Cardinals: Defensive metrics love Wetherholt and help push him to 4.5 WAR in 139 games. He hit .242/.339/.365 with 17 homers, 14 steals and 89 runs.
National League Relief Pitcher of the Year
Jhoan Duran, Phillies: In his first full season with the Phillies, Duran closed down 33 of his 35 save chances with a 1.82 ERA, 0.99 WHIP and 84 strikeouts in 59 ⅓ innings.
Mason Miller, Padres: In 70 innings across 66 appearances, Miller pitched to a 1.67 ERA, 0.90 WHIP and struck out 129 hitters. He won five games and converted 38 of his 41 save chances.
Trevor Megill, Brewers: Though the Brewers didn't always employ a traditional closer, Megill was the closest thing to it, securing 30 saves in 33 chances with a 2.63 ERA, 0.89 WHIP and 69 strikeouts in 61 2/3 innings.
National League Manager of the Year
Don Mattingly, Phillies: Mattingly started the season as the bench coach before taking over a 9-19 team for the fired Rob Thomson. Immediately, the Phillies got hot. They ended up going 79-55 under Mattingly, making the playoffs yet again despite starting 10 games under .500.
Pat Murphy, Brewers: Managers almost never win this award in back-to-back seasons because it's generally given to the guy whose team most exceeded expectations. How could that possibly happen two straight years? Well, Murphy now is going for three. In 2025, the Brewers set a franchise record with 97 wins and had the best record in baseball. In 2026, they set a franchise record with 103 wins and had the best record in baseball.
Walt Weiss, Braves: In 2025, the final season of Brian Snitker's career, the Braves were a disappointing 76-86. Weiss was hired in the offseason and went 94-68, getting the Braves back on top in the NL East after a two-year hiatus.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers Get Major Tarik Skubal Free Agency Timeline Update
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: As free agency begins, ESPN insiders revealed the timeline for Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal to sign. Tarik Skubal’s timeline Skubal is not only the Dodgers’ biggest free agent but also the biggest domino in the market, and as in the past, his landmark deal will likely unlock the floodgates for MLB transactions. As the offseason really kicks into gear, ESPN’s MLB reporters all chimed in for an intel report on the biggest storylines of the next month before the lockout. Top MLB insider
item.content:encoded:
As free agency begins, ESPN insiders revealed the timeline for Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal to sign.
Tarik Skubal’s timeline
Skubal is not only the Dodgers’ biggest free agent but also the biggest domino in the market, and as in the past, his landmark deal will likely unlock the floodgates for MLB transactions.
As the offseason really kicks into gear, ESPN’s MLB reporters all chimed in for an intel report on the biggest storylines of the next month before the lockout.
Top MLB insider Jeff Passan reports that Skubal is expected to sign before the December 1st lockout, giving the Dodgers and the rest of the league a month to make their best offers.
“Skubal is far and away the best player in this class, and the expectation is he will sign before the Dec. 1 lockout. The two most obvious suitors are the two teams with the highest payrolls in baseball: The Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets,” Passan wrote.
“There are bound to be others. The Chicago Cubs badly want Skubal. They also are skeptical that they will be willing to compete at the sort of dollars Skubal is expected to get — well, in excess of $300 million, potentially in the $400 million-plus range.”
How this timeline affects the Dodgers
On paper, the Dodgers have the money to match any offer for Skubal, given their revenue and their tendency to splash cash when they feel it is appropriate.
Skubal, being a high-caliber difference-maker, has the markings of a player that the Dodgers would do a lot to keep.
However, as team owner Mark Walter continues to sell off pieces of his sports portfolio, and news broke today that he is looking to sell Cadillac F1, questions about how his monetary needs will affect the Dodgers continue to grow.
If Walter needs money urgently, spending big on Skubal may be the last thing he wants to do.
Walter has publicly maintained that the team will not slow down spending-wise, and if the negative speculation is just that, speculation, then Skubal’s timeline is moot, and the team will be in the race until the bitter end.

item.content:encoded:
Dylan Cease was announced as a finalist for the American League Cy Young Award on Monday by MLB and the Baseball Writers Association of America (BBWAA).
Meanwhile, the Blue Jays also have a chance to win their first AL Reliever of the Year Award, as Louis Varland was announced as a finalist.
Cam Schlittler and Parker Messick rounded out the top-three AL Cy Young vote-getters, while Canadian Cade Smith and Rays closer Bryan Baker were the other relief finalists. The winners will be announced next week.
Cease pitched to a 2.40 ERA with 239 strikeouts and 78 walks over 169 innings in his first season with the Blue Jays.
This included two no-hit bids over the span of three games in July.
First Cease took a no-no into the ninth against the San Francisco Giants but allowed Heliot Ramos to single leading off the final inning. He pitched a complete-game one-hitter at Fenway Park 17 days later.
However, Cease threw 118 and 120 pitches in those two starts, respectively, and his fastball velocity began to decline afterwards.
His four-seam fastball averaged 97.4 m.p.h. before the July 25 complete game against the Red Sox and 95.5 m.p.h. after.
It culminated in his final outing of the season when his first pitch of the game was the slowest fastball of his career at 91.1 m.p.h. Cease's second offering registered at 90 m.p.h.
After going just 2.2 innings and walking six batters against the Texas Rangers, Cease was eventually placed on the 15-day injured list and shut down for the season due to right shoulder inflammation.
The 30-year-old right-hander signed a seven-year, $210-million contract with Toronto last off-season.
Varland, 28, was acquired from the Minnesota Twins at the 2025 trade deadline and set the MLB post-season record for relief appearances during the Blue Jays' run to the World Series.
He took over Toronto's closer role from Jeff Hoffman in late April and went on to record 35 saves along with 97 strikeouts and 23 walks over 78 innings.
Varland's 1.27 ERA was the lowest among all qualified relievers.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers' Tarik Skubal Has Clear Timeline to Sign Blockbuster Free Agent Contract
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have a ton of key free agents this winter, but none are bigger than superstar Tarik Skubal. The Skubal sweepstakes are officially underway after the five-day negotiating period ended, and the left-hander can now speak with all 30 MLB teams as he searches for his next home. This is the first time that Skubal will be a free agent in his career, and he is by far the best one on the open market. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have a ton of key free agents this winter, but none are bigger than superstar Tarik Skubal.
The Skubal sweepstakes are officially underway after the five-day negotiating period ended, and the left-hander can now speak with all 30 MLB teams as he searches for his next home.
This is the first time that Skubal will be a free agent in his career, and he is by far the best one on the open market. The 29-year-old is coming off another stellar season, and the Dodgers will look to retain him after trading for him before the deadline.
While Skubal is a highly sought-after player this offseason, he may make his decision sooner rather than later.
According to ESPN MLB insider Jeff Passan, Skubal is expected to sign before the Dec. 1 lockout.
"Skubal is far and away the best player in this class, and the expectation is he will sign before the Dec. 1 lockout," Passan wrote.
By signing before the Dec. 1 lockout, Skubal will maximize his potential earnings before potential payroll restrictions are implemented.
As for who he could sign with?
"The two most obvious suitors are the two teams with the highest payrolls in baseball: The Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets," Passan wrote. "There are bound to be others. The Chicago Cubs badly want Skubal. They also are skeptical that they will be willing to compete at the sort of dollars Skubal is expected to get — well in excess of $300 million, potentially in the $400 million-plus range. With Michael King and Nick Pivetta being free agents, the San Diego Padres need a rotation anchor, and arguably the best pitcher in baseball would more than suffice."
Dodgers Have Strong Chance to Retain Tarik Skubal This Offseason
The Dodgers are among the favorites, as they are one of only a few teams with the financial muscle to provide Skubal the contract he's seeking.
Moreover, Skubal loved his time in LA, and reportedly wants to return assuming the Dodgers offer him the contract he wants.
However, nothing is guaranteed.
The Dodgers have other issues to address on their roster, which should look different by the time the 2027 season rolls around.
Skubal was stellar in his 10 starts for the Dodgers. The California native posted a 2.61 ERA, 60 strikeouts and a 1.04 WHIP in 62 innings.
If Skubal returns, the Dodgers would retain their all-world starting rotation for years to come.

Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

MLB is announcing the finalists for its major awards Monday night, featuring the top three vote-getters for each of its major end-of-season individual honors.
The awards are voted on by the Baseball Writers' Association of America and include three finalists for each award in each league.
The awards include MVP, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year, Manager of the Year and Relief Pitcher of the Year, which will be awarded for the first time this season. The awards will be announced during the week of Nov. 9, starting with the Rookie of the Year reveals on Monday.

item.description: Toronto Blue Jays ace Dylan Cease got good news in the American League Cy Young Award race, as he has been named a finalist for the honor. Cease just finished his first season with the Blue Jays after signing a seven-year, $210 million free-agent deal with the team last offseason. He was incredible for Toronto, and his excellent season now has him as a finalist for one of baseball’s top honors. Dylan Cease Named AL Cy Young Award Finalist MLB announced the award finalists on Monday night for all
item.content:encoded:
Toronto Blue Jays ace Dylan Cease got good news in the American League Cy Young Award race, as he has been named a finalist for the honor.
Cease just finished his first season with the Blue Jays after signing a seven-year, $210 million free-agent deal with the team last offseason. He was incredible for Toronto, and his excellent season now has him as a finalist for one of baseball’s top honors.
Dylan Cease Named AL Cy Young Award Finalist
MLB announced the award finalists on Monday night for all of its major honors, and Cease was named one of three AL Cy Young Award finalists, along with Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees and Parker Messick of the Cleveland Guardians.
“Your 2026 @officialBBWAA AL Cy Young Award finalists: Dylan Cease, Blue Jays Parker Messick, Guardians Cam Schlittler, Yankees.”
Will Dylan Cease Win the AL Cy Young Award?
Although Cease had an amazing season for the Blue Jays, he is likely going to finish as the runner-up for the AL Cy Young Award to Schlittler, who appears to be the frontrunner to capture the year-end honor.
Cease was 11-6 with a 2.40 ERA in 29 games pitched for Toronto while also racking up 5.5 bWAR for the team. He pitched 169 IP with 239 strikeouts. He led the league in FIP, H9, HR9, and SO9.
However, Schlittler was 14-6 with a 1.95 ERA while racking up 7.0 bWAR in 33 starts. He pitched 193.2 IP with 239 strikeouts while leading the league in ERA, ERA+, and bWAR.
Messick, meanwhile, will likely be third in the race, as while he had a really strong year for Cleveland, Schlittler and Cease were better.
Cease was arguably the frontrunner to win the AL Cy Young Award at certain points during the season, but after getting injured late in the season and having a couple of rough starts, Schlittler leapfrogged him in the race.
Even if Cease ultimately comes in second place, it was still an incredible first season for him in Toronto, and the team should be thrilled about what an incredible performance they got from him in his first year after signing as a free agent.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees rumors: New York could solve infield uncertainty by signing star player from Japan appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Once again, the New York Yankees' quest for their 28th World Series title fell short. For the second straight year, the Yankees defeated the Boston Red Sox in the AL Wild Card series. However, the same result followed in their AL Division Series (ALDS) matchup. In 2025, the Yankees lost to another division rival, the Toronto Blue Jays, in four games. This fall, a third division rival, the Tampa Bay Rays, swept New York in the ALDS.
As the Bronx Bombers look to return to the Fall Classic for the first time since 2024, it's clear that there are areas that need to be improved. One key spot is third base, where 2025 trade deadline pickup Ryan McMahon has failed to lock down the hot corner. Because of this, the Yankees are looking to upgrade the position. While appearing on Foul Territory, MLB insider Ken Rosenthal discussed the opening. Shared via X, formerly Twitter, Rosenthal expects New York to chase star Japanese third baseman Teruaki Sato this winter.
"I expect the Yankees to be involved in the Sato market."@Ken_Rosenthal says the Japanese Triple Crown winner makes sense for New York, especially at third base. pic.twitter.com/r0XipGCGXp
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
— Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) November 2, 2026
"I expect the Yankees to be involved in the Sato market," Rosenthal remarked on Monday morning.
The Yankees have had success with Japanese stars before, most notably Hideki Matsui and former staff ace Masahiro Tanaka. However, New York has failed to attract overseas talent over the last few years, falling short in their pursuit of superstars like Shohei Ohtani and Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Will Sato prove to be different?
If so, the Yankees could very well solve their third base woes. Arguably the top free agent hitter available, Sato could be the first Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB) player to win the MVP then leave for the MLB since Matsui joined New York in the mid-2000s. After winning NPB's Triple Crown in 2026, it could be time for the 27-year-old to make his mark in the majors. Will he join the Bombers? Or will Sato ply his trade elsewhere in America?
Related: Astros interviewing Aaron Boone's trusted Yankees bench coach

item.dc:creator: Nick Ziegler; Unknown
item.description: The Philadelphia Phillies are getting set for what could be a wild month of November with a potential lockout looming. item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies are getting set for what could be a wild month of November with a potential lockout looming. This is a team that has a number of needs, and how they look to address them will be interesting.
While it was the fifth straight year in which the Phillies were able to make the postseason, the team was once again eliminated earlier than they would have liked.
Right from the start of the year, it was pretty clear that this was a flawed team. However, bouncing back from being 10 games under .500 early on in the season was impressive.
At the trade deadline, the team did try to address their issues, but it ultimately didn’t work out. Now, they will be facing a lot of the same roster problems heading into the winter, and it will be interesting to see how they address it.
David Schoenfield of ESPN recently wrote about some of the best fits for upcoming free agents. For right-handed slugger Randy Arozarena, the Phillies were wisely mentioned as a possible spot.
Arozarena Would Fill Major Need
When looking at some of the needs for Philadelphia this offseason, getting some help for their lineup is one of the top ones. Due to both Alec Bohm and Luis Arraez being free agents, the infield is going to have a different look compared to the second half of last year.
Both of those players very well could have played their final games with the Phillies, and it will be Bryce Harper returning to first base after spending the second half of the year in the outfield.
In terms of offensive production, the outfield has been a major issue. Adding a player like Arozarena would help solve a lot of those issues, and he is also a right-handed batter, which the team could use.
Last season, he slashed .281/.381/.484 with 26 home runs, 79 RBI, and 26 stolen bases. Those are some excellent numbers for the slugger, and that would be a welcome addition to this lineup.
However, while he is a good fit, he is 31 years old and will be commanding a significant contract. The Phillies’ payroll is already a very large one, and with an aging core, they would likely want to get a bit younger.
With that being said, if they are going to be trying to win a World Series, Arozarena checks a lot of boxes for the team and would be a good fit.
Nick Ziegler is an alumnus of the Connecticut School of Broadcasting. He has been working in sports media covering the NFL, NBA, MLB, and NHL for nearly a decade with various publications online. With his free time, Nick enjoys being at the Jersey Shore with his wife, daughter, and their golden retriever. You can follow him on X, formerly Twitter, @NickZiegler20.

item.description: Ex-Guardians Pitchers Emmanuel Clase, Luis Ortiz Begin Federal Fraud Trial Former Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz go to trial Monday on charges that they accepted bribes as they colluded with gamblers who made hundreds of thousands of dollars betting correctly on individual pitches. Their careers and possibly their freedom are at stake in the jury trial expected to unfold over the next month in Brooklyn federal court. Several professional baseball players, including ca
item.content:encoded:
Ex-Guardians Pitchers Emmanuel Clase, Luis Ortiz Begin Federal Fraud Trial
Former Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz go to trial Monday on charges that they accepted bribes as they colluded with gamblers who made hundreds of thousands of dollars betting correctly on individual pitches.
Their careers and possibly their freedom are at stake in the jury trial expected to unfold over the next month in Brooklyn federal court. Several professional baseball players, including catchers and baseball executives, are among witnesses expected to testify.
Clase, the Guardians’ former closer, and Ortiz, a starter, have pleaded not guilty to conspiracy charges and are on nondisciplinary leave from the club without pay while their fate is determined.
According to an indictment, the pitchers accepted several thousand dollars in payoffs to help two gamblers from their native Dominican Republic win at least $460,000 on in-game prop bets on the speed and outcome of certain pitches.
Before his trial, Emmanuel Clase spent years in the majors as one of baseball’s most dominant closers, earning three All-Star selections and two AL Reliever of the Year awards in Cleveland. (Photo by Tanner Gatlin/MLB Photos via Getty Images)
Prosecutors allege that Clase began providing the bettors with information about his pitches in 2023 and recruited Ortiz into the scheme in 2025. Lawyers for Ortiz unsuccessfully sought to have Ortiz tried separately from Clase.
Judge Kiyo A. Matsumoto said at a conference Friday that she hopes to complete jury selection quickly enough that lawyers can deliver relatively short opening statements in the afternoon.
Clase, 28, is a three-time All-Star and two-time American League Reliever of the Year who had completed his fourth season of a $20 million, five-year contract when charges against the pitchers were revealed in November 2025.
Ortiz, 27, had earned $782,600 as a starting pitcher for the Guardians during the 2025 season.
The pitchers have been charged with wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, money laundering conspiracy and conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery.
Defense lawyers are expected to argue that the pitchers did not collude with gamblers and instead were varying the placement of pitches strategically to fool batters.
On Friday, the judge ruled that prosecutors cannot show the jury proof that Clase owed $500,000 in U.S. taxes because they had only provided the evidence to defense lawyers several days earlier and long after a deadline had passed to turn over evidence to their adversaries.
A prosecutor had argued that the government wanted to put the evidence in the trial to offset any claim by Clase's lawyers that he had no incentive to collude with gamblers because he had several million dollars in financial accounts in the Dominican Republic.
Major League Baseball and the Guardians have both said they've fully cooperated with authorities. MLB has said it contacted federal law enforcement when it began investigating unusual betting activity.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: [Chicago Sun-Times] Pete Crow-Armstrong, Alex Bregman win Gold Glove Awards, backing Cubs' reputation as baseball's best defense
item.dc:creator: Vinnie Duber
item.description: The Cubs had baseball’s best defense in 2026, and it wasn’t even close. Now, they’ve got the hardware to prove it. Center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman won Gold Gloves when the annual position-by-position defensive awards were announced Sunday night. Three other Cubs – shortstop Dansby Swanson, left fielder Ian Happ and right fielder Seiya Suzuki – were previously announced as finalists at their respective positions but did not win. Still, between the winners and the
item.content:encoded:
The Cubs had baseball’s best defense in 2026, and it wasn’t even close.
Now, they’ve got the hardware to prove it.
Center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman won Gold Gloves when the annual position-by-position defensive awards were announced Sunday night.
Three other Cubs – shortstop Dansby Swanson, left fielder Ian Happ and right fielder Seiya Suzuki – were previously announced as finalists at their respective positions but did not win.
Still, between the winners and the near-winners, the team’s reputation as the sport’s finest in the field was backed up in a big way.
The statistics did that plenty prior to Sunday’s haul, with the Cubs boasting massive leads in defensive metrics like Outs Above Average (73, compared to the 44 of the second-place Diamondbacks), Defensive Runs Saved (115, compared to the 87 of the second-place Rays) and Fielding Run Value (72, compared to the 46 mark of the second-place Blue Jays).
So whether you prefer numbers or trophies, there was no question: The Cubs were baseball’s best defensive team.
The eye test, if that’s your thing, did a lot to seal that argument, too, and the Cubs spent the summer making one fantastic play after another, talking often about defense as the backbone of a team built to contend for a championship.
That championship, of course, never came, and as good as the gloves were, they did little to stave off postseason embarrassment. The Cubs stumbled in the regular season’s final week, failing to secure home-field advantage in the wild-card round, and were swept without putting up too much fight in just two games against the Padres.
That finish might dominate the memory of fans, but they watched an otherwise thrilling summer at Wrigley Field – and the defense had a lot to do with that.
Crow-Armstrong, who’s expected to win the NL MVP, made defense a cornerstone of his case for the sport’s top individual award, with his excellence in the field and at the plate compared to the two-way dominance of Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani, creating a meaty debate prior to late-season health issues that took Ohtani out of the race.
Crow-Armstrong’s defensive exploits helped him to a jaw-dropping 10.6 fWAR that dwarfed that of all other position players in the game. This Gold Glove was his second in as many seasons.
Bregman, now a two-time Gold Glover, isn’t going anywhere after the Cubs locked him up last offseason, and that’s great news for them after the 32-year-old posted perhaps the best defensive season of his career at the hot corner. His 15 Defensive Runs Saved nearly doubled his previous career high, and he set a new career high with eight Outs Above Average, as well.
Bregman became the Cubs’ first Gold Glover at third base since Ron Santo in 1968.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Matt Olson, Mauricio Dubon win Gold Gloves for Atlanta Braves
item.dc:creator: Scott Coleman
item.description: Matt Olson and Mauricio Dubon both won Gold Gloves on Sunday night, a deserved recognition for two of the most reliable defenders in the National League. It was the fourth time Olson has won a Gold Glove in his career. Olson took home the Gold Glove hardware in 2025 with Atlanta, plus won two additional times in the American League with the Oakland Athletics in 2018 and 2019. It was a no-brainer to award Olson the Gold Glove, who has established himself as the best in the game at his position th
item.content:encoded:
Matt Olson and Mauricio Dubon both won Gold Gloves on Sunday night, a deserved recognition for two of the most reliable defenders in the National League.
It was the fourth time Olson has won a Gold Glove in his career. Olson took home the Gold Glove hardware in 2025 with Atlanta, plus won two additional times in the American League with the Oakland Athletics in 2018 and 2019.
It was a no-brainer to award Olson the Gold Glove, who has established himself as the best in the game at his position the last few years. Olson led all first basemen in Outs Above Average (+12) this past season, and he was +11 Defensive Runs Saved on the corner. Olson is also a strong receiver of the baseball and does a strong job picking any errant throws from his infield peers.
As for Dubon, it's the third time he's won a Gold Glove. He took home the hardware as a utility man with the Houston Astros in 2023 and 2025.
Dubon was stellar defensively in his first season with the Braves, playing all over the diamond. He ranked in the 91st percentile in Outs Above Average and graded out well with his throwing ability as well. Dubon's ability to play any position on the field is pretty incredible to watch on a nightly basis.
The Braves had two Gold Glove nominees in addition to Olson and Dubon: starter Chris Sale and center fielder Michael Harris. The National League gold glove for pitchers went to Nolan McLean of the Mets. Harris, while certainly deserving of a Gold Glove, fell short to Pete Crow Armstrong of the Cubs.

Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman won the National League Gold Glove Award at their respective positions while three other finalists — left fielder Ian Happ, right fielder Seiya Suzuki and shortstop Dansby Swanson — fell short of the ultimate defensive honor. item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball’s best defense earned hardware Sunday night.
Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman won the National League Gold Glove Award at their respective positions while three other finalists — left fielder Ian Happ, right fielder Seiya Suzuki and shortstop Dansby Swanson — fell short of the ultimate defensive honor.
Milwaukee Brewers’ Jackson Chourio prevented Happ from winning his fifth straight Gold Glove Award in left field while the Arizona Diamondbacks’ Corbin Carroll and Geraldo Perdomo finished in front of Suzuki, a first-time finalist, and Swanson.
The recognition is just getting started for Crow-Armstrong, who was voted Player of the Year and NL Outstanding Player by his peers league-wide last week — and he is expected to be named NL MVP next week. The 24-year-old won his first Gold Glove Award last year and should be considered the favorite to receive the Platinum Glove Award, which will be voted by fans and announced Friday.
Crow-Armstrong led all MLB outfielders with 26 outs above average (OAA) and a 26 fielding run value (FRV). His elite outfield coverage led to converting a remarkable 50% of five-star catch opportunities.
Bregman overcame a tough start to the season with shaky defense the first couple of weeks. He put in the work to earn his second Gold Glove Award, the other coming in 2024 during his last season with the Houston Astros. Among NL third basemen, his 7 FRV was tied for second-best while his 15 defensive runs saved led the majors at his position as one of only two third basemen to record double-digit DRS. Bregman also recorded the most assists by an NL third baseman.
Bregman is the first Cubs third baseman to win a Gold Glove Award since Ron Santo won the last of his five awards in 1968.
Chicago White Sox infielder Chase Meidroth was a finalist for the American League second base honor, which went to Cole Young of the Seattle Mariners. Meidroth led all AL second basemen in fielding run value (10) and was third in fielding percentage (.986) and outs above average (9), appearing in 150 games at the position.
— Chicago Tribune’s LaMond Pope contributed to this report.

item.content:encoded:
米大リーグ機構（ＭＬＢ）は１日（日本時間２日）、守備のベストナインにあたる「ゴールド・グラブ賞」を発表し、日本人選手の受賞はなかった。
日本人選手でゴールド・グラブ賞を受賞したのは、２００１〜１０年に１０年連続で受賞したイチロー（マリナーズ）だけ。１６年連続で受賞者なしとなった。１０月１４日（同１５日）に発表された各ポジションの最終候補３人には、ナ・リーグ右翼手部門でカブス・鈴木誠也外野手（３２）がベンジ（メッツ）、キャロル（ダイヤモンドバックス）とともに名を連ねていたが、受賞はならなかった。日本人選手が最終候補に入るのも２０年の投手・前田健太（ツインズ）、左翼手・秋山翔吾（レッズ）以来６年ぶりだった。
誠也は、広島時代にゴールデングラブ賞を外野で５度受賞。だが、カブスにはこれまで守備力の高い外野手も多かったことから、２５年は指名打者中心の起用だった。今季は正右翼手だったタッカーがドジャースに移籍して、右翼のレギュラーとなると、打撃だけではなく守備でも再三チームを救った。失策は「２」のみで、メジャー５年間で最も少なかった。１１１試合、９７２回３分の２、右翼の守備についた。守備機会２４２の失策２で、守備率は・９９２。右翼手の中ではトップの数字だった。誠也の右翼での守備率は２２年が・９８１、２３年が・９８７、２４年が・９８１、２５年が・９５１だったが、今季は一気に上昇した。
ＭＬＢのゴールド・グラブ賞は全３０チームの監督、コーチが自チームの選手以外に投票。その投票が７５％をしめ、残りの２５％は守備指標「ＳＡＢＲ」によって選出される。
誠也は今季限りで２２年に結んだカブスとの５年８５００万ドル（約１０１億円＝契約時のレート）が終了し、ＦＡとなった。４年連続で２０本塁打以上をマークし打撃力に加えて、守備力も兼ね備えていることから、今オフの外野手では目玉クラスの注目を受けている。

item.content:encoded:
ST. LOUIS (AP) — First basemen Christian Walker of Houston and Matt Olson of Atlanta won their fourth Gold Gloves on Sunday while Boston right fielder Wilyer Abreu won the fielding honor for the third year in a row.
The Red Sox and Arizona tied for the high with three Gold Glove winners each. Red Sox center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela earned the honor for the second straight season and third baseman Caleb Durbin was a first-time winner.
Diamondbacks catcher Gabriel Moreno won his second Gold Glove, his first since 2023, while shortstop Geraldo Perdomo and right fielder Corbin Carroll were first-time winners.
Walker added to Gold Gloves he won in 2022, '23 and '24. Olson also earned the honor in 2018, '19 and '25.
Braves utility man Mauricio Dubón won his third Gold Glove after 2023 and '25.
Other second-time winners included Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman and center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong; New York Yankees left fielder Cody Bellinger; Detroit catcher Dillon Dingler; and Milwaukee second baseman Brice Turang.
Additional first-time winners included Cleveland pitcher Tanner Bibee; Milwaukee left fielder Jackson Chourio; Texas utility man Ezequiel Duran; New York Mets pitcher Nolan McLean; Tampa Bay shortstop Tanner Walls' and Seattle second baseman Cole Young.
Voting was conducted among managers and up to six coaches from each team, who can't select players on their own club. Since 2013, voting has been factored with a Society for American Baseball Research defensive index, which comprises about 25% of the total.
The utility category is based on a SABR formula and additional defensive statistics.
Walker earned a $75,000 bonus for winning the honor, Bibee $50,000 and Turang $25,000.

item.content:encoded:
With the 2026 MLB season in the rearview mirror, it’s officially hot stove and award season across Major League Baseball.
First up in the major award reveal category are the Gold Glove winners, which were announced on Sunday, November 1, on ESPN.
And yep, you guessed it, Atlanta Braves star Matt Olson has won the Rawlings Gold Glove for the fourth time in his career.
More MLB on Heavy: 6-Year New York Yankees Player Suddenly Becomes an MLB Free Agent
Matt Olson Wins 2026 Gold Glove
It’s no surprise that Matt Olson took home the 2026 Gold Glove for qualified NL first baseman.
Olson played in all 162 games this season and provided exceptional defense in just about every one of them.
He was pretty heavily favored to win the award, which is why I said it’s ‘no surprise’, but as someone who follows and keeps up with the Braves on a regular basis, this was Olson’s Gold Glove to lose.
It’s the second straight season that Olson has won the award, and the other 2 times he brought home the Gold Glove hardware were in 2018 and 2019. Olson has not missed an MLB game since 2021, which may have played a slight role in his recent achievement.
More MLB on Heavy: 6-Year New York Yankees Player Suddenly Becomes an MLB Free Agent
Taking a Quick Look at Matt Olson’s 2026 Defensive #s
ATLANTA, GEORGIA – OCTOBER 01: Matt Olson #28 of the Atlanta Braves celebrates a home run against the Philadelphia Phillies during the seventh inning in game three of the National League Wild Card Series at Truist Park on October 01, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Edward M. Pio Roda/Getty Images)
Across 1,311 chances in 2026 (475 IP), Olson made just 8 errors (.994 fielding percentage).
He also added 11 defensive runs saved.
Defense is, of course, just half of Matt Olson’s game, as he also clubbed 34 doubles and 41 home runs in 2026, while also driving in 93 runs.
Just an exceptional season for Olson, who will likely receive a handful of NL MVP votes.

item.dc:creator: This article first appeared; Was Syndicated
item.description: You can add more names to the growing free agent market. Nick Pivetta is now a free agent after two seasons with the Padres, while Luis Robert Jr., who spent 2026 between the Mets and Orioles, will go to market for the first time in his MLB career. Nick Pivetta‘s $14MM club option was not picked by the Padres, adding another high-profile pitcher to free agency. Pivetta turned into the Padres’ top starter in 2025, months after the club signed him to a two-year deal with a team and player option f
item.content:encoded:
You can add more names to the growing free agent market. Nick Pivetta is now a free agent after two seasons with the Padres, while Luis Robert Jr., who spent 2026 between the Mets and Orioles, will go to market for the first time in his MLB career.
Nick Pivetta‘s $14MM club option was not picked by the Padres, adding another high-profile pitcher to free agency.
Pivetta turned into the Padres’ top starter in 2025, months after the club signed him to a two-year deal with a team and player option for 2027 and 2028, respectively. He struck out 190 over 181.2 IP that season, thriving in San Diego despite a lot of well-hit contact.
But in 2026, Pivetta only made eight regular-season starts thanks to an elbow injury sustained in April. When healthy, Pivetta pitched very well with 42 strikeouts over 34 innings, plus a 2.86 ERA.
The Padres will keep three other pitchers. Kyle Hart‘s $2.5MM team option will be picked. Yuki Matsui and Wandy Peralta picked up their player options for 2027 (h/t SD Union-Tribune).
On the 31st, Jose Barrero, Albert Suarez, and Luis Robert Jr. of the Orioles went to free agency.
The big one was Robert Jr., whose club option for 2027 was declined. Baltimore acquired Robert Jr. before the postseason roster deadline on August 31, as he was claimed off waivers by the Mets. He hit one home run and two extra-base hits in three games with the O’s before a hamstring injury ended his season.
Additionally, pitchers Codi Heuer and Colin Selby were outrighted to Triple-A.
Emilio Pagan, Eugenio Suarez, and Pierce Johnson all hit the free agent market on October 31.
The Rangers selected Aidan Curry from Double-A Frisco. We noted in July and September that Curry, one of the top swing-and-miss pitchers in Double-A this season, was an obvious Rule 5 candidate.

item.content:encoded:
The Chicago White Sox have a narrow window to fix their pitching, but the market is shifting beneath their feet. Tarik Skubal is likely to shatter every record for a pitcher with a deal worth eight years and $355 million, according to ESPN. That number is the average of 27 projections from insiders polled by Kiley McDaniel. It is a massive sum that could drain the payroll for years to come. The 2026-27 free agent class is considered one of the weakest in a decade. They need help, but the top tier of the market is priced out of reach.
The Skubal Health Question
Skubal will be 30 in 2027 and posted a 2.72 ERA with 186 strikeouts this season. His stats are elite, yet his medical history raises red flags for a long-term commitment. He had Tommy John surgery in college and elbow surgery in 2022. He even underwent a procedure in May to remove loose bodies from his elbow. That minimally invasive surgery allowed him to pitch at a Cy Young level for the rest of the season. The White Sox cannot ignore this risk. The team paid a record price for an arm with three past surgeries.
The Peralta Pivot
Chasing Skubal might be a mistake when better value exists elsewhere. The White Sox need starting pitchers and position players more than anything else, says Yahoo Sports. While the market has more starting pitching talent than outfielders, the best position players like Randy Arozarena are still available. Pursuing Freddy Peralta makes more sense than betting the farm on Skubal. Yahoo Sports notes that going after Peralta or Michael King while also targeting top position players is a tall order. The team has six players entering free agency, including pitchers Erick Fedde and Sean Newcomb, per Sports Mockery. Newcomb threw 90.1 innings with a 3.09 ERA last season, per Sports Mockery. The Sox must find a way to fill holes without breaking the bank on one risky arm.
The collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec 1. They have to weigh the cost of a $355 million contract against the need for immediate depth. If they overspend on Skubal, they might lose out on the position players they also need.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers’ offense largely struggled during the 2026 postseason, but one bright spot was Kyle Tucker emerging as the team’s most productive hitter in October.
After underperforming for most of the year, Tucker finally looked like the player the Dodgers expected when they signed him to a record-setting contract before the 2026 season. He hit .333/.419/.519 with two doubles, one home run and two RBI across 31 plate appearances, reaching base safely in all eight of his postseason games.
Tucker’s strong performance earned him a spot on MLB’s All-Postseason Team for position players, receiving the nod in right field.
Shined when it mattered most
Here is the All-Postseason Team for position players!
#NoTimeLikeOctober https://t.co/3zDNPkYnFo
— MLB (@MLB) October 31, 2026
Unsurprisingly, several players from the World Series-champion Milwaukee Brewers also received spots on MLB’s all-postseason team for position players: William Contreras (catcher), Jake Bauers (first base), Brice Turang (second base), Cooper Pratt (shortstop) and Jackson Chourio (left field) were all included.
The rest of the roster is comprised of San Diego Padres third baseman Manny Machado, Atlanta Braves center fielder Michael Harris II and New York Yankees designated hitter Ben Rice.
Tucker’s first season with the Dodgers did not go according to plan, but he at least found some success when it mattered most and will now look to build on that momentum in 2027. His turnaround started on Sept. 4, when he crushed a home run on a 99 mph fastball at the top of the strike zone.
The four-time All-Star continued to produce down the stretch, which Dodgers manager Dave Roberts previously attributed to sorting out his swing mechanics. He finished the year batting .233/.330/.385 with 23 doubles, four triples, 17 home runs and 70 RBI in 154 regular-season games.
After the Brewers eliminated the Dodgers in the National League Championship Series, Tucker thanked fans for their support and vowed to come back stronger next season.
The 29-year-old remains an important part of the Dodgers going forward, so he will look to get off to a better start in 2027. Tucker also has something to play for on a personal level, as he could potentially reach free agency by declining a player option. However, that may only be feasible if he can bounce back and have a year that meets his standards.

item.content:encoded:
Phillies star Bryce Harper doesn't expect to play baseball in 2027 appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Philadelphia Phillies star Bryce Harper is bracing for a long offseason, as he does not sound optimistic that the looming MLB lockout will be resolved in time for the 2027 season.
The two-time NL MVP dropped the hint on TikTok, replying to a few comments on one of his posts. When one user joked that March through October seems to be the offseason for Harper, the Phillies slugger responded, "It will be this year."
Another user pointed out that Harper appears to like the offseason more than the season, and he simply answered, "This is true."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
His comments come at a tense time for the sport. The collective bargaining agreement between MLB and the players union expires at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1, and a lockout is widely expected.
At the center of the dispute is a salary cap. Owners are making their strongest push for one in decades, proposing a cap of $245.3 million along with a payroll floor of $171.2 million. The players have long opposed a cap, and MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer has made the union's stance clear.
"The fundamental nature of a salary cap is bad for players on multiple levels," Meyer said in March.
Harper has been one of the most outspoken players on the issue. In July 2025, he reportedly told commissioner Rob Manfred to "get the f*** out of our clubhouse" when Manfred brought up a salary cap during a meeting with the Phillies, according to ESPN's Jeff Passan. In May, Harper urged both sides to find common ground, saying, "We can't lose that momentum as players. We can't lose that momentum as owners."
He is not the only one expecting a lengthy fight. USA Today's Bob Nightingale reported in September that executives believe the 2027 season will not begin until around Memorial Day weekend.
For Harper, the time off comes after another early postseason exit. The Phillies were eliminated by the Atlanta Braves in the Wild Card Series, losing 6-2 in Game 3. Harper hit .269 with 29 home runs, 87 RBIs and an .865 OPS during the regular season.
The 34-year-old may be enjoying the offseason for now, but if his prediction is right, Phillies fans could be waiting a long time to see him back on the field.
Related: Phillies must consider signing these 4 players in MLB free agency

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] Should the Yankees revisit Sonny Gray after $30 million option?
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: Sonny Gray is a free agent again, and the most uncomfortable version of the question is also the useful one: should the Yankees consider bringing him back? The MLB Players Association included Gray on its October 30 free-agent list after his option decision. His Red Sox contract included a $30 million mutual option for 2027, which required both sides to agree. His availability creates an opportunity to evaluate him, not evidence that New York has made contact or intends to pursue a reunion. The
item.content:encoded:
Sonny Gray is a free agent again, and the most uncomfortable version of the question is also the useful one: should the Yankees consider bringing him back?
The MLB Players Association included Gray on its October 30 free-agent list after his option decision. His Red Sox contract included a $30 million mutual option for 2027, which required both sides to agree. His availability creates an opportunity to evaluate him, not evidence that New York has made contact or intends to pursue a reunion.
The Yankees would be buying a different pitcher
Gray posted a 2.72 ERA over 169 innings for Boston in 2026. He made 29 starts, struck out 149 and gave the Red Sox length. Those are difficult innings to dismiss just because his first Yankees stint did not go as either side hoped.
The Yankees also saw him in the Wild Card Series, when they defeated Boston in two games. One October start should not erase an entire regular season, but New York knows firsthand how quickly a matchup can change the evaluation.
I’d inquire only if the club believes it needs another starter and the commitment fits its broader spending plan. Gray will pitch the 2027 season at 37, and his velocity and durability are legitimate considerations when discussing more than a short deal.
The alternative is to spend on the bullpen and position players while trusting the starters already in place. That may be the stronger use of resources if another rotation job would come at the expense of a younger arm.
Familiarity should not dictate the decision
Gray’s history in the Bronx is worth acknowledging, not using as a shortcut for the next negotiation. His 2026 production says he can still help a contender; it does not guarantee he will match those numbers at 37.
His preferences, offers and New York’s actual interest are unknown. A phone call would be due diligence, not a promise to recreate an old pairing.

Sure, the Yankees have deep pockets, but it’s extremely unli
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees can only bring so many bold trade proposals to fruition.
But this doesn’t stop rumors from surfacing.
In a recent New York trade pitch, an MLB writer sent a $288 million shortstop to the Bronx.
Let’s take a look at his daring suggestion.
Yankees Urged To Target Royals’ Bobby Witt Jr.
When Anthony Ranaudo of FanSided first named Bobby Witt Jr. as a potential target for New York, I imagine a few eyebrows were raised.
Sure, the Yankees have deep pockets, but it’s extremely unlikely they’d empty them on Witt right now.
But Ranaudo brings up an interesting string of hypothetical events:
“The package would have to start with Lombard, and it would probably sting, badly. Volpe might be included as an upside play, and Kansas City would almost certainly demand Kilby, the system’s top prospect.
“Add a big-league-ready arm like Elmer Rodríguez or Carlos Lagrange, or maybe Will Warren or Clarke Schmidt, then sprinkle in a couple of high-ceiling lottery tickets from the lower levels, like Yostin Peña or Wilberson De Peña. Think of that last part as a venture capital play, where the Royals bet that one of them turns into their next billion-dollar company.”
The boldest statement?
“So… George Lombard Jr, Anthony Volpe, Will Warren, and Yostin Pena for Bobby Witt Jr.? The Yanks would get at least four years of Bobby’s prime with Aaron Judge? Sign me up!”
PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – JULY 14: Bobby Witt Jr. #7 of the Kansas City Royals runs to first base during the third inning of the 2026 MLB All-Star Game at Citizens Bank Park on July 14, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images)
Any Yankee fan — or any baseball fan, in general — would love to see Witt with their ballclub.
Realistically, this deal isn’t really, well, much of a possibility. However, baseball is a game of surprise, and I’m not one to rule anything out.
Let’s entertain the idea for a minute.
What Could Witt Offer the Yankees?
TAMPA, FLORIDA – MAY 01: Bobby Witt Jr. #7 of the Kansas City Royals reacts after hitting a two-run home run in the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays at George M. Steinbrenner Field on May 01, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images)
The two-time Gold Glove recipient (2024, 2025) brings elite defensive prowess to the diamond.
Equally as impressive is his explosive bat.
During his 2026 campaign, he slashed .281/.359/.441 with a clean .800 OPS and 18 homers through 143 games.
He logged 33 doubles, one triple and 54 RBIs.
Not to mention, he’s a three-time MLB All-Star (2024, 2025 and 2026).
KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI – AUGUST 06: Bobby Witt Jr. #7 of the Kansas City Royals is congratulated by teammates in the dugout after scoring during the 3rd inning of the game against the Minnesota Twins at Kauffman Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images)
Witt — hot bat and all — would undoubtedly provide an immediate boost to the Yankees’ lineup.
This is merely a top-of-the-wishlist player for loyal New York fans, but who said dreams can’t come true?

Robert was once one of baseball's top rising stars, ranking third on MLB.com's 2020 prospect list while he was in the Chicago White Sox organization. Chicago initially signed the Cuban outfielder in 2017 in a deal that included a $26 million signing bonus. Before he even reached the majors, Ro
item.content:encoded:
The Baltimore Orioles have declined their $20 million team option on outfielder Luis Robert Jr., opting to instead pay him a $2 million buyout and make him a free agent, according to ESPN's Alden Gonzalez.
Robert was once one of baseball's top rising stars, ranking third on MLB.com's 2020 prospect list while he was in the Chicago White Sox organization. Chicago initially signed the Cuban outfielder in 2017 in a deal that included a $26 million signing bonus.
Before he even reached the majors, Robert signed a six-year, $50 million contract in Jan. 2020 with a pair of team options for 2026 and 2027.
He finished second in the American League 2020 Rookie of the Year race and earned Gold Glove honors as well.
Injuries held him back in 2021 and 2022, when he played just 166 of a total 324 games. Those ailments included a complete tear of his right hip flexor in 2021 and a sprained left wrist in 2022.
Robert enjoyed his best season in 2023, when he hit 38 home runs (80 RBI) and posted an .857 OPS in 145 games. He earned All-Star and Silver Slugger honors.
However, Robert encountered more injury issues in 2024 (Grade 2 flexor strain in his right hip) and 2025 (Grade 2 hamstring strain, groin tightness). He ultimately missed 114 games over those seasons. During that stretch, Robert hit .223 (.660 OPS) with 28 homers and 88 RBI in 210 games.
Chicago traded Robert to the Mets last January for Luisangel Acuña and minor leaguer Truman Pauley, and he began the year as the team's starting center fielder.
Robert then dealt with more injuries, this time a lumbar disc herniation. He played just 58 games for the Mets, hitting .223 (.702 OPS) with 10 homers and 23 RBI. New York placed Robert on outright waivers on Aug. 29.
Two days later, the Orioles claimed the 29-year-old Robert for the rest of the season. Robert landed on the injured list again, this time with left hamstring discomfort. He played just three games, going 2-for-11 with a homer and three RBI.
In total, Robert slashed .221/.300/.407 with 11 home runs and 26 RBI in 2026.

item.title: [Boston Sports Journal] MLB Notebook: Sonny Gray enters free agency, Red Sox scramble to clear roster space
item.dc:creator: Chris Henrique

item.content:encoded:
Sonny Gray is officially a free agent after his $30 million mutual option for 2027 has been declined. The veteran will get a $10 million buyout and will see if he can land a multi-year deal on the free agent market.
Gray, 36, was widely expected to decline his option, as the veteran right-hander figures to command a more lucrative deal on the free-agent market this winter.
Gray emerged as the Red Sox’ most dependable starter this season, serving as their de facto ace after Garrett Crochet suffered an injury that sidelined him for the entire summer. The veteran should also be considered for the American League Cy Young Award after leading the league with 18 wins. Philadelphia's Cristopher Sánchez was the only other pitcher in the majors to reach that mark.
The righty was outstanding in his first season with Boston, posting a 2.72 ERA and 1.15 WHIP while holding opposing hitters to a .236 batting average across 29 starts. The veteran right-hander struck out 149 batters and walked just 46 over 169 innings despite missing several starts early in the season with a hamstring injury.
He now joins former teammates left-hander Patrick Sandoval and infielder Isiah Kiner-Falefa on the free agent market. Both Sandoval and Kiner-Falefa elected free agency on Thursday.
There had been speculation that Gray would retire following the season, but he reached out to The Boston Globe on Oct. 9, indicating his intention of pitching beyond this past season.
“My family and I have talked about it and it’s an easy decision. I still want to win a World Series, whether that is Boston or with whoever wants me,” Gray wrote in a text.
Gray's willingness to return to the Red Sox is particularly noteworthy given his comments to the Globe. Following Boston's Wild Card Series loss to the Yankees, the veteran right-hander was noncommittal about returning to the organization, especially after how his outing was handled in Game 2 of the series.
Red Sox manager Chad Tracy pulled Gray after just 4 2/3 innings in Game 2 where he allowed just one run to the Yankees. Gray publicly acknowledged his frustration with the decision, but Gray, Tracy, and Craig Breslow following the loss and cleared the air. Gray mentioned that he never had a bad relationship with Tracy said it was “in a fine place.”
Boston acquired Gray from the Cardinals last offseason for right-hander Richard Fitts, left-handed pitching prospect Brandon Clarke, and a player to be named later or cash.
If Gray was to leave the Red Sox in free agency, the rotation is still in a good spot with Crochet, the emergence of Payton Tolle, Ranger Suarez, Brayan Bello, Tanner Houck, Johan Oviedo, and Jake Bennett.
Even with that depth, the Sox were tested all season, having to use Eduardo Rivera, Raymond Burgos, and Jedixson Paez in spot starts with Alec Gamboa and Jovani Moran as openers.
The Sox should look to add another starter to the rotation next season, even if it’s someone who could pitch at the back end of the rotation. High-profile arms on the market include Michael King, whom the Sox had interest in signing last offseason, Tarik Skubal, Robbie Ray, and Nick Martinez, to name a few. Breslow had interest in Shane Bieber a few offseasons ago, but he opted to remain with the Guardians at the time. The Sox could look to bring the veteran in after pitching for the Blue Jays last season.
As noted in a previous column, Martinez is another intriguing option to replace Gray following a successful stint with the Rays. His mutual option was declined, making him a free agent. The veteran right-hander figures to draw plenty of interest and could return to Tampa Bay, particularly if the Rays lose Freddy Peralta in free agency.
Another possibility, albeit an unlikely one, is a reunion with Lucas Giolito. If the Red Sox are looking to take a one-year flyer on a veteran starter, Giolito is expected to return to the open market after struggling with the Padres last season, posting a 5.16 ERA and 1.85 WHIP across seven appearances.
Roster Crunch
As Gray enters free agency, the Red Sox have additional housekeeping to do before Monday's deadline to get their 40-man roster in order.
Boston has already made two trades to create roster flexibility, sending outfielder Nate Eaton to the Athletics and infielder Tsung-Che Cheng to the Tigers, with the latter deal bringing back cash considerations.
The moves free up two spots on the Red Sox’ 40-man roster, but Boston still needs to clear two more by Monday to accommodate seven players returning from the 60-day injured list, including Kutter Crawford, Zack Kelly, Johan Oviedo, Eduardo Rivera, Justin Slaten, Triston Casas and Eli White.
The Red Sox acquired Cheng from the Nationals last February. The 25-year-old spent just 32 games on Boston's active roster this past season, appearing in 14 games while the team went 13-1. Cheng made 13 starts at shortstop during June and July while Trevor Story was on the injured list, batting .256 (10-for-39) with one double, five RBI, seven runs scored and 14 strikeouts.
Although his offensive contributions were limited, Cheng made his presence felt defensively during Boston's 15-game winning streak. With the Red Sox clinging to a 6-5 lead and two runners in scoring position on July 20, Cheng made a leaping catch on a 93.8 mph line drive for the final out, securing Boston's 14th consecutive victory.
He followed that performance with another highlight-reel play, fielding a 109.9 mph ground ball for the final out of the Red Sox’ 15th straight win.
Cheng also made history at Triple-A Worcester, becoming the first player in WooSox history to hit for the cycle. He was the first player at Boston's Triple-A affiliate to accomplish the feat since Henry Ramos did so for Pawtucket on July 4, 2016, against Charlotte.
With additional roster spots needed, Breslow faces several decisions involving players on the bubble.
One name worth monitoring is Crawford, who has missed the past two seasons because of injuries. Boston could also consider non-tendering Jahmai Jones before attempting to bring him back on a minor league contract.
Casas presents a more complicated decision for the Red Sox. The first baseman has missed significant time over the past two seasons and has been sidelined since suffering a patellar injury to his knee.
There is still a possibility Casas could develop into

item.title: [Reviewing the Brew] Jacob Misiorowski’s stellar Game 5 World Series start continued Brewers' ace’s impressive trend
item.dc:creator: Brandon Glick
item.description: So much of the angst Milwaukee Brewers fans had about the Freddy Peralta trade last offseason was that it, ostensibly, left the team without an ace. Unlike the Corbin Burnes trade from a few years prior -- when Peralta himself was ready to step into those top-of-the-rotation shoes -- no one knew if Brandon Woodruff would be healthy enough or if Jacob Misiorowski was ready to take on that pressure. item.content:encoded:
So much of the angst Milwaukee Brewers fans had about the Freddy Peralta trade last offseason was that it, ostensibly, left the team without an ace. Unlike the Corbin Burnes trade from a few years prior -- when Peralta himself was ready to step into those top-of-the-rotation shoes -- no one knew if Brandon Woodruff would be healthy enough or if Jacob Misiorowski was ready to take on that pressure.
Of course, Miz was entrusted with the Opening Day nod, a sign of confidence from the organization that he would be able to go toe-to-toe with the best of the best in just his second season in the big leagues.
That confidence was thoroughly rewarded in 2026. Not only was Misiorowski named an All-Star for the second straight year, but he's a shoo-in to win the NL Cy Young award (the first Brewers pitcher to do so since Burnes in 2021). That earned him Game 1 starts in each postseason series, plus the fateful Game 5 assignment that proved, without a shred of doubt, the kid has always been ready to live up to the moment.
Jacob Misiorowski is already one of baseball's most reliable big-game pitchers
Whether it's the 2025 playoffs, during which he faced two of the best offenses in the league -- the Cubs and Dodgers -- Misiorowski, who wasn't even a guarantee to make the postseason roster, shows up. He recorded a 1.50 ERA in those three outings, leading the Brewers to two of their three wins over the Cubs, including the all-important Game 5 in the NLDS.
Whether it's Opening Day, when he was asked to open the Crew's season on a high note as a 23-year-old, Misiorowski shows up. He struck out 11 White Sox batters over five impossibly dominant innings, setting the franchise record for the most Opening Day punchouts in the process.
Whether it's Game 1 of the NLDS, NLCS, or World Series, Misiorowski shows up. He allowed just four runs over 13⅓ innings combined, shutting down a red-hot Padres squad, the two-time reigning champion Dodgers, and the pennant-winning Rays. The Brewers won each of those three games.
Even when it's Game 5 of the Fall Classic, with the Brewers nine innings away from the first title in franchise history, Misiorowski shows up. He willingly pitched to a little more contact than usual, mowing down Tampa Bay's lineup over 5⅔ scoreless frames. Only a leg cramp could get him out of the game, at which point the Crew were able to turn to their high-leverage relievers and finish off their postseason run with a victory.
No matter what the moment or who the opponent, Misiorowski shows up. He's already one of baseball's premier big-game starters, a certified ace capable of going toe-to-toe with anyone.

Spencer Jones is coming off his rookie season at the MLB level.
The New York Yankees outfielder showed a lot of promise that has many fans excited about his potential.
Jones Announced Personal News
On Saturday, Jones announced heartfelt personal news to Instagram.
He wrote: “Forever starts today. I feel like the luckiest man on Earth to propose to the most beautiful, intelligent, and sweetest woman I’ve ever met. You’ve elevated my life in so many ways & I can’t wait to take your hand in marriage. You are the brightest light in a city of endless opportunities. I truly believe the world is ours when I am with you. There is nothing we cannot do when we are together. You are so easy to love. The Joneses coming soon!”

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Tarik Skubal Predicted To Join NL Central Club Over Other Contenders
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers acquired Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline, and after failing to win the World Series after their all-in move, they must now decide if they want to retain him as a free agent. Skubal is a two-time American League Cy Young Award winner and was great again this year for the Detroit Tigers and the Dodgers. Any team would love to have him, but his price tag will limit which teams actually have a chance to get him. The real contenders are all big-market teams, and SNY's John
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers acquired Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline, and after failing to win the World Series after their all-in move, they must now decide if they want to retain him as a free agent.
Skubal is a two-time American League Cy Young Award winner and was great again this year for the Detroit Tigers and the Dodgers. Any team would love to have him, but his price tag will limit which teams actually have a chance to get him. The real contenders are all big-market teams, and SNY's John Harper predicted he would sign with the Chicago Cubs.
The Cubs would seem like one of the least likely big markets to land Skubal, especially if the Dodgers, New York Mets and New York Yankees make an effort. However, they are desperate for an ace and have a ton of money coming off the books.
"After a quick exit in the postseason, the Cubs have more than $100 million coming off their payroll, a glaring need for an ace, and the added incentive of knowing their neighbors to the north, the rival Brewers, just won the World Series," wrote Harper. "All of which I believe will add up to them outbidding the Mets, the Dodgers, and anybody else who pursues Skubal, even if it means going to eight years at $45 million or so per season."
Skubal would not fix the Cubs' rotation single-handedly, but he would go a long way in doing so. He is a true ace, and the Cubs would have a great chance to win the 30-plus games he starts a season. However, they would still need to fill the spots behind him. Edward Cabrera struggled and dealt with injuries last year and Cade Horton could be out for the year.
Justin Steele coming back could help, but they will still need to add more starters even if they land Skubal.
More MLB: Brewers' Championship Caps Unique 2026 MLB Postseason

item.title: [Bleacher Report] Ketel Marte Trade Must Be Made By D-Backs Amid Latest MLB Rumors Ahead of 2027 Season
item.dc:creator: Zach Bachar
item.description: As the Arizona Diamondbacks enter the offseason, the future of star second baseman Ketel Marte remains murky. Marte has spent the past 10 years of his career in Arizona, but a trade could benefit both sides.
