item.content:encoded:
As the Arizona Diamondbacks enter the offseason, the future of star second baseman Ketel Marte remains murky.
Marte has spent the past 10 years of his career in Arizona, but a trade could benefit both sides.
According to Nick Piecoro of the Arizona Republic, multiple teams have expressed interest in acquiring the three-time All-Star on the trade market.
Diamondbacks general manager Mike Hazen was also noncommittal when asked about Marte's availability in trade discussions.
"I think we need to look at some ways to shake the team up a little bit," Hazen said when asked if he would listen to offers on Marte, per Piecoro. "I think we've had this team together for a long time. We've had some success, but we're going to find ways to make some changes in some cases. I don't know where that's going to take us."
Marte previously signed a six-year extension worth $116.5 million with Arizona in April 2025, as he's still still under contract through 2030 and owns a player option for his 2031 campaign.
It's worth noting that Marte can choose to stay with the Diamondbacks regardless of his potential involvement in trade talks, as he holds a full no-trade clause.
Still, he may be willing to waive his no-trade clause and move on from Arizona after a recent tumultuous stretch as a member of the club.
In 2025, Marte's home in Scottsdale was burglarized during the All-Star break. He eventually went to the Dominican Republic following the All-Star festivities, missing the Diamondbacks' first three games after the break as a result.
During the ensuing offseason, the Diamondbacks held trade talks involving Marte as the Boston Red Sox, Toronto Blue Jays, Seattle Mariners, Detroit Tigers, Pittsburgh Pirates and Tampa Bay Rays were all linked to the second baseman.
While he ultimately remained in Arizona, his 2026 campaign was also eventful.
On Aug. 17, the Diamondbacks placed Marte on the restricted list after he didn't show up for a game against the Boston Red Sox. It turned out that he had returned to Arizona to have an MRI on his knee and was placed on the injured list instead.
Marte later revealed that he made an individual decision to skip the matchup with Boston after waking up in significant pain and planned to apologize to his teammates once again.
He ended the 2026 season by hitting .249 with 22 home runs, 31 doubles and 76 RBI while appearing in 141 games. It represented a step back for Marte compared to past years, as his .748 OPS was his lowest mark since 2022.
Although it could be risky for the Diamondbacks to potentially sell low on the 33-year-old following the 2026 season, it isn't hard to imagine his trade value dropping drastically if his production continues to decline in 2027.
On the other hand, opposing front offices may believe that Marte will be able to bounce back following a possible trade. After all, he racked up 89 home runs while slashing .283/.368/.519 from 2023-25.
Arizona has missed the playoffs in each of the three years since its 2023 World Series appearance and could look to make significant roster changes in order to acquiring younger players that fit the timeline of star outfielder Corbin Caroll, who's just 26 years old.
While Marte's overall tenure on the Diamondbacks has been successful, it's time for a change of scenery.

item.title: [Just Baseball] Can the Dodgers Afford to Sign Skubal Before the Lockout? | Just Baseball
item.dc:creator: Ryan Murphy

item.content:encoded:
On August 1, 2026, the Los Angeles Dodgers faced off against the Boston Red Sox. Having lost the first game of their weekend series the day prior, the Dodgers looked to put themselves back into the win column that Saturday evening.
The Red Sox jumped out to an early lead thanks to a first-inning home run from Ceddanne Rafaela, but the Dodgers answered in the second inning with two runs of their own. Then, the Red Sox tied the game in the top of the third inning when Rafaela hit his second home run of the game.
Despite recording ten hits over the course of the game, the Dodgers went on to lose with a score of 3-2. They dropped the next game as well, culminating in a series sweep for the Red Sox and setting the Dodgers’ season record at 69-43.
However, as frustrated as Dodgers fans may have been watching their team fall short that Saturday night, few were vocal about it. This is because halfway through the game, MLB insider Jeff Passan fired off a shot heard round the world.
After months of speculation, it had actually happened. No matter the wealth of talent the Dodgers had already accumulated, they had finally collected the last Infinity Stone needed to complete their gauntlet: Tarik Skubal was a Dodger. Yet, it mattered not.
A relentless Milwaukee Brewers squad, fueled by an insatiable hunger to hoist their franchise’s first-ever World Series banner, swept the Dodgers in the NLCS. They have since gone up 3-1 over the Tampa Bay Rays, who are fighting to bring the same vision to reality for their city.
Now, the Dodgers have a decision to make. Skubal is projected to sign a massive deal in the offseason, and the Dodgers’ payroll is already bursting at the seams.
With a long winter ahead, potentially made longer by ongoing CBA negotiations resulting in an extended lockout, what will factor into the Dodgers’ pursuit of Skubal’s service long-term?
Down the Stretch
For starters, it is worth taking a look at how Skubal performed for the Dodgers following the trade.
In 10 starts for the Boys in Blue, Skubal posted a 2.61 ERA over 62 innings. He notched 70 strikeouts while allowing 13 walks and four home runs.
Skubal recorded his signature performance of this stretch on his final start of the year against the San Francisco Giants, striking out 10 batters over seven scoreless frames. Notably, he allowed just three hits and did not walk a batter, facing just 23 batters throughout the outing.
Dodgers fans would understandably love to see him back in Los Angeles in 2027 and beyond. The southpaw has been considered one of, if not the best pitchers in baseball over the past few years, with back-to-back AL Cy Young wins in 2024 and 2025 to back it up.
Another factor in wanting Skubal to return is the package of prospects the Dodgers sent to the Detroit Tigers in the trade. Both outfielder Zyhir Hope and starting pitcher River Ryan have enormous potential.
In particular, Hope has seen a meteoric rise through top prospect lists in recent years. He put up a .287/.367/.513 line with 29 homers and 26 stolen bags across 124 games in Double-A last year. Ryan has spent much of the past few years recovering from Tommy John surgery, but he should be a significant part of the Tigers’ pitching staff in the coming seasons.
Now that the season has come to a close, this prospect package is somewhat of a sunk cost for the Dodgers. The intent was to give themselves the best chance at a three-peat, and Skubal did just that. It just didn’t pan out as they had hoped.
Such is the high-risk, high-reward nature of trade deadline splashes. For Dodgers general manager Andrew Friedman, he now has the tall task of seeing whether they can get a bit more return on their investment in the offseason.
Sticker Shock
In The Athletic, Jim Bowden predicted that Skubal’s contract will fall somewhere between $350 million to $500 million. His agent, Scott Boras, is highly recognized for his clients’ high-profile contracts. Given Skubal’s profile, he seems primed to shoot for the moon this offseason.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto sports the largest guaranteed contract for a pitcher in MLB history at $325 million. As for average annual value (AAV), Zack Wheeler’s 3-year, $126 million deal in 2025 sits at $42 million per year. Bowden expects Skubal to break both of these records.
The Dodgers have immense financial resources. However, a Skubal signing might test the limits of just how much they can leverage those resources.
In 2027, the Dodgers already owe seven individual players over $25 million in luxury tax salary. Their projected luxury tax payroll stands at a whopping $384,757,413 – the highest in MLB.
By this estimate, the Dodgers would land nearly $78 million over the top luxury tax threshold ($307 million). This assumes that they make no changes to their roster, but still. As a result, the Dodgers’ tax bill is projected to land at $126,933,154. The bill is massive in its own right, but a Skubal contract would nearly double it.
Based on how long the Dodgers have remained over the luxury tax, and by how much, they would owe 110% of Skubal’s luxury tax salary in additional tax. Say Skubal were to sign a 9-year, $405 million contract. At an AAV of $45 million, that would push the Dodgers’ tax hit for this hypothetical deal to $94.5 million. For one year!
That means that, in this same scenario, their total tax hit would jump all the way to $221.4 million. For reference, that would be a larger commitment than current payroll allocations for 22 out of 30 MLB teams in 2027.
The Dodgers’ payroll allocations already sit over $370.5 million for next year. That means that the Dodgers would owe nearly $592 million to just payroll and luxury tax payments. Needless to say, either the Dodgers would tighten their margins, or something would have to change.
Not Quite Tetris
In order for the Dodgers to keep Skubal on the roster comfortably, they’ll likely have to move some players.
Looking at their current contracts, the Dodgers will clear over $77.1 million in luxury tax salary in 2029. The year after that, they are set to move on from another $82.4 million. This can provide the room they’re looking for in a long-term deal for Skubal, but only after a few years.
The Dodgers could trade players set to become free agents in 2029 or 2030 as a remedy. This would allow them to tap into some of their upcoming payroll flexibility early. It would also allow the Dodgers to further reinforce their organization with more young talent in return.
One such example would be Tyler Glasnow, owed $27.3 million next year. He would fetch a strong return, and is the highest-paid player aside from Kyle Tucker, who will become a free agent by 2030.
The hometown kid has pitched well for the Dodgers, albeit for a limited amount of innings. The Dodgers may be reluctant to move a frontline arm like Glasnow, as they tend to value starting pitching depth.
However, Teoscar Hernández is a player the Dodgers could move off of. He’s owed nearly $20 million next year, and would likely still attract interest around the league. Plus, it would give the Dodgers some needed flexibility in their outfield – room for top prospect Josue De Paula to get regular reps.
These two are the most likely candidates. Meanwhile, Tanner Scott, Edwin Díaz, or the aforementioned Tucker could wind up on the block if the Dodgers feel they need to get creative.
So, Can the Dodgers Bring Him Back?
As of now, the Dodgers are unlikely to retain Skubal.
We still don’t know what could happen with the upcoming CBA negotiations. If a salary cap is agreed upon without an adjustment period of some kind, signing Skubal could force them to cut payroll at a position of incredibly low leverage.
The Dodgers likely want to avoid being put into this position. Hence, they would want to sign Skubal after a new CBA is ratified. However, Skubal has the opposite incentive.
If Skubal waits until after a new CBA is ratified, that decision could significantly impact his potential earnings. After all, MLB’s salary cap proposal has been the focal point of negotiations for over a year. As such, he is likely to want to sign prior to the beginning of the impending lockout.
If the Dodgers want to keep Skubal, they will have to be bold, and they will have to act quickly. Dodgers starter Blake Snell had already begun his recruiting pitch directly following their NLCS exit.
“I just said, he can’t leave me, especially on these terms. The goal is to win a World Series, and we weren’t able to do that… I would love nothing more than for him to be back,” Snell told Jack Harris at The California Post.
It would not be a surprise to see Skubal sign elsewhere. Still, it also should not surprise folks if he returns to Los Angeles. So long as Skubal has not signed with another team, the Dodgers will remain in play. Skubal has spoken fondly of his time with the Dodgers organization, and could easily be motivated to come back.
The onus will be on the Dodgers’ front office to find a way to make it happen – if they can.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Kyle Tucker Earns Major MLB Honor After Dodgers Postseason Redemption
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers right fielder Kyle Tucker earned a notable award after a disastrous regular season for his sensational October. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers right fielder Kyle Tucker earned a notable award after a disastrous regular season for his sensational October.
Kyle Tucker’s redemption arc
Tucker flopped in the regular season, given his $60 million contract and what was expected of him in a supposed Dodgers super-lineup.
His season was his worst since his rookie year, with a .233/.330/.385 line, 17 home runs, and a league-average 100 wRC+.
He was valued at just 0.9 fWAR. Tucker had little hard contact, more strikeouts than usual, and fewer walks than normal.
It was bizarre for a player who became a lock for an All-Star nod and was regularly a top-20 player in the league.
However, things started to ramp up in the last month of action, and that hot hitting carried into the postseason.
He played in eight playoff games, had 31 plate appearances, and hit one home run, scored four runs, drove in two runs, and stole two bases.
Tucker finished with a line of .333/.419/.519, far better than the regular season, and was arguably the best player on the team throughout the postseason.
Now, after the postseason, Tucker has received an MLB All-Postseason Team nod via MLB.com.
“To his credit, Tucker put a lost regular season behind him and looked at his best in the postseason — ironic, too, considering how the rest of L.A.’s high-powered lineup slumped around him,” Jared Greenspan wrote for MLB.com.
What is next for Kyle Tucker
Tucker and the Dodgers now get the chance to regroup, assess what happened, and work on avoiding another disappointing regular season.
His postseason exploits weren’t enough to erase his regular-season slump, but an All-Star-caliber year in 2027 would put that down year behind him.
After the season, Tucker seemed grateful to Dodgers fans for their support.
“Through every high and low, thank you to our fans for riding with us all season, Tucker wrote. “We appreciate the love and support more than you know. This isn’t the end – we’ll be back.”

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Red Sox-Randy Arozarena Rumors Heating Up Before Free Agency
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: Will the Boston Red Sox go shopping at the top of the market in free agency this winter? After the 2026 season, there's no denying the fact that the Red Sox need a little bit more offense. The most obvious way to boost it would be more power. The Red Sox finished 26th in the league in home runs in 2026 with 163. Naturally, this has led to a lot of buzz already about which players could help the club. Earlier in the week, ESPN's David Schoenfield shared a column featuring the "best fit" for each
item.content:encoded:
Will the Boston Red Sox go shopping at the top of the market in free agency this winter?
After the 2026 season, there's no denying the fact that the Red Sox need a little bit more offense. The most obvious way to boost it would be more power. The Red Sox finished 26th in the league in home runs in 2026 with 163. Naturally, this has led to a lot of buzz already about which players could help the club. Earlier in the week, ESPN's David Schoenfield shared a column featuring the "best fit" for each top free agent and connected Boston to one of the top bats available, along with the Atlanta Braves. He now joins others, like Ryan Divish of The Seattle Times who have connected Boston to the slugger.
"[Randy Arozarena] one of the few good hitters available — but he's also 32 years old and is limited to left field on defense," Schoenfield wrote. "Arozarena has reportedly expressed a desire to return to the East Coast. If that's the case, there are two logical fits in the Braves and Red Sox. Braves left fielders were 27th in OPS while Red Sox left fielders -- mostly Jarren Duran, who had a bad offensive season — were 26th."
Is Randy Arozarena The Answer?
A lack of power has been the talk of Boston dating back to last offseason. It's true that the Red Sox could use more pop in the middle of the order. Arozarena hit 26 home runs in 2026 and would give Boston a boost in that area. Another important area where he would help Boston is on the base paths. He stole 26 bases in 2026, which would have led the Red Sox.
In the World Series, the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays showed you don't necessarily need to lead the league in homers to have success. The Brewers hit fewer home runs than Boston in the regular season. But both the Brewers and Rays make up for the lack of pop in other ways. The Rays finished tied for second in the league in stolen bases and the Brewers finished fifth, for example. The Brewers also led the league in on-base percentage and Milwaukee and Tampa Bay tied at the top of the standings in team batting average.
Arozarena is a player who would give Boston the best of both worlds. He'd add power, but also speed that Boston is lacking. Arguably, the Red Sox aren't very far from contending. A full season of Adley Rutschman and Curtis Mead will improve the offense. Plus, if Roman Anthony can stay healthy that would be a game-changer.
If Boston is comfortable handing out a big contract, Arozarena would help. But there would be more work to do afterward, like trading Jarren Duran. He's not a perfect fit, but he would boost two areas the Red Sox need. If Boston doesn't go for Arozarena, it will still need to find an offensive identity for 2027. If power isn't the answer, then Boston needs speed or another high on-base guy. The Red Sox's pitching is right up there with the Rays and Brewers. Now, the Red Sox need the offense to catch up.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding Boston Red Sox On SI, please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com
Follow patmcavoy

item.description: カブスからFAとなった鈴木誠也外野手（32）について、複数の米メディアが移籍先に最も適した球団として岡本和真内野手（30）が所属するブルージェイズを挙げた。 ESPN電子版は30日付の記事で、今オフFA市場の目玉の1人と目される鈴木について「カブスでの5年間は、目を見張るほど安定して結果を出す打者だった」と称賛。「ブルージェイズは計算できる打線の中軸の獲得が必須。外野手兼DHのジョージ・スプリンガーとマイルズ・ストローがFAとなって抜けるため、その予算をスズキに使える」とした。 ニューヨークのスポーツ専門テレビ局SNY電子版も同日付の「今オフのFAトップ10」を特集した記事で、鈴木について「インパクトのある打者が市場に少ない中で、最も高評価になる可能性がある。右翼の守備でも強肩を発揮した」と称賛。ブルージェイズに入団すれば「今季不振に苦しんだウラジーミル・ゲレロをプロテクトする存在になるかもしれない」とした。これらメディアの予想通りなら、侍ジャパンのメンバーとして共にWBCを戦った2人がメジャーでもタッグを組むことになる。

item.content:encoded:
「すべてを凌駕するオファーを…」ドジャース、鈴木誠也獲得の可能性が高くなった！？ 米メディアが示唆「争奪戦になる可能性は高いが…」
2026.10.31 11:45 NEW
Getty Images
大谷翔平 最新情報
　ロサンゼルス・ドジャースが今オフ、テオスカー・ヘルナンデス外野手をトレードで放出した場合、その後釜としてシカゴ・カブスの鈴木誠也選手を獲得する可能性が浮上している。右打ちの長打力を補える存在として、鈴木への関心が取り沙汰されている。米メディア『ヘビー』のT.J.フレンチ記者が10月28日（日本時間29日）に言及した。
鈴木は今季、打率.270、本塁打26、打点86、安打147を記録。今オフでは日本からポスティングされて以降、初めてMLBのフリーエージェント（FA）市場に出る予定で、外野手では有力選手の1人とみられている。
そこで、来季のワールドシリーズ進出を目指すドジャースが獲得すべき選手として鈴木が挙げられた。ドジャースは有望株のホスエ・デポーラ外野手の出場枠を空けるためヘルナンデスを放出するとの見方がある一方、経験豊富な打者も補強したいとも考えている。
鈴木の市場価値については、4年総額1億700万ドル（約169億円）程度になると予想された。ドジャースであれば、この金額を出すことは問題ないだろう。
注目の集まる鈴木の動向についてフレンチ氏は「これはドジャースにとって十分に支払える金額であり、今オフに一部の契約金を帳簿から切り離すことができればなおさらだ。しかし、彼は争奪戦になる可能性が高いため、現実的にドジャースがそれらすべてを凌駕するオファーを出せるだろうか。それは、球団がこの32歳の外野手にどれほど強い関心を寄せているかにかかっている」と言及した。
ドジャースにはすでに大谷翔平選手という主軸がいるが、もし鈴木が加入となれば、日本人同級生として共闘することになる。ドジャース打線もさらに厚みを増すことになり、鈴木の去就に注目したい。

カブスFAとなった鈴木誠也外野手（32）の移籍先候補として30日（日本時間31日）、「ESPN」がブルージェイズを最適球団に挙げた。昨季、岡本和真内野手（29）を補強したカナダ・トロントに本拠地を置く球団で、カブスとの再契約は「最優先事項にはならない」と見込んだ。
鈴木の評価について「5年間で驚くほど安定した打撃成績を残した。今季は予想外ともいえるほど優れた守備指標にも支えられ、WARで自己最高を記録。仮に守備面での好成績が一時的なものだったとしても、鈴木は打撃で得点を生み出せる選手」と好守で優れた能力を強調。だが、カブスは「補強資金を優先的に投入するのは先発ローテーションとなる見込み」とした。
昨年ワールドシリーズに進出するも、今季はア・リーグ最下位に沈んだブルージェイズは「外野陣のOPSが2025年のMLB7位から19位に低下し、戦力の底上げが必要。打線の中軸を任せられる安定した打者の獲得が不可欠となっている」と分析。他の移籍先候補にはタイガースを挙げ、「打線の新たな柱となる選手を獲得すべき。ライリー・グリーン、マックス・クラーク、鈴木で構成される外野陣を想像してみてほしい。デトロイトの来季の年俸総額は2026年と比べて約7000万ドル少なくなる見込みで、鈴木の獲得に加え、投手陣の補強にも資金を投入する余裕がある」と金銭的な余裕がある球団も候補になるとした。

item.title: [Sportsnet.ca] Bichette exercises $42 million player option to keep Mets contract
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: NEW YORK — Sandy Alcantara was blocked from becoming a free agent by the Miami Marlins, while Michael King went on the market Friday and Bo Bichette decided to keep his contract with the New York Mets. item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK — Sandy Alcantara was blocked from becoming a free agent by the Miami Marlins, while Michael King went on the market Friday and Bo Bichette decided to keep his contract with the New York Mets.
Starting pitchers Sonny Gray and Nick Martinez also will become free agents after their teams declined mutual options.
Miami exercised its $21 million option on Alcantara rather than pay a $2 million buyout, a decision that guarantees the pitcher $75 million over six years as part of the deal he agreed to in November 2021.
A 31-year-old right-hander, Alcantara was 13-11 with a 3.87 ERA in 33 starts and three relief appearances this year, his second season following Tommy John surgery.
King, also a 31-year-old right-hander, is a free agent for the second straight off-season after declining a $28 million player option in favour of a $5 million buyout. He agreed in December to a deal guaranteeing $75 million over three seasons that allowed him to end it after one year and $17 million. He was 12-10 with a 3.21 ERA in 32 starts.
King was among 14 new free agents Friday, raising the total to 155 in the two days following the World Series. About 40 more players potentially could go free by Monday, the deadline for exercising options.
Bichette agreed in January to a $126 million, three-year contract with the Mets that included a $40 million signing bonus, a $2 million salary for 2026 and $42 million player options for both 2027 and 2028.
A two-time All-Star shortstop in Toronto, Bichette shifted primarily to third base in New York, where Francisco Lindor plays shortstop. The 28-year-old Bichette hit .260 with 18 homers and 78 RBIs for the disappointing Mets.
AL champion Tampa Bay declined mutual options on Martinez and outfielder Cedric Mullins.
Martinez, 36, had a $20 million mutual option with a $4 million buyout as part of a $13 million, one-year contract. He set a career high for wins, going 15-6 with a 3.10 ERA in 31 starts and became a first-time All-Star, then went 1-1 with a 2.81 ERA in four post-season appearances that included a start in Game 1 of the World Series.
Mullins, 32, hit .205 with 15 homers, 48 RBIs and 21 stolen bases. He had a $7.5 million, one-year deal that included a $10 million mutual option with a $500,000 buyout.
Boston declined a $30 million option on Gray, who gets a $5 million buyout payable in five $1 million installments on each Jan. 15 from 2027-31. If the Red Sox had exercised the option, Gray could have opted out and received the $5 million as a buyout payable on the same dates.
Gray, a right-hander who turns 37 next week, agreed to a $75 million, three-year contract with St. Louis in November 2023 and was traded to Boston last November. He tied for the major league lead with 18 wins this year and posted a 2.72 ERA, his best in a full season.
Dustin May, who started Game 4 of the World Series for Milwaukee on Tuesday, went free when he declined a $20 million mutual option with the World Series champion Brewers in favour of a $500,000 buyout. May agreed to a $12.5 million contract with the Cardinals in December and was acquired by the Brewers at the Aug. 3 trade deadline. The 29-year-old right-hander went 7-9 with a 4.70 ERA in 31 starts.
Chicago Cubs left-hander Matt Boyd and catcher Carson Kelly declined mutual options.
A 35-year-old left-hander, Boyd agreed to a $29 million, two-year contract before the 2024 season that included a $15 million mutual option for 2027 with a $2 million buyout. He became a first-time All-Star in 2025, going 14-8 with a 3.21 ERA, and was 10-5 with a 3.91 ERA this season.
Kelly, 32, gets a $1.5 million buyout rather than a $7.5 million salary as part of the $11.5 million, two-year deal he reached in December 2024. He hit .258 with 10 homers and 58 RBIs in 120 games this year.
Baltimore declined a $25 million mutual option on pitcher Zach Eflin and owes a $2 million buyout as part of a one-year contract guaranteeing $10 million. The right-hander made one appearance, on March 31, and had Tommy John surgery on April 8, his 32nd birthday.
First baseman Josh Bell became a free agent after his $10 million mutual option was declined by the Minnesota Twins. He gets a $1.25 million buyout as part of a $7 million, one-year contract. The 34-year-old hit .255 with 21 homers and 96 RBIs.
Minnesota also declined a $13 million mutual option on right-hander Joe Ryan, who gets a $100,000 buyout as part of a $6.2 million, one-year contract. Ryan remains under club control and is eligible for salary arbitration.
The Athletics declined options on infielder Jeff McNeil and left-hander Jeffrey Springs.
McNeil had a $15.75 million club option with a $2 million buyout as part of a $50 million, four-year contract he signed with the Mets after leading the major leagues with a .326 batting average in 2022. The 34-year-old was acquired in a trade last December and batted .264 with nine homers and 59 RBIs.
Springs' $15 million team option was declined in favour of a $750,000 buyout, completing a $15 million, four-year contract he signed with Tampa Bay. The 34-year-old left-hander, acquired by the A's in a December 2024 trade, was 4-14 with a 6.18 ERA in 29 starts this year and allowed an AL-high 35 home runs.
Kansas City declined a $13 million option on reliever Carlos Estévez, who gets a $2 million buyout as part of a $22 million, two-year contract. The 33-year-old right-hander led the major leagues with 42 saves in 2024, then made just one appearance this year during an injury-decimated season, allowing a game-ending grand slam to Atlanta's Dominic Smith on March 28.
Estévez was placed on the injured list April 1 because of a bruised left foot, strained the rotator cuff in his pitching shoulder during rehab and had shoulder surgery in September.
Kansas City exercised a $2.5 million club option on right-hander Tony Gonsolin, a 2022 All-Star with the Los Angeles Dodgers who signed in mid-August for a prorated portion of a $1 million salary. He had right elbow surgery in August 2025, made four minor league injury rehab appearances for the Royals last Aug. 26 to Sept. 17 and returned to the major leagues when he allowed five runs over 2 2/3 innings against the Chicago White Sox on Sept. 22.
Houston declined a $5 million team option on Ryan Weiss and owes a $500,000 buyout as part of a $2.6 million, one-year deal he signed after two years with Hanwha in South Korea. The 29-year-old right-hander was 0-3 with a 7.62 ERA in two starts and seven relief appearances, then was optioned to Triple-A Sugar Land on May 5 and spent the rest of the season at Triple-A.
Robert Stephenson's $2.5 million option was declined by the Los Angeles Angels. A 33-year-old right-hander, Stephenson signed a $33 million, three-year contract before the 2024 season and pitched just 10 innings over 12 games during the deal. He had Tommy John surgery in April 2024, returned to make a pair of appearances for the Angels in late May 2025, then went on the injured list with right biceps inflammation. Stephenson made eight more appearances in late August and September, was bothered by thoracic outlet syndrome symptoms during the off-season and had ligament and flexor tendon surgery this April.

Misiorowski was asked to name the teammate who made th
item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers capped their season with a World Series championship on Wednesday, thanks in large part to contributions from Jacob Misiorowski and William Contreras. Misiorowski is expected to contend for the National League Cy Young Award, while Contreras took home World Series MVP honors. After the title-clinching victory, the MLB Players Association posted a video showing Misiorowski delivering a memorable shoutout to his teammate.
Misiorowski was asked to name the teammate who made the greatest difference in his game throughout the 2026 campaign.
"I mean, it's easy to say William," commented the Brewers flamethrower.
You know, he's there every outing it feels like. He's there motivating me through. You know, even when I'm not on the field, he's still giving me pointers of like, 'Hey, did you see this swing off this guy? We should do that next time you come out.'"
Jacob Misiorowski on William Contreras' impact on his game
The MLBPA summed up their connection with a fitting caption: "The relationship between a pitcher and his catcher is truly one of a kind."
"That dude's always grinding, always doing something to help the pitchers out… Obviously I'm just one of the six guys we have starting, and I think every single one of our guys would say the exact same thing… That dude has worked his a** off all year," Misiorowski continued.
Statistics only tell part of the story. A pitcher's connection with his catcher can shape how well they perform together, from building trust to making adjustments throughout a game. Contreras was behind the plate for Misiorowski throughout the season, and it's worth considering how much that partnership contributed to the young pitcher's success.
Misiorowski deserves plenty of recognition for what he accomplished, especially with a fastball that can reach the triple digits. However, Contreras' ability to manage the game and work behind the plate also played an important part in helping the young pitcher thrive.

item.content:encoded:
Which current players may be potential witnesses during Guardians' Emmanuel Clase, Luis Ortiz trial? appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The federal trial involving Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz is expected to feature testimony from several prominent MLB figures, including current players, team executives and league officials. Among the potential witnesses identified in court-related documents are Guardians general manager Mike Chernoff, assistant general manager Matt Forman, pitching coach Carl Willis and coach/interpreter Agustin Rivero, per The Athletic.
Current and former Cleveland catchers Austin Hedges, Mike Zunino and Bo Naylor have also been identified as potential witnesses. All three catchers were involved in receiving pitches that prosecutors allege were manipulated as part of the betting scheme. However, the actual witness lists remain under seal, and it is not yet established which individuals will ultimately testify.
Regardless, an MLB monitor had initially notified Matt Forman that Clase was using his cellphone in the clubhouse during a game, violating league policy. Forman subsequently reported the incident to MLB.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Quest Meeks, who leads MLB's policy, integrity and compliance division, is also among the identified potential witnesses. Meeks previously testified as a prosecution witness in the federal case involving former Los Angeles Dodgers player Yasiel Puig in January.
Paul Mifsud, MLB's head baseball operations counsel, is also listed. The government identified a total of 42 potential witnesses in proposed jury-selection questions, with the final list expected to be announced later.
The financial allegations are substantial. According to the prosecution, bettors involved in the arrangement generated more than $450,000 in profits through wagers connected to Clase's pitches.
The trial will determine whether Clase and Ortiz deliberately manipulated pitches to help bettors profit, or whether the alleged suspicious pitches were legitimate baseball strategy. With both pitchers pleading not guilty and MLB awaiting the outcome of its investigation, the case could have significant consequences for their careers.

item.description: As the Seattle Mariners enter the offseason, trade suggestions fit them as a potential landing spot for Cleveland Guardians outfielder Steven Kwan. item.content:encoded:
As the Seattle Mariners enter the offseason, trade suggestions fit them as a potential landing spot for Cleveland Guardians outfielder Steven Kwan. Many Mariners fans continue to discuss about the possibility of adding Kwan given the need for a well-balanced corner outfielder. While Kwan lacks the power that the Mariners have coveted at that position, his bat-t0-ball skills and quality fielding make him an incredibly valuable player.
In five seasons with the Cleveland Guardians, Kwan batted .282/.357/.382 with 39 home runs. The lack of power is a concern for Kwan if he comes to T-Mobile park, but the Mariners would be acquiring a player with a solid floor. Seattle desperately needs players who can be a for sure acquisition, and he could fit the bill there.
Kwan is also on the last year of his contract. While the Guardians will assuredly want an impactful return to give up Kwan, the Mariners have the farm system and pitching to deal from to get a deal done. It is just a matter if the Mariners feel like his offense would not crater in Seattle. That has been their hesitancy about acquiring contact first players previously.
Seattle Mariners Trade Speculation Involves Cleveland Guardians Steven Kwan Yet Again
Acquiring Kwan would certainly signal to Mariners fans that the organization is serious about reviving this team’s postseason aspirations in 2027. As the world just saw, Kwan operated at a high level throughout the postseason to help the Cleveland Guardians reach the American League Championship Series against the Tampa Bay Rays. He would be a meaningful part of any Major League roster, but the Mariners need outfielders more than other teams especially with the expected departure of Randy Arozarena.
Other trade suggestions have speculated the Mariners with players such as Jarren Durran of the Boston Red Sox and Teoscar Hernandez of the Los Angeles Dodgers, which would be an unexpected reunion to say the least. While those two players have a pedigree of their own, their recent production also indicates that they would need to bounce back significantly in 2027 to help Seattle. Kwan on the other hand would not necessarily require that much of a leap of faith unless you believe he would not be able to hit with the Mariners.
A Kwan Trade Would Solve More Problems Than Not
The Mariners acquiring Kwan would certainly appease the appetite of Seattle fans, many of whom have sought to add Steven Kwan for years.
An outfield of Kwan, Julio Rodriguez, and Dominic Canzone would certainly be an improvement defensively for the Seattle Mariners. However, the team needs to do more than that if such a move would to occur. The team needs offense, which would not be the focus of adding a player like Kwan. He is a good all-around player though there is no doubt about that, and the Mariners lacked complete players in 2026. Their stars regressed not just offensively but defensively as well. For Kwan, there is very little downside in his profile compared to the boom-or-bust approach of other Mariners hitters like Cal Raleigh.

item.title: [OCNJ Daily] Seiya Suzuki or Randy Arozarena, who would be a better fit for Phillies?
item.dc:creator: Tim Kelly
item.description: If you want the Phillies to sign either Seiya Suzuki or Randy Arozarena this winter, you’d better get comfortable with being uncomfortable. Suzuki and Arozarena — probably the top two bats available this offseason, and certainly the best outfield sticks — will both receive and decline qualifying offers. item.content:encoded:
If you want the Phillies to sign either Seiya Suzuki or Randy Arozarena this winter, you’d better get comfortable with being uncomfortable.
Suzuki and Arozarena — probably the top two bats available this offseason, and certainly the best outfield sticks — will both receive and decline qualifying offers. That means the Phillies would have to give up $1 million in international bonus pool money, along with their second- and fifth-round picks in the 2027 MLB Draft to sign either. That’s in addition to whatever it takes to sign either, with it very possible that both will require commitments of five years and at least $100 million.
Considering both Suzuki and Arozarena are entering their age-32 seasons and coming off of career years, there’s definitely a case to be made that the Phillies should look elsewhere for outfield help. Ian Happ — Suzuki’s long-time teammate with the Chicago Cubs — could be an alternative who requires a shorter commitment.
But for much, if not all, of this era, the Phillies have lacked right-handed thump in their outfield. Even if president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski doesn’t want to give five years to Suzuki or Arozarena, you can argue that the Phillies can’t afford to pass up on the opportunity to sign one of these two given how hard it’s proven to find a middle-of-the-order bat that’s right-handed and plays in the outfield in recent years.
The question then becomes, if the Phillies are going to take the plunge, which of the two would be better?
Seiya Suzuki’s Pros and Cons
The Cubs gave Seiya Suzuki a five-year/$85 million deal when he came stateside before the 2022 season, and he’s likely to get another half decade contract this offseason, but with a higher overall value this time around.
He hit .270 with 26 home runs, 86 RBIs, 81 walks and an .841 OPS in his contract year. While this was probably Suzuki’s best overall offensive season, he’s been pretty consistent at the plate over his five seasons. He’s recorded exactly 31 doubles in three of the last four seasons, including 2026. He’s a career .269 hitter with an .823 OPS, so it’s not like this year was a major outlier.
However, the reason Suzuki set a career-high with a 4.5 WAR this season — FanGraphs says his previous high water mark was 3.5 in 2024 — is because he made drastic defensive improvements. He played just 282 innings in right field in 2025, with the Cubs utilizing him mostly as a DH and occasionally left field when they had Kyle Tucker. But after Tucker departed in free agency, Suzuki returned to right field on a full-time basis. He went from posting minus-four defensive runs saved and minus-one out above average over 282 innings in right field in 2025 to 14 DRS and four OAA across 972 2/3 frames in 2026.
It’s a credit to Suzuki, and the fact that he’s a right fielder might make him slightly more valuable defensively than Arozarena. But that’s only if you buy his defensive improvement this past year, because the Phillies don’t have room for another DH.
Another interesting angle to Suzuki as a free agent is that the Phillies as an organization have been trying to establish a foothold in the Japanese market, a place they’ve clearly lagged behind other major spenders. The only two Japanese-born players to ever play for the Phillies are Tadahito Iguchi and So Taguchi, both of whom last suited up for the club in 2008. Signing Suzuki would get the monkey off the back of the Phillies, and potentially allow them to show future Japanese prospects that they are an organization who can support players who come from that portion of the world. Of course, that assumes things go well if they sign Suzuki. And it’s unclear if Suzuki would want that type of pressure.
Randy Arozarena’s Pros and Cons
For as disappointing of a season as the Seattle Mariners had as a team, Arozarena could be headed for a top-five finish in AL MVP voting. The former AL Rookie of the Year led the American League with 113 runs scored, while also homering 26 times, driving in 79 runs, drawing 68 walks and posting an .865 OPS. Arozarena’s season seems even more remarkable considering he played his home games at T-Mobile Park, which consistently grades out as one of the worst stadiums for hitters. Indeed, his OPS was .788 at home, as opposed to .933 on the road. It stands to reason that Arozarena’s season could have been even better if he was playing for pretty much any other team in the sport.
Arozarena’s agent, Scott Boras, will certainly point to that, along with the fact that Arozarena is a red-light player. With just 42 career regular season games under his belt, Arozarena set a new MLB single postseason record with 10 homers in the 2020 playoffs, helping the Tampa Bay Rays to win the pennant. He’s a showman, one whose personality would probably make him an immediate fan favorite in Philadelphia.
That’s the good, but where are the downsides? Arozarena was an A-level player in 2026. He’s been that for other portions of his career, although the .761 OPS he posted between 2022 and 2025 is more than 100 points lower than what he did in 2026. There’s a real chance Arozarena will get paid like an A-level player this offseason, but there’s definitely a risk that he proves be more like a B-level player over the lifetime of his contract.
The other drawback with Arozarena would be that he’s pretty much only a left fielder. In his career, he has minus-five defensive runs saved and minus-26 outs above average in left field. Citizens Bank Park is an easier outfield to patrol than T-Mobile Park or Tropicana Field, the two home parks he’s played in most of his career. But Arozarena has never been a great fielder, and he would be joining a team that finished tied for last in DRS in 2026 at minus-51. Plus, if he’s cemented in left field, that would limit the options the Phillies have with Trea Turner if he’s not able to convince them to keep him at shortstop.
Verdict
Suzuki is a safer bet offensively, but there’s probably a wider variance in defensive outcomes with him.
Arozarena, if successful, would be one of the most popular players the Phillies have ever had because of the swagger he plays the game with.
But if the Phillies are going to make an investment in another expensive veteran, they better be sure in what they are getting. Over his five MLB seasons, Suzuki has an .823 OPS. During that same period, Arozarena has a .782 OPS. Even if you factor in Arozarena spending the last two and a half seasons in Seattle, Suzuki’s bat gives him the edge.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Braves-Royals Trade Pitch Dumps Ronald Acuña Jr. for $51 Million All-Star Starter
item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: Now that the 2026 MLB season has officially concluded, hot stove season is right around the corner, and there’s been no shortage of rumors circulating across the league. One pertinent rumor about the Atlanta Braves is the idea of trading Ronald Acuña Jr. Atlanta just picked up Ronald’s contract for the 2027 season, but that doesn’t shield him from a trade, and with an apparent rift between him, the Braves organization, and the fans, it makes some sense to move on from Acuña Jr. this offseason be
item.content:encoded:
Now that the 2026 MLB season has officially concluded, hot stove season is right around the corner, and there’s been no shortage of rumors circulating across the league.
One pertinent rumor about the Atlanta Braves is the idea of trading Ronald Acuña Jr. Atlanta just picked up Ronald’s contract for the 2027 season, but that doesn’t shield him from a trade, and with an apparent rift between him, the Braves organization, and the fans, it makes some sense to move on from Acuña Jr. this offseason before he hits free agency after the 2027 campaign.
And if the Braves were to dump Ronald Acuña Jr. in a trade, the Kansas City Royals could be a potential suitor, and in return, Atlanta could ask for All-Star starter Michael Wacha.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Beloved World Series Champion Officially An MLB Free Agent
Recent Rumor Suggests Ronald Acuña Jr. as Trade Target for Royals
In a recent trade rumors piece for FanSided.com, MLB writer Chris Landers suggests the Kansas City Royals acquire Ronald Acuña Jr. in a trade this offseason:
“Overly ambitious? Perhaps. But you can’t deny that Acuña Jr. would be an ideal fit for a Royals team that’s been trying to add more offense to its outfield for years now. Plus, with just two reasonable team options remaining, Kansas City wouldn’t even be on the hook for a new contract that will take an injury-prone player well into his 30s. If the Braves are willing to listen on their star outfielder — and all indications suggest they won’t hang up the phone, at the very least — JJ Picollo needs to be all over this.”
To take it one step further after Landers’ prediction, the Braves could ask the Royals for Michael Wacha in exchange.
A player-swap deal between the Royals and Braves including Wacha and Acuña Jr. would be a deal of pretty equal financial value. Wacha is tied to a 3-year, $51 million contract, which is set to expire after the 2027 season (with a 2028 team option).
If, as Landers notes, the Braves are at least going to field offers for Acuña Jr., they might as well try to acquire a quality starter in return. In 2026, Michael Wacha posted an ERA of 3.32 over 200+ innings.
More MLB on Heavy: 8-Year Atlanta Braves Player Suddenly Becomes MLB Free Agent
Michael Wacha Stands Out as Perfect Braves Trade Target
Although the Royals may be a little hesitant to dish away Michael Wacha, the 35-year-old starter stands out as the perfect trade target for the Atlanta Braves.
He’s a durable, productive arm who has shown an ability in recent seasons to take the ball every fifth day, and he would slot perfectly as the Braves’ No. 2 rotation option behind Chris Sale.
Everyone knows that the Braves have dealt with some starting pitching injury woes in recent woes, which seems to be the biggest topic of discussion in the offseason, but perhaps this offseason is the time when Alex Anthopoulos will finally come to his senses about acquiring (or signing) a durable starter.

item.content:encoded:
Watch William Contreras get 'MVP' chants during Brewers' World Series parade appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Milwaukee Brewers are celebrating with fans on Friday in the World Series parade. While there have been numerous viral moments, one that stood out was the fanbase in attendance giving William Contreras "MVP" chants during the parade.
Contreras was beaming with joy, holding the Commissioner's Trophy in front of thousands of Brewers fans. The 28-year-old catcher bobbed his head to the beat of "MVP" chants swarming through downtown Milwaukee.
Shortly after the "MVP" chants quieted down, Contreras opened up about how much he appreciates the fans giving him and his teammates so much support. He also admitted how much he loves playing for the Brewers, and how proud he is to represent the city of Milwaukee.
"I love it. I love it," Contreras said when asked about being named World Series MVP. "I love it, to be honest. I don't even know what I feel right now. I mean, I'm so glad to be a Milwaukee Brewer. I'm really happy for the city."
In the five games played in the World Series, the seven-year veteran proved to be a difference-maker for his team. Against the Tampa Bay Rays, Contreras recorded eight hits and four RBIs off21 at-bats, giving him a .381 batting average. He was also elite defensively, catching four of the Rays' nine steal attempts and was successful on nine of his 11 challenge attempts.
Not only was he red hot in the World Series, but William Contreras was a menace throughout the entire 2026 campaign. He finished the regular season with a .270 batting average and .341 OBP while totaling 153 hits, 18 home runs, and 94 RBIs (career-high). He also led MLB with 48 assists, along with a league-high fielding percentage for catchers of 100.0%.
Related: Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski draws 'nasty' truth bomb from Hall of Fame pitcher

item.dc:creator: Cole Sullivan
item.description: The MLB season concluded this week when the Milwaukee Brewers were crowned champions for the first time in franchise history after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in five games. Now, the focus shifts to the offseason. On Thursday, 144 players officially entered the free agent market, according to an announcement from the MLBPA. One of those players was a former Houston Astros star who helped the organization win the 2017 World Series. George Springer Immediately Becomes Free Agent Springer left the
item.content:encoded:
The MLB season concluded this week when the Milwaukee Brewers were crowned champions for the first time in franchise history after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in five games.
Now, the focus shifts to the offseason. On Thursday, 144 players officially entered the free agent market, according to an announcement from the MLBPA.
One of those players was a former Houston Astros star who helped the organization win the 2017 World Series.
George Springer Immediately Becomes Free Agent
Springer left the Astros in 2021 and signed with the Toronto Blue Jays, where he has spent the past six seasons. Now, at 37 years old, he has officially hit the open market.
Springer has yet to decide what comes next, as he is reportedly contemplating retirement after an illustrious 13-year career.
When asked about his future at the end of the season and his time with the Blue Jays, Springer said he doesn't know whether he'll retire but emphasized how much he enjoyed his time in Toronto.
"I don't know," Springer said, via Sportsnet's Hazel Mae. "I loved being a Blue Jay. I've loved every single bit of being here. I haven't really gotten that far yet. I've kind of taken every day with these guys in stride."
"Toronto Blue Jays (8): Shane Bieber, Patrick Corbin, Yimi Garcia, Max Scherzer, Paul Sewald, George Springer, Jameson Taillon, Luis Urias."
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
144 Players Become XX(B) Free Agents
➡️ XX(B) Free Agents will be updated daily here: https://t.co/PxfYRZWuOF https://t.co/4LX5aemoJc
— MLBPA Communications (@MLBPA_News) October 29, 2026
Springer's MLB Career
After making his MLB debut with the Astros in 2014, Springer became a staple of the organization for seven seasons. During that time, Houston consistently ranked among the best teams in the major leagues.
Springer earned three All-Star selections during his time in Houston and claimed World Series MVP honors in 2017. He helped the Astros defeat the Los Angeles Dodgers by hitting an impressive five home runs in the series.
Across 795 games with Houston, Springer hit .270 with 832 hits, 174 home runs and 458 RBIs. He undoubtedly established himself as one of the best players in franchise history.
Over his entire MLB career, Springer has appeared in 1,571 games and recorded more than 6,000 at-bats. He has totaled 1,595 hits, 308 home runs and 850 RBIs.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Legendary Astros World Series Champion Immediately Becomes Free Agent appeared first on HEAVY.

Duran is coming off a down season, but his underlying metrics indicate a bounce back season is possible. Previously, Duran performed as one of the better all-around outfielders in all of Major League Baseball. He possesses plenty of power and speed, and he also grades out as an average defender overall. The Seattle Mariners may need a corner outfielder replacement for A
item.content:encoded:
With the MLB offseason now underway, the Seattle Mariners were named as a trade fit for Boston Red Sox outfielder Jarren Duran. Duran is coming off a down season, but his underlying metrics indicate a bounce back season is possible. Previously, Duran performed as one of the better all-around outfielders in all of Major League Baseball. He possesses plenty of power and speed, and he also grades out as an average defender overall.
The Seattle Mariners may need a corner outfielder replacement for All-Star Randy Arozarena as many expect him to depart in free agency. Perhaps Randy will even sign with the Boston Red Sox, making Duran available for a respectable price. If the Seattle Mariners feel they can get Duran back to the player he used to be, a move like this could pay off major dividends.
However, Duran also is known as a fiery personality within the clubhouse, and he has been apart of a few controversies in the past involving fans. Given the Mariners are looking to improve their clubhouse atmosphere, there seem to be too many red flags for the Mariners to be interested.
Seattle Mariners Trade Speculation Involves Boston Red Sox Jarren Duran
This season, Duran batted .207/.266/.361 with 20 home runs and 21 stolen bases. Looking at his contact rates, his hard contact increased significantly this season, yet his batting average of balls in play was .252. Simply, Duran attempted to become less of a contact bat and more of a power bat in 2026, and the results did not help his offensive value. For his career, Duran owns a .254 career batting average, so this is not the norm for him.
In his three best seasons with the Boston Red Sox from 2023 to 2025, Duran’s batting average sat at .276 but he only hit 45 home runs in that span with only one season getting over 20 home runs. It’s logical why he made the adjustment, but he also lost what made him such a fearful presence at the plate before. Seattle tends to rely on power to be successful, so the path for Duran resolving his issues with the Mariners seems to be narrow.
Duran Seems Like a Gamble For a Team In Need of a Guaranteed Option
The Seattle Mariners have too many players looking to bounce back for them to take a chance on another.
While the Mariners do need an outfielder, there is no reason for them to sacrifice prospect capital for a player coming off a down season. That may be more appropriate for free agency, and the Boston Red Sox will assuredly not give up of Duran for nothing. While he may not cost a top 100 prospect from the Mariners farm system, it will be a player not from that accolade. The offseason will yield plenty of superficial connections like this. At the end of the day, it all depends on the price, but Duran may see himself moving teams this offseason given where the Red Sox are at heading into 2027.

item.dc:creator: Nathan Yasis
item.description: William Contreras earned World Series MVP honors after delivering an outstanding performance in the Milwaukee Brewers' five-game triumph over the Tampa Bay Rays. He capped off his impressive series with an RBI double in the decisive Game 5, finishing the matchup with eight hits and four RBIs across five games. Just days after capturing the World Series championship and MVP honors, Contreras added another distinction to his growing list of accolades, this time earning recognition in a more lighth
item.content:encoded:
William Contreras earned World Series MVP honors after delivering an outstanding performance in the Milwaukee Brewers' five-game triumph over the Tampa Bay Rays. He capped off his impressive series with an RBI double in the decisive Game 5, finishing the matchup with eight hits and four RBIs across five games.
Just days after capturing the World Series championship and MVP honors, Contreras added another distinction to his growing list of accolades, this time earning recognition in a more lighthearted and modest fashion.
"I don't want to offend any of the other catchers in the league," Contreras remarked via an interpreter.
"The last thing I want to do is offend any of them, But sitting up here today, champion of the world, I feel like I'm the best catcher in the league. Again, that's no disrespect to any of them. That's the last thing I want to do. But today I feel like I'm the best catcher in the world."
William Contreras' MVP run with the Brewers
Contreras' playoff run has given him a strong argument for being considered baseball's best catcher. He made a major impact at the plate, batting .373 with three home runs and nine RBIs throughout the postseason.
His contributions were especially noticeable in the World Series, where he recorded multiple hits in three consecutive games to help Milwaukee take a 3-0 series advantage. He was just as effective behind the plate, throwing out four baserunners and winning 10-of-13 ABS challenges while showcasing his pitch-framing skills.
Few catchers can match the impact Contreras made on both offense and defense throughout the postseason. His role in bringing a championship to Milwaukee only strengthens his case as one of the game's premier players at the position. After a performance like that, anyone looking to challenge his claim as baseball's top catcher will have a high bar to clear.

item.title: [New York Post] Brewers’ bizarre cigarette ritual revealed after World Series win

Before every game, the Brewers indulged in cigarettes while they took batting practice, hearkening back to the baseball days of yore in which players were synonymous with tobacco usage. “You walk by the cage and see the cigs lit,” outfielder Christian Yelich told ESPN, “and you’re like, the boys are ready to rock.” It’s not uncommon to see players celebrating a massive win with cigars in the middle of their champagne-and-bee
item.content:encoded:
The Brewers threw it back on the way to their first World Series title.
Before every game, the Brewers indulged in cigarettes while they took batting practice, hearkening back to the baseball days of yore in which players were synonymous with tobacco usage.
“You walk by the cage and see the cigs lit,” outfielder Christian Yelich told ESPN, “and you’re like, the boys are ready to rock.”
It’s not uncommon to see players celebrating a massive win with cigars in the middle of their champagne-and-beer-fueled clubhouse parties, though cigarettes are seemingly making a comeback in the big leagues. Several Guardians players were spotted enjoying darts after winning the AL Central last season,
This time around, the Brewers used them as “rally heaters,” as a way to get up for big games.
It worked.
Milwaukee entered the 2026 postseason as MLB’s top seed on the strength of a 103-59 record — one of two teams to break the century mark — and ran roughshod through their playoff foes, compiling an 11-2 mark against the Padres (3-1), Dodgers (4-0) and Rays (4-1).
In the NL Division series against San Diego, they batted .250 with a .688 OPS, and, much like the tips of their cigarettes, were just heating up.
Their sweep of the Dodgers came with a .250/.445/.792 slash line and 2.25 ERA and 1.03 WHIP. Against the Rays, with everything on the line, they mashed to the tune of .280/.396/745.
Players celebrated with them, too. Jake Bauers, Sal Frelick and Brandon Woodruff were caught taking drags following their World Series-clinching 4-1 win over the Rays.
Per ESPN’s Jeff Passan, every MLB team has “at least one player who relishes a dart now and again,” even after baseball banned smokeless tobacco as part of the 2016 collective bargaining agreement.
With baseball about to enter what promises to be a lengthy shutdown during the latest round of CBA talks, the Brewers have time to enjoy some extra puffs.

올 시즌 부상·부진 시달려…거취에 눈길
샐러리캡 두고 노사 갈등 심화 '변수'
[마이애미=AP/뉴시스] 애틀랜타 브레이브스의 김하성이 26일(현지 시간) 미 플로리다주 마이애미 론디포 파크에서 열린 2026 메이저리그 마이애미 말린스와의 경기 8회 초 삼진당한 후 아쉬워하고 있다. 김하성은 3타수 1안타 2득점 1볼넷 1삼진을 기록했고, 애틀랜타는 8-3으로 승리했다. 2026.09.27.
부상과 부진이 겹쳐 올 시즌 기대에 밑도는 성적을 낸 김하성의 이번 겨울은 녹록치 않을 전망이다. MLB 노사가 새 협약을 두고 갈등을 빚고 있는 것도 변수다.
밀워키 브루어스가 월드시리즈 우승을 확정해 MLB의 2026시즌이 완전히 종료되고 하루 뒤인 30일(한국 시간) 메이저리그 선수노조(MLBPA)는 FA 명단을 공개했다.
총 144명의 선수가 FA 자격을 취득했고, 애틀랜타와 1년 계약이 만료된 김하성도 포함됐다.
김하성은 2024시즌을 마친 후부터 3년 연속 FA 시장에 나온다.
2021년 MLB에 진출한 김하성은 2024시즌을 마친 뒤 4년 간 몸 담은 샌디에이고 파드리스를 떠났다.
2024시즌을 앞두고 김하성이 연 평균 2000만 달러, 총액 1억 달러 이상의 대형 계약을 맺을 수 있을 것이라는 전망도 나왔지만, 그해 8월 오른 어깨 부상을 당하면서 스텝이 꼬였다.
김하성은 2024시즌을 마친 후 탬파베이 레이스와 2년, 최대 2900만 달러에 계약했다.
재활을 마치고 2025년 7월에야 빅리그에 복귀한 김하성은 부상 여파로 부진에 시달렸고, 지난해 9월 방출된 후 애틀랜타로 이적했다.
김하성은 2026시즌 연봉 1600만 달러를 받고 애틀랜타에서 뛸 수 있었지만, 옵트아웃(계약 파기 권한)을 행사했다.
다시 FA가 된 김하성은 애틀랜타와 1년, 2000만 달러에 계약하며 2026시즌에도 동행을 이어갔다.
김하성이 단기 계약을 이어간 것은 가치를 입증한 후 장기 계약을 노리겠다는 계산이었지만, 올 시즌에도 불의의 부상 속에 부진한 모습을 보였다.
올해 1월 중순 빙판길에 넘어져 오른손 중지 힘줄 파열 부상을 당하고 수술대에 오른 김하성은 5월에야 빅리그에 돌아왔지만, 극심한 타격 부진을 보였다.
7월에도 오른손 중지 염증 증세를 보여 부상자 명단 신세를 졌던 김하성은 올 시즌 51경기에 출전해 타율 0.116(129타수 15안타) 9타점 11득점, OPS(출루율+장타율) 0.679에 그쳤다.
2023년 내셔널리그 유틸리티 부문 골드글러브를 수상할 정도로 수비력을 갖췄으나 2년 동안 타격 부진에 시달려 좋은 조건의 계약을 기대하기는 어려운 상황이다.
애틀랜타가 김하성에게 퀄리파잉 오퍼를 제안할 가능성은 지극히 낮다.
퀄리파잉 오퍼는 원소속 구단이 FA 자격을 얻는 선수에게 상위 125명 평균 연봉 수준으로 1년 재계약을 제안하는 제도다.
올해 퀄리파잉 오퍼 금액은 2315만 달러로, 김하성의 올해 연봉을 웃돈다. 몸값에 비해 아쉬운 성적을 냈기에 퀄리파잉 오퍼를 기대하긴 어렵다.
MLB 노사가 샐러리캡 도입을 놓고 갈등을 빚고 있는 점도 김하성에게는 달갑지 않다.
올해 12월을 끝으로 기존 노사 협약이 만료되는 가운데 MLB 구단주 측과 선수노조는 새 협약 내용을 두고 팽팽한 줄다리기를 이어가는 중이다.
MLB 30개 구단과 사무국은 샐러리캡 도입을 추진 중이다. 반면 선수노조는 선수 권익을 침해하는 일이라며 강력하게 반발하고 있다.
양 측이 합의에 이르지 못하면 구단주 측이 직장폐쇄에 돌입할 가능성이 있다.
직장폐쇄가 현실화하면 FA 협상과 계약 체결에 차질이 생길 수 있고, 김하성에게도 영향을 미치게 된다.
MLB는 2021시즌 후에도 노사 협상 결렬로 직장폐쇄에 들어갔고, 정규시즌 개막이 일주일 정도 늦춰졌다.
MLB 구단주 측이 마지막으로 샐러리캡 도입을 제안한 1994년에는 선수들이 거세게 반발하면서 7개월 반 동안 파업이 이어졌다. 또 90년 만에 월드시리즈가 취소되는 등 리그가 파행을 겪었다.
김하성은 FA 시장 상황 뿐 아니라 노사 협상까지 지켜봐야 한다.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] MLB’s 2026 Photo of the Year Belongs to Brewers' William Contreras
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: If there is one photo that is going to sum up the 2026 Major League Baseball season, it is going to be the shot of Milwaukee Brewers star William Contreras right after the World Series came to a close on Wednesday night. This photo was a long time coming. It took 57 years for the Brewers organization to hoist a World Series trophy for the first time. item.content:encoded:
If there is one photo that is going to sum up the 2026 Major League Baseball season, it is going to be the shot of Milwaukee Brewers star William Contreras right after the World Series came to a close on Wednesday night.
This photo was a long time coming. It took 57 years for the Brewers organization to hoist a World Series trophy for the first time. This image of Contreras, who was named as the 2026 World Series Most Valuable Player, is a perfect representation of the pure bliss and elation that the fanbase and organization felt on Wednesday night.
Game 5 Was Baseball At It's Best
Baseball brings people together. Whether you're a fan of the Brewers, or any other team in the league, history was made on Wednesday night and fans were paying attention. This is what the league can be when it's at its best. Two great teams faced off in the World Series in the Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays and it just so happened that it was the Brewers came out on top. Fans got to witness a great series and saw two teams playing the right way. In this case, the Brewers won their first title and we came away with this photo. If the Rays had won, it would've been their first title as well.
All in all, a great season ended on a high note.
Unfortunately, now we have to wait until March, at the very least, for real, meaningful games to begin again. But that's not even a guarantee. The collective bargaining agreement will expire in December and there's no way to know right now when the two sides will sort out the labor issues facing the league. The league wants a salary cap and the MLBPA does not. That's going to be at the crux of the discussion this winter, although there's far more than just that simplified summary.
Neither side has come close to caving yet, which isn't shocking. The two sides are negotiating and neither side has a reason to give in yet. But it would be a mistake if they don't meet in the middle and find a way to not ruin the momentum the league has right now. Viewership was up around the league all year and fans were just rewarded with an elite postseason. The baseball world is paying attention. Game 5 on Wednesday night was a perfect example of baseball at its best. Hopefully, the offseason isn't at its worst.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick also received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding Fastball On SI, please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

item.content:encoded:
Pete Crow-Armstrong said the mental side of baseball is the part of the game he struggles with most, and the piece he believes can take him to another level.
The Chicago Cubs center fielder made the comments in a conversation with Cam Johnson on The Old Man and the Three podcast. The episode was released Feb. 24, a month before Opening Day.
“That’s probably the last piece to the puzzle for me,” Crow-Armstrong said. “I know my swing is always going to, I could be Aaron Judge, and his swing doesn’t always feel great. So the mental part really feels like the last thing that can take me to another level.”
Crow-Armstrong was coming off a 2025 season in which he hit 31 home runs and stole 35 bases in 157 games. He made his first All-Star team and won a Gold Glove.
It did not finish cleanly. Amid a second-half slump that September, Cubs manager Craig Counsell sat him for consecutive games to give him what Counsell called a physical and mental break, according to MLB.com.
What drives him day to day is something Crow-Armstrong said he has not settled.
“That’s what I’m still figuring out,” Crow-Armstrong said. “I don’t really know yet. I’ve done the therapy thing. I’ve talked to mental-skills people. But there’s definitely always something that drives you. I love playing baseball, and I love how difficult the sport is. There’s something new about it every day.”
“You’re constantly learning,” Crow-Armstrong continued. “You’re making do with what you’ve got that day, and I think that’s super special.”
“Honestly, the days you wake up feeling like death are probably my favorite days, because you’re like, ‘How are you going to make this work today?'” Crow-Armstrong added. “But I’m not really the one to talk about the mental side of things just yet, because I struggle with that the most. So I just try to take little bits and pieces from dudes I admire, mostly guys on my team.”
Nico Hoerner, a Gold Glove second baseman, finalized a six-year, $141 million extension with the Cubs on March 29.
“Last year, Justin Turner was a big one, just because he has so many years of experience,” Crow-Armstrong explained. “But Nico Hoerner is probably somebody whose mindset I admire the most. He talked to me about being kind to yourself and being emotionally aware, because the season is so long. You forget how you’re actually feeling sometimes when everything is about baseball.”
“He’s like your model baseball player,” Crow-Armstrong continued. “If I had kids, I’d be like, ‘Watch how he runs to first base and then comes back to the dugout.’ He’s wired all the time. He lets his emotions out when the time calls for it, but other than that, he’s super stoic. So I lean on him very heavily.”
The Cubs announced Crow-Armstrong’s six-year, $115 million extension on March 26, after a season-opening loss to the Washington Nationals. With escalators, the deal can reach $133 million.
It begins in 2027 and includes a $5 million signing bonus. His salary sits at $10 million in each of the first three seasons. In 2030 it climbs to $20 million, followed by $30 million in 2031 and again in 2032.
Crow-Armstrong played all 162 games in 2026 and hit .280 with a .372 on-base percentage and a .570 slugging percentage. His 45 home runs led the National League. He added 107 RBI, 119 runs and 41 stolen bases to join the 40-40 club.
October was a different story. The Cubs went 89-73, finished 14 games behind the Milwaukee Brewers in the NL Central and were swept by the San Diego Padres in the NL Wild Card Series, losing 8-0 and 4-1 at Petco Park. Crow-Armstrong went 0-for-7, and the Cubs scored one run in the series.
Should that last piece fall into place, the Cubs have the 24-year-old under contract through 2032.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers Get Boost in Tarik Skubal Free Agency Pursuit
item.dc:creator: Aaron Coloma
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers free agent starting pitcher Tarik Skubal is the best free agent on the market this offseason, with some experts believing he could receive a deal in excess of $400 million. According to ESPN's Alden Gonzalez, though, the two-time Cy Young-winning left-hander may command a lower price than that, which is good news for the Dodgers, who will definitely be in the race to maintain him. Yoshinobu Yamamoto currently holds the largest pitcher contract by total value in MLB history at
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers free agent starting pitcher Tarik Skubal is the best free agent on the market this offseason, with some experts believing he could receive a deal in excess of $400 million.
According to ESPN's Alden Gonzalez, though, the two-time Cy Young-winning left-hander may command a lower price than that, which is good news for the Dodgers, who will definitely be in the race to maintain him.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto currently holds the largest pitcher contract by total value in MLB history at $325 million, which may have been possible for Skubal a couple of years ago, but Gonzalez believes Skubal is being held back by a few factors.
"But he's also 30 years old, at a time when pitchers break down and teams are only willing to dole out massive contracts to players at earlier ages, with a recent elbow surgery to boot," Gonzalez wrote. "Skubal clearly won't get the 12-year deal that allowed Yamamoto's guarantee to stretch so high, and some executives have a hard time believing he'll get 10. Said one: 'The price will be huge, but I don't think he's touching 400.'"
Why is This Good News for the Dodgers?
The Dodgers aren't any strangers to handing out big, long contracts, but Katie Woo of The Athletic doesn't see them doing the same with a 10-year, $400 million deal with Skubal.
'I can't see [Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman] stomaching a 10-year, $400 million contract if it gets up that high," Woo said on 97.1 The Fan.
"The only way I see the Dodgers really being fierce competitors for Skubal is if Skubal is willing to take a deal similar to the structure and the concept like Kyle Tucker.
"Obviously, the money and the monetary values are going to be different, but if you can get a shorter-term, three-to-four-year contract with opt-outs and a super high AAV, that's, I think, the only way that we can see the Dodgers being real major players for Skubal."
The Dodgers signed Tucker to a four-year, $240 million deal last offseason, and his $60 million annual average value is second on the team only to Shohei Ohtani. The Dodgers are more than capable of handing out a deal of that size, and could very well do so if they see Skubal in their long-term plans.
Does Tarik Skubal Deserve a Big Deal?
Skubal, 30, is without a doubt one of MLB's best pitchers, but entering the latter half of his MLB career, it's understandable that teams would offer him less than they would have a few years ago.
The southpaw will enter his eighth MLB season next year, fresh off of an elbow surgery in 2026 to remove loose bodies from his elbow. He had a 2.72 ERA across 26 starts with the Dodgers and the Detroit Tigers, striking out 186 batters in 158.2 innings pitched.
Those numbers aren't quite at the same level as his unbelievable 2024 and 2025 seasons, but they're also nothing to scoff at.
The better part of Skubal's season came with the Dodgers, as he had a 2.61 ERA through 10 starts to close the year, striking out 70 batters in 62 innings. He also had a good postseason, allowing just three runs through 11 innings for a 2.45 ERA.
Skubal's performances with the Dodgers proved he can be a functioning piece in the Dodgers' puzzle, and bringing him back on a deal similar to Tucker's would make a statement to the rest of the league following a disappointing end to the 2026 season.

米大リーグ選手会は29日（日本時間30日）、FA選手144人のリストを公表。日本選手ではロッキーズの菅野智之投手、カブスの今永昇太投手と鈴木誠也外野手の3人が入った。米報道によると、アストロズの今井達也投手は残り2年3600万ドル（約56億8000万円）の契約を破棄できるオプトアウトの権利を行使せず、来季のチーム残留を決断した。
11日に37歳を迎えた菅野はチームのエースとして29先発し、メジャー1年目だった昨季の10勝を上回る12勝（12敗、防御率5・37）をマーク。今季の年俸は昨季の1300万ドル（約20億5000万円）から510万ドル（約8億円）に下げたが、154回1／3を投げてチーム最多の勝ち星を手にした。
カブスの鈴木は5年8500万ドル（約134億3000万円）の契約を満了。5年目の今季は143試合に出場して、打率・270、26本塁打、86打点、OPS・841をマーク。3月のワールド・ベースボール・クラシック（WBC）で右膝を負傷したため、開幕を出遅れたが、打線の中軸として4年連続20本塁打をマークするなど、攻守でチームをけん引し、プレーオフ進出に大きく貢献した。
今オフは阪神からポスティングシステムを利用してメジャー移籍を目指す佐藤輝明内野手とともに野手最大の目玉として注目を集めている。
メジャー3年目の今永は自己最多の32先発＆174回1／3を投げて11勝10敗、防御率3・77をマーク。単年2202万5000ドル（約34億8000万円）のクオリファイングオファーを受諾して臨んだシーズンはローテーションの柱として先発陣を支えた。
大谷翔平、山本由伸、佐々木朗希の3投手が所属するドジャースからは9人がFAに。8月のトレード期限にタイガースから獲得したタリク・スクバル投手をはじめ、ベテランユーティリティのキケ・ヘルナンデス内野手、ブレイク・トライネン、アレックス・ベシア、エバン・フィリップス、クリス・ブービック、ブラスダー・グラテロル、エリック・ラウアーの6投手、すでに現役引退を表明しているミゲル・ロハス内野手がリスト入り。中でも2年連続サイ・ヤング賞を受賞している左腕のスクバルは今オフ、最大のFA選手と位置付けられている。

item.dc:creator: Grey Papke
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers won their first World Series in franchise history on Wednesday night, but the entire team wished Bob Uecker could have been around to see it. item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers won their first World Series in franchise history on Wednesday night, but the entire team wished Bob Uecker could have been around to see it.
Uecker, the Brewers’ famous longtime radio voice, died at 90 in January of 2025, but his name was invoked frequently both during and after the team’s run to the championship. Christian Yelich, one of the longest-tenured Brewers, summed that up in his postgame interview.
“He’s smiling, man. I really wish he could have been here to see this,” Yelich said. “It would have meant everything to him, but like we said a bunch, he’s been with us a lot. We keep him close to our hearts.
“This one’s still for Bob, still for Ueck. Uecky, I love you, man, and we did it.”
“I don’t even know how to describe this, it’s the best feeling ever!” @Brewers captain Christian Yelich talks with @Ken_Rosenthal after winning the 2026 World Series @MLBONFOX https://t.co/Hfs07kJ986
— FOX Sports (@FOXSports) October 29, 2026
Uecker died of cancer in January 2025. He was recognizable nationally thanks to his commercial exploits and his role in “Major League.” He was particularly loved in Milwaukee, where he had called games since 1971.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Red Sox decisions on Sonny Gray, Garrett Whitlock due soon — and there's not much suspense
item.dc:creator: Chris Cotillo
item.description: With the Brewers defeating the Rays in the World Series, MLB's offseason is upon us. It should be a busy one for the Red Sox, who will try to make moves to get over the hump after quick postseason exits in back-to-back seasons. The first days of hot stove season include deadlines that force action so the Red Sox have to make some moves before next week. On Wednesday, we outlined the impending 40-man roster crunch that's about to take place and the Red Sox need to clear four roster spots by Monda
item.content:encoded:
With the Brewers defeating the Rays in the World Series, MLB's offseason is upon us. It should be a busy one for the Red Sox, who will try to make moves to get over the hump after quick postseason exits in back-to-back seasons.
The first days of hot stove season include deadlines that force action so the Red Sox have to make some moves before next week. On Wednesday, we outlined the impending 40-man roster crunch that's about to take place and the Red Sox need to clear four roster spots by Monday afternoon. The other business at hand this week involves two categories: player options/opt-outs and qualifying offers.
The Sox won't find themselves in the qualifying offer business this year because two of their free agents, Isiah Kiner-Falefa and Patrick Sandoval, aren't candidates to receive a $23.15 million salary for 2027 and Sonny Gray, their other projected free agent, isn't eligible for one because he received one (and declined it) as a member of the Twins in 2023. (Players can't get qualifying offers more than once in their careers). When it comes to options, the Red Sox have just two pieces of business to solve, and both are rather straightforward.
Garrett Whitlock — $8.25 million club option (or $1 million buyout)
When Whitlock signed a four-year, $21.75 million extension with the Red Sox in April 2022, that deal included club options for a fifth and sixth season (2027 and 2028). A decision is due on the first of those this week with the Red Sox having the option to retain Whitlock for $8.25 million or send him into free agency with a $1 million buyout.
Considering Whitlock was one of the best relievers in baseball last year — he had a 1.72 ERA and struck out 59 batters in 52 ⅓ innings — that should be an easy call. He'd make much more on the open market as a dominant 30-year-old reliever and re-upping him at $8.25 million would seem to be a bargain for the Red Sox. Under Craig Breslow, the club doesn't like making decisions until it absolutely has to, which is likely the primary reason no official call has been made yet. Still, it feels like a formality.
Whitlock's deal includes a $10.5 million option for 2028 (with a $500,000 buyout attached). He could be a candidate for another extension in the next year or so considering his strong performance in the last two seasons.
Sonny Gray — $30 million mutual option (or $10 million buyout)
Gray's contract — originally a three-year, $75 million deal with St. Louis — was restructured with a sweetener to get him to waive his no-trade clause to join the Red Sox last fall. It paid him a $31 million base salary last year (with the Cardinals chipping in $20 million) with a $30 million mutual option (or $10 million buyout) for 2027.
Mutual options are never exercised in baseball and instead are included as accounting mechanisms that allow teams to manipulate their competitive balance tax (CBT) numbers or pay schedules. Gray's option is all about the buyout being tacked onto the $31 million salary and therefore having his total earnings in 2026 equal $41 million. Either he or the Red Sox will decline the mutual option in the coming days and he will be a free agent. The Red Sox will not receive a compensatory draft pick if he signs elsewhere because he's not a qualifying offer candidate.

item.title: [MLB.com] Which Blue Jays could be up for award hardware?
item.dc:creator: Keegan Matheson
