item.content:encoded:
TORONTO -- The long wait is almost over for the Blue Jays, who have been stuck waiting for the offseason to roll around for over a month now.
On this day last year, the Blue Jays won Game 5 of the World Series in Los Angeles, sending the series back to Toronto with a 3-2 lead over the Dodgers. The 365 days since then haven’t been very kind to Canada’s team.
It’s time to work on turning this back around, though, and that finally gets rolling soon:
Key November dates
First day after World Series: Players become free agents; players may be traded between clubs
Five days after World Series (5 p.m. ET): Deadline for teams to make a qualifying offer to players; players can begin signing with any club
Nov. 10-12: General Managers Meetings in Las Vegas
Nov. 17 (4 p.m. ET): Deadline for players to accept a qualifying offer
Nov. 20: Tender deadline
Major League Baseball’s award season will also feature some Blue Jays content, especially with their five finalists for the AL Gold Glove Awards. Here’s a look at how the awards could break down and which Blue Jays will be involved.
Award watch: Gold Gloves
The Gold Glove Awards will be announced on Sunday on ESPN, with the broadcast beginning at 8:30 p.m. ET.
1B Vladimir Guerrero Jr.
Yes, this one will require you to remember, just for a moment, that the Gold Glove Award is strictly a defensive award. It’s easy to lose this in the mess of a season Guerrero just went through, but his defense was excellent, and if you can look at that in a silo, you’ll see one of his best seasons as a big leaguer. Guerrero’s fielding run value of +6 was the third best among first basemen in the American League, and the eye test backed that up with both fundamental plays and some highlight-reel scoops and dives. He’ll be up against Vinnie Pasquantino of the Royals and Christian Walker of the Astros.
SS Andrés Giménez
It felt like Giménez got better as the year went on, finally settling in as the club’s shortstop after spending most of his big league career at second. Giménez already has three Gold Glove Awards (2022, ‘23, ‘24) from his time with the Guardians, and his +16 fielding run value ranks him second in the AL behind only Bobby Witt Jr. of the Royals. Along with Witt, Taylor Walls of the Rays rounds out the finalists.
RF Nathan Lukes
It’s great to see Lukes get this recognition as a finalist. His defense is criminally underrated, which kept showing up in games when opponents would try to run on Lukes. He’s up against Wilyer Abreu of the Red Sox and Cam Smith of the Astros.
C Brandon Valenzuela
If Valenzuela had started 115 games behind the plate, he might just run away with this award. He and Alejandro Kirk tied for third in the AL at +11 fielding run value, and Valenzuela did that with just 68 starts behind the plate. With his blocking, framing and incredible throwing arm, there might be a couple of these in Valenzuela’s future. He’s up against Dillon Dingler of the Tigers and Austin Wells of the Yankees.
SP José Soriano
Pitchers are always the most difficult race to measure, but Soriano’s reputation as a good fielder and strong athlete have been recognized here. He’ll be up against Tanner Bibee of the Guardians and Jacob deGrom of the Rangers.
Award watch: Everything else
It’s possible that Kazuma Okamoto gets some outside consideration for the AL Rookie of the Year Award after launching 33 home runs in his first MLB season, but his age (30) coming over from Japan adds an interesting wrinkle when compared to players in their early 20s who came up through the Minor Leagues.
Dylan Cease’s case for the Cy Young Award feels like the Blue Jays’ best shot to rank in the top three on a ballot, though. For much of the season, Cease and New York’s Cam Schlittler were in a dead heat, but Schlittler appears to have pulled away down the stretch while Cease’s case faded and he eventually landed on the IL. Regardless, Cease’s season is worth celebrating.
In the first year of his seven-year, $210 million deal, Cease put up a 2.40 ERA with 239 strikeouts over 169 innings, which included some absolutely dominant stretches through the middle of the summer. He’s been everything the Blue Jays could have hoped for and more.

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Florida — El venezolano William Contreras, receptor de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee, fue elegido este miércoles como Jugador Más Valioso (MVP) de la Serie Mundial, la cual ganó su equipo 4-1 ante los Rays de Tampa Bay.
Con la bandera de Venezuela sobre los hombros, una amplia sonrisa y un orgullo evidente, William Contreras estaba dispuesto a alardear un poco.
“No quiero ofender a ninguno de los otros receptores de la liga. Lo último que quiero hacer es ofender a cualquiera de ellos”, dijo. “Pero sentado aquí hoy, campeón del mundo, siento que soy el mejor receptor de la Liga. De nuevo, eso no es una falta de respeto para ninguno de ellos. Es lo último que quiero hacer. Pero hoy siento que soy el mejor catcher del mundo”.
Contreras se convirtió en el octavo receptor elegido el Jugador Más Valioso de la Serie Mundial después de conducir a los Cerveceros de Milwaukee a su primera coronación.
Así fue el rendimiento del venezolano
El venezolano, corazón y alma de un equipo de mercado pequeño, bateó para .381 mientras guiaba al cuerpo de lanzadores de Milwaukee, retiraba a cuatro corredores que intentaron robar base y sacaba provecho del primer Clásico de Otoño con el sistema automatizado de desafío de bolas y strikes (ABS) al ganar 10 de 13 apelaciones. Contreras conectó un doble impulsor en la victoria 4-1 de Milwaukee que aseguró el título en el quinto juego la noche del miércoles.
“Es nuestro pit bull . No te acercas simplemente y lo acaricias . Hay una posibilidad de que te muerda ”, dijo el mánager Pat Murphy.
Deportes
Momentos después de recibir el premio al Más Valioso (MVP), Contreras abrazó a su hermano mayor Willson, primera base de los Medias Rojas de Boston, quien ganó una Serie Mundial con los Cachorros de Chicago en 2016.
“Mi hermano es mi modelo a seguir. No tengo muchos amigos. Él es mi amigo”, dijo William Contreras. “Si tengo algo que preguntarle a alguien, le pregunto a Willson”.
Volvió a emocionarse cuando le preguntaron por Venezuela, su país natal. Contreras integró la selección venezolana que ganó su primer Clásico Mundial de béisbol en marzo, aunque se fue de 13-0 sin carreras impulsadas.
Contreras, junto con sus compañeros y compatriotas Jackson Chourio y Antonio Senzatela se unieron a Alex Bregman y Luke Gregerson (selección de Estados Unidos/Astros de Houston en 2017) como los únicos jugadores en ganar el Clásico Mundial de Béisbol y la Serie Mundial en el mismo año.
“Significa todo porque es la primera vez que los muchachos de Venezuela ganan el Clásico y la Serie Mundial ”, expresó. “Es historia, historia para mi país. Amo a Venezuela. Es mi país”.
Contreras se une a Gene Tenace (1972), Johnny Bench (1976), Steve Yeager (co-ganador en 1981), Darrell Porter (1982), Rick Dempsey (1983), Pat Borders (1992) y su compatriota Salvador Pérez (2015) como receptores que han ganado el premio.
Contreras, de 28 años y tres veces elegido al Juego de Estrellas, bateó para .270 con 18 jonrones y un récord personal de 94 carreras impulsadas. Los Cerveceros ganaron su cuarto título consecutivo de la División Central de la Liga Nacional.
“Piensen en lo que ha logrado, y está decepcionado de que sus números no sean mejores”, dijo Murphy. “Está decepcionado de que no sea Guante de Oro”.
Sacó más provecho que nadie del nuevo sistema de desafío al árbitro robot del béisbol, al liderar las Grandes Ligas con 185 impugnaciones y 105 reversiones durante la temporada regular. Acertó en 22 de 33 en total en la postemporada.
“No es magia”, dijo Contreras. “Creo que es la experiencia de jugar todos los días durante toda la temporada”.
Bateó para .444 con un par de jonrones solitarios en la serie divisional contra San Diego, al conectar un batazo que rompió el empate en la séptima entrada del primer juego y otro jonrón en el tercero. Ostentó un promedio de .357 con un jonrón y tres carreras impulsadas en la barrida de la Serie de Campeonato sobre los Dodgers de Los Ángeles.
Milwaukee tuvo varios candidatos dignos para el MVP.
Cooper Pratt estableció un récord de novato de la Serie Mundial con seis hits consecutivos e igualó la marca de novato de Gil McDougald de 1951 con siete carreras impulsadas, incluyendo hits para tomar la ventaja en los últimos tres juegos. El venezolano Jackson Chourio contabilizó 11 hits, la mayor cantidad de un pelotero en una Serie Mundial de cinco juegos. El as Jacob Misiorowski tuvo marca de 2-0 y permitió apenas una carrera en 10 2/3 entradas, y el relevista Aaron Ashby lanzó 5 2/3 innings sin permitir anotación con un salvamento y nueve ponches.
“Le dije antes del juego: Serás el MVP de la Serie Mundial”, dijo Murphy sobre Contreras. “La gente reconoció lo que ese muchacho hizo por nosotros. No había duda en mi mente. Sí, es especial”.

item.title: [New York Post] Christian Yelich pays heartfelt tribute to Bob Uecker as Brewers finally win World Series
item.dc:creator: Christian Arnold
item.description: Bob Uecker’s presence has remained a big part of the Brewers’ culture since he died last year, and in the franchise’s biggest moment on Wednesday night, Christian Yelich made sure the beloved broadcaster wasn’t forgotten. Yelich had a heartfelt message for Uecker after the Brewers won their first-ever World Series title, defeating the Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night in St. Petersburg, Fla. “He’s smiling, man,” Yelich said to Ken Rosenthal on the Fox broadcast. “I really wish he could have
item.content:encoded:
Bob Uecker’s presence has remained a big part of the Brewers’ culture since he died last year, and in the franchise’s biggest moment on Wednesday night, Christian Yelich made sure the beloved broadcaster wasn’t forgotten.
Yelich had a heartfelt message for Uecker after the Brewers won their first-ever World Series title, defeating the Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night in St. Petersburg, Fla.
“He’s smiling, man,” Yelich said to Ken Rosenthal on the Fox broadcast. “I really wish he could have been here to see this. It would have meant everything to him, but we said a bunch, he’s been with us a lot. We keep him close to our hearts, and this one’s still for Bob and still for Ueck. Ueck, I love you, man, and we did it.”
Uecker was the voice of the Brewers for 54 years and became a beloved figure among Brewers supporters and baseball fans as a whole.
Uecker died on Jan. 16, 2025, at the age of 90 after a private battle with cancer.
Ahead of the first pitch on Wednesday, fans left beer cans at the Uecker statue, TMJ 4 reported.
Following the final out, Hall of Famer CC Sabathia paid homage to Uecker in a post on X.
“Bob Uecker smiling down,” wrote Sabathia, who spent the 2008 season in Milwaukee.
During the Game 4 broadcast on Tuesday, Fox play-by-play man Joe Davis paid tribute to the famed Brewers announcer with his home run call on Cooper Pratt’s solo blast in the 12th inning.
“Hitting a high drive! Deep left field! Get up, get up, gone!” Davis said, emulating Uecker’s signature home run call of “Get up, get up, get outta here, gone!”
“Ueck is obviously a guy that you grew up listening to and was underrated because he was such a comic genius that his ability to master the craft and be an amazing play-by-play announcer didn’t get enough love,” Davis told MLB.com.
“I say that to say I was always studying him and listening to him, and just by osmosis, that stuff is in there.”

item.title: [FOX Sports] Christian Yelich Dedicates Brewers’ First World Series Title To Bob Uecker
item.description: Christian Yelich Dedicates Brewers’ First World Series Title To Bob Uecker Christian Yelich has waited a long time to call himself a World Series champion. In the middle of the celebration, his thoughts turned to the man who wanted it as badly as anyone. After the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 to clinch the first championship in franchise history, Yelich spoke with FOX Sports’ Ken Rosenthal. Rosenthal asked what longtime Brewers broadcaster Bob Uecker would be thinking
item.content:encoded:
Christian Yelich Dedicates Brewers’ First World Series Title To Bob Uecker
Christian Yelich has waited a long time to call himself a World Series champion.
In the middle of the celebration, his thoughts turned to the man who wanted it as badly as anyone.
After the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 to clinch the first championship in franchise history, Yelich spoke with FOX Sports’ Ken Rosenthal. Rosenthal asked what longtime Brewers broadcaster Bob Uecker would be thinking if he were looking down.
"He’s smiling, man. He’s smiling," Yelich said. "I really wish he could have been here to see this. … But like we said a bunch, he’s been with us a lot. We keep him close to our hearts. And this one’s still for Bob."
Bob Uecker, who died in 2025, was the longtime voice of the Brewers. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images)
Uecker, the voice of the Brewers for 54 seasons, died in January 2025 at 90 from small-cell lung cancer, months after calling his final Brewers postseason game. His diagnosis was never made public, but those closest to him knew, including Yelich.
During the Stand Up To Cancer moment in Game 4, every Brewers player’s placard read "UECK." (Photo by Mary DeCicco/MLB Photos via Getty Images)
Uecker’s memory followed the Brewers throughout October.
During Game 4 on Tuesday, play paused after the fifth inning for the annual Stand Up To Cancer moment, when everyone in the ballpark holds up a placard with the name of someone affected by cancer.
As cameras panned across the Brewers lined up in front of their dugout, every placard carried the same name: "UECK."
"It just feels like it’s fitting, the obvious choice to make," Yelich said afterwards.
Yelich has seen this Brewers run take shape since the day he arrived in Milwaukee.
Acquired from the Miami Marlins in January 2018, he won NL MVP in his first season in Milwaukee.
He’s now the second-longest-tenured Brewer behind Brandon Woodruff, and they’re the last two players left from the 2018 team that lost Game 7 of the NLCS to the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Eight years later, Milwaukee finally finished the job. The Brewers swept the Dodgers in the NLCS and then beat the Rays to bring home the city’s first World Series title.
"We’re coming home, baby," Yelich told Rosenthal when asked for his message to Brewers fans. "We can’t wait to see you. Can’t wait to celebrate."

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Ex-Tigers Ace Tarik Skubal Crosses One Potential Suitor Off His List
item.dc:creator: Michael Whitaker
item.description: Because they weren't able to come to an agreement with ace pitcher Tarik Skubal before the 2026 MLB Trade Deadline, the Detroit Tigers shipped him to the defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers in return for a trio of prospects. Skubal and the Dodgers were swept out of the National League Championship Series by the Milwaukee Brewers, ending any dreams of becoming the first team in over 25 years to win three straight World Series titles. Skubal can become an unrestricted free agent af
item.content:encoded:
Because they weren't able to come to an agreement with ace pitcher Tarik Skubal before the 2026 MLB Trade Deadline, the Detroit Tigers shipped him to the defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers in return for a trio of prospects.
Skubal and the Dodgers were swept out of the National League Championship Series by the Milwaukee Brewers, ending any dreams of becoming the first team in over 25 years to win three straight World Series titles.
Skubal can become an unrestricted free agent after the conclusion of the World Series, and he's in line to land a record-breaking new contract. But which team will be the one to step up to the plate and hand him a giant deal?
According to the latest reports, at least one major contender to land Skubal can take their name off his list of potential destinations.
Ex-Detroit Tigers Ace Tarik Skubal Crosses One Potential Suitor Off His List
According to former Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Kevin Pillar, Skubal won't be coming to the Jays.
When asked about the chances of Toronto extending an offer/making a play to land Skubal, Pillar said he didn't believe that it will happen.
"I don't," Pillar said. "They got their ace, they got Dylan Cease and as much as you want to build your team around having this elite starting pitching, I think the Blue Jays have good starting pitching. You can never have enough starting pitching."
"I think the Blue Jays learned this year that they need to distribute that money over position groups as opposed to going out to sign Skubal."
The Blue Jays, who came within a single victory of winning the World Series last fall, failed to defend their American League Championship of 2025 when they failed to make the playoffs this year.
Tarik Skubal Left The Door Open To Returning To The Tigers
Not long after being acquired by the Dodgers, Skubal left the door open to potentially returning to the Tigers at some point.
"I would love to play my whole career in Detroit. I would love to," Skubal explained in an interview with Pardon My Take. "And hopefully those negotiations can pick back up in November once the playoffs are done. We'll see where that goes. Hopefully they're involved with everything. I would love to return."
Meanwhile, he also lamented the fact that the Tigers weren't able to live up to their expectations of competing for the World Series.
"This wasn't the way the season was supposed to go. Going into the offseason, [with] the people that we acquired through free agency and who we signed, I'm like, 'This is the World Series team,'" Skubal said. "This is the team that I'm gonna go and win a World Series and beat anybody. It doesn't matter what's going on."

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Christian Yelich Speaks As Brewers Capture 1st World Series Title
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are finally World Series champions. It took a long time for the Brewers to get to this point and there was plenty of heartbreak along the way. But the journey has finally reached the top of the mountain. No one can take away what the 2026 Brewers just did. item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers are finally World Series champions.
It took a long time for the Brewers to get to this point and there was plenty of heartbreak along the way. But the journey has finally reached the top of the mountain. No one can take away what the 2026 Brewers just did. Milwaukee entered the 2026 World Series as one of just a few teams who hadn't ever won a title before. That is no longer the case. From here on out, the Brewers will always have a title under their belt. The 2026 team will forever be in the record books. How can you not get romantic about baseball? Think of captain Christian Yelich, for example. When Yelich got to town, the Brewers weren't the contender they are now. Before Yelich arrived, the Brewers had made the playoffs just twice since the club made it all the way to the World Series in 1982 (2008 and 2011).
Yelich was the missing piece and he spoke after Milwaukee finally was able to get over the hump on Wednesday night.
"I don't even know how to describe it," Yelich said. "It's the best feeling ever. All of our fans are here [and] I know the city has waited a long, long time for this. We're so happy to bring it home to them. I can't wait to get back there and celebrate. Man, I wish everyone could experience what this feels like. It feels amazing. I'm so proud of this group of guys."
Christian Yelich Was The Missing Piece
That's not all, though. He shared a message specifically for the fans.
"We're coming home, baby," Yelich continued. "We can't wait to see you. Can't wait to celebrate. Your support has been everything to us this year. You were incredibly loud in the playoffs. I mean, it was almost a home game here for us in a World Series game, which was insane. We can't wait to get back there and celebrate and enjoy this, baby."
Since Yelich joined the Brewers' organization, things have changed. Again, the Brewers had made the playoffs just two times, dating all the way back to 1982. With Yelich in the organization, Milwaukee has made it to the playoffs in eight of nine seasons and now, has a World Series title under its belt. Yelich came to town and helped to change the culture. Of course, he's not the only guy who has had success in the organization. Him and Brandon Woodruff have been together throughout this entire run. The golden age of the Brewers starts and ends with these two.
On top of Yelich's play on the field, he is the leader in the clubhouse. He's the captain for a reason and that goes far beyond just his play. This is a guy who just simply gets it. While speaking after Milwaukee won the World Series, Yelich made sure to talk about and show love to the longtime voice of the franchise, Bob Uecker. Yelich is a class act, an incredible baseball player, a leader and now, finally, a champion.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Cam Schlittler Named AL Outstanding Pitcher by His Fellow MLB Players
item.dc:creator: Chris Trant
item.description: The New York Yankees put together a strong regular season during the 2026 MLB season, finishing 93-68 and earning the top American League Wild Card spot before sweeping the Boston Red Sox in the opening round of the postseason. However, their postseason run came to a screeching halt in the ALDS against the Tampa Bay Rays. The Yankees were swept by the Rays, who would eventually go on to win the American League Pennant. While New York's season ended in disappointment, one of the biggest positives
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees put together a strong regular season during the 2026 MLB season, finishing 93-68 and earning the top American League Wild Card spot before sweeping the Boston Red Sox in the opening round of the postseason.
However, their postseason run came to a screeching halt in the ALDS against the Tampa Bay Rays. The Yankees were swept by the Rays, who would eventually go on to win the American League Pennant. While New York's season ended in disappointment, one of the biggest positives from the year was the emergence of right-hander Cam Schlittler in his second MLB season.
Schlittler started 33 games for the Yankees this season, going 14-6 and posting an American League-leading 1.95 ERA, with 239 strikeouts and a 0.92 WHIP over 193.2 innings. Schlittler was one of the most dominant pitchers in the American League this season and is a heavy favorite to win the AL Cy Young Award for 2026.
While Schlittler will have to wait until Nov. 11 for the Cy Young voting results, the Yankees announced on Wednesday that the right-hander was named the 2026 Players Choice Awards AL Outstanding Pitcher.
Presented by the MLB Players Association, the award is voted on by active players across the league. Schlittler was among three finalists, including Dylan Cease of the Toronto Blue Jays and Sonny Gray of the Boston Red Sox.
After showing promise as a rookie in 2025, the 25-year-old made a significant leap in his second year and earned his first career All-Star selection.
Schlittler also carried his regular season success into the postseason, where he pitched 6⅓ scoreless innings, striking out 10 in Game 1 of the Wild Card series against the Red Sox.
With the Players Choice Award now added to his résumé, Schlittler has quickly become one of the most accomplished young pitchers in baseball.
Greatest Yankees of All-Time

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Blue Jays Learn Bo Bichette’s Likely MLB Future
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: The Toronto Blue Jays' first season after losing Bo Bichette in free agency to the New York Mets wasn't a good one. item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays' first season after losing Bo Bichette in free agency to the New York Mets wasn't a good one.
A year after Bichette helped the Blue Jays reach Game 7 of the World Series, this team missed the postseason entirely. Technically, they held onto mathematical hope until the final week of the season, but Toronto was sledding uphill for most of the season.
Bichette's season with the Mets didn't go much better. He took a big step back from his 2025 performance, and New York was even further out of the playoff picture than the Blue Jays.
It all sets up for a fascinating offseason, because Bichette's three-year, $126 million deal with the Mets actually has an opt-out built in after each season. If he wants to be a free agent again this offseason, Bichette can be.
That doesn't mean the Blue Jays would bring him back, but it does mean Bichette's next steps are still to be determined. He's not guaranteed to play with the Mets in 2027. He's got a decision to make.
And there's some new intel on what Bichette might do.
Bo Bichette Update
SNY's Chelsea Janes, a plugged-in MLB insider, put out a mailbag article on Wednesday in which she was asked what she thinks Bichette might do.
Janes' short answer was that she thinks Bichette will opt-in and stay on his current contract with the Mets. But she had plenty more to say and explain.
"My read – and it is truly just my read, because no one has said anything to me definitively – is that Bichette will opt in," Janes writes. "I say that for a few reasons, one of which is as simple as he did not look like a player saying his goodbyes when he left Washington on the last day of the season. Plus, that day, both Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor spoke like they expected to have him back more than simply hoped for it. But reading into things like that is risky and certainly is not enough to say anything for sure."
It also seems that even though Bichette and the Mets didn't have a good year, they liked their time together.
"The other evidence I have is that people around the Mets – so people who spend time around the team daily but are not necessarily in decision-making capacities to know first-hand – also seem fairly convinced Bichette will stay," Janes writes. "He has spoken glowingly of Andy Green. He seems to want to prove he can succeed in New York. And frankly, he isn't going to get anywhere near the average annual value on another deal they gave him on this one. He seemed to settle into the clubhouse down the stretch, much like everyone did. So read into that what you will."
That line about the money that Janes throws in there is probably the most relevant piece here, too.
Bo Bichette Salary
If Bichette stays on his current deal, he'd make $42 million in the 2027 season.
Opting-out does include a $5 million buyout (which accounts for two season and $84 million remaining), so Bichette would still have to get about $40 million per year on a new free agent deal to make it financially logical to opt-out.
If he really didn't like the Mets, Bichette could still choose to leave and start anew elsewhere.
But a year after leaving the Blue Jays, it's currently looking unlikely that Bichette would leave his next team this quickly.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Blue Jays Learn Bo Bichette's Likely MLB Future appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Jacob Misiorowski's Age, Height Wow World Series Fans
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: Jacob Misiorowski is a tall, lanky, right-handed pitching ace for the Milwaukee Brewers with a baby face who loves Pokemon cards. His age and height are two of his most-searched characteristics every time he pitches, and he’s got his biggest stage yet in the 2026 World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays. Misiorowski made his Fall Classic debut in Game 1 in Milwaukee, a game the Brewers won 3-2. He wasn’t at his absolute best, but his fastball did sit in the triple digits, and “The Miz” limited da
item.content:encoded:
Jacob Misiorowski is a tall, lanky, right-handed pitching ace for the Milwaukee Brewers with a baby face who loves Pokemon cards.
His age and height are two of his most-searched characteristics every time he pitches, and he’s got his biggest stage yet in the 2026 World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Misiorowski made his Fall Classic debut in Game 1 in Milwaukee, a game the Brewers won 3-2.
He wasn’t at his absolute best, but his fastball did sit in the triple digits, and “The Miz” limited damage.
He threw 5.0 innings in that game, allowing four hits and one run while walking one. Misiorowski struck out three and threw 78 pitches, 56 of them for strikes.
He’ll get his next chance on the World Series mound in Game 5 on Wednesday night in Tampa Bay at Tropicana Field. The Brewers now hold a 3-1 series lead and can close it out.
If Misiorowski is at or near his best, Milwaukee will have a great chance of celebrating a World Series title on Wednesday.
And with him on the mound again, we’ve got some of those key answers for you here.
How Old is Jacob Misiorowski?
Jacob Misiorowski is 24 years old.
He was born on April 3, 2002.
Yep, he’s definitely got a baby face. And yeah, he loves his Pokemon cards, which appear to be what he’s checking out in the picture above.
But Misiorowski isn’t overly young. He’s just starting to come into his prime.
How Tall is Jacob Misiorowski?
Jacob Misiorowski is officially listed at 6-foot-7 and 201-pounds.
He definitely looks super lanky and has some long levers out there on the mound.
At 6-foot-7, he’s the second-tallest pitcher on the Brewers, behind just their closer Trevor Megill — who is 6-8 and 253 pounds.
Jacob Misiorowski College
The other most interesting biographical feature of Misiorowski is that he was a second-round pick out of little-known Crowder College.
That’s a community college in Missouri, and it’s where an even-skinnier Misiorowski ended up after high school.
By the time he was touching triple digits on the radar gun there, though, teams had noticed him.
The Brewers had to give him a signing bonus of more than $2 million to keep him from going to LSU, where he would’ve been in the same pitching rotation as Paul Skenes.

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Andy Pettitte's Yankees role debunks narrative of Jorge Posada, Core Four being shut out
item.dc:creator: Pat Ragazzo
item.description: Former New York Yankees World Series champion catcher Jorge Posada made headlines on Tuesday after his appearance on The New York Post's "The Show" podcast went live. When asked if he would ever consider helping the team, Posada claimed that the Yankees don't make him feel welcome and that they don't want him around. There has been plenty of criticism drawn from ex-Yankees players following the team's exit in the ALDS round this year. Former ace and World Series champion CC Sabathia even went as
item.content:encoded:
Former New York Yankees World Series champion catcher Jorge Posada made headlines on Tuesday after his appearance on The New York Post's "The Show" podcast went live. When asked if he would ever consider helping the team, Posada claimed that the Yankees don't make him feel welcome and that they don't want him around.
There has been plenty of criticism drawn from ex-Yankees players following the team's exit in the ALDS round this year. Former ace and World Series champion CC Sabathia even went as far as to say the Yankees no longer set the standard of winning because they don't have their franchise legends around the club anymore.
All of that being said, the narrative that the "Core Four" is being completely shut out by the Yankees isn't accurate. And the proof of this stems from former starter and five-time World Series champion Andy Pettitte's role with the organization.
Pettitte's role with the Yankees debunks recent claims from ex-players
Pettitte, who pitched for the Yankees from 1995-2003, 2007-2010 and 2012-2013, rejoined the Yankees as an advisor coach in July of 2023. He now officially serves as a special assistant to Yankees GM Brian Cashman.
As reported by Brendan Kuty of The Athletic in late September, Pettitte is also a mentor to Yankees ace and AL Cy Young front-runner Cam Schlittler. The two remain in close and constant contact throughout the season, and Pettitte attends some Yankee games, where he will give advice during Schlittler's starts.
Schlittler isn't the only Yankees pitcher that Pettitte lends advice to when he is around the team. When Pettitte isn't at his home in Texas, he will often be at Yankee Stadium having conversations with the club's pitchers and pitching coaches around the bullpen, dugout and clubhouse.
Pettitte was also seen throwing batting practice to the Yankees before Game 1 of the AL Wild Card series against the AL East rival Boston Red Sox last month. So, it's safe to say that at least one member of the "Core Four" is involved and around the Yankees in Pettitte.
While Pettitte has a specified role with the Yankees, that doesn't mean the organization can't lean on more of their former players like they used to do in the past. Pettitte clearly brings a positive presence to the team and organization. Why not do more of that? But to say they don't have any former players around the team anymore would be inaccurate.

item.title: [New York Daily News] Key dates & storylines as Mets approach offseason
item.dc:creator: Abbey Mastracco
item.description: When the World Series concludes, the Mets can start to get a move on in their offseason. In what is expected to be a turbulent winter, the Mets don’t have an immense amount of business to take care of before the expected lockout on Dec. 1. They traded away the veterans who were on expiring contracts at the deadline over the summer and installed a manager, Andy Green, before the end of the regular season. item.content:encoded:
When the World Series concludes, the Mets can start to get a move on in their offseason.
In what is expected to be a turbulent winter, the Mets don’t have an immense amount of business to take care of before the expected lockout on Dec. 1. They traded away the veterans who were on expiring contracts at the deadline over the summer and installed a manager, Andy Green, before the end of the regular season. The club is looking to make some minor changes to the coaching staff after firing hitting coach Jeff Albert, and in the front office, where the team is seeking a farm director to replace Green.
Here are key dates and storylines to watch for as the offseason approaches.
DAY AFTER THE WORLD SERIES: FREE AGENCY
After the commissioner’s trophy is awarded, a five-day “quiet period” begins where pending free agents can negotiate with their current teams. Bo Bichette is the only potential free agent for the Mets. The third baseman has a player option for 2027 and one for 2028, and will have five days from the conclusion of the World Series to make a decision.
Late in the season, Bichette sounded as though he was leaning toward staying in Queens, but nothing is final.
It was an uncharacteristic season for the infielder. He played third base for the first time, though he was moved back to his natural shortstop position for a few months while Francisco Lindor was on the injured list. He hit just .260, though he matched his 2025 home run total with 18.
Bichette, 28, often lamented his inability to come through for the team in the first half, saying if he had, the Mets might have been in a better position. A good teammate with a strong work ethic, the Mets want him back. With the lockout looming, it might benefit him to take the option for next season instead of trying to feel out free agency for the second year in a row.
Free agents can negotiate with other teams after the quiet period ends. The biggest name on the market is Los Angeles Dodgers ace and two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal. The Mets, in need of starting pitching, should do what they can to sign the lefty.
NOV. 10-12: GENERAL MANAGER MEETINGS
The GM Meetings used to be a quiet affair. Rule changes were discussed at resorts around various Southwestern cities. It’s where executives used to lay the framework for roster building, discussing things in broad terms and doing initial check-ins on items they would later circle back to at the Winter Meetings.
That isn’t the case this season. The meetings have moved to Las Vegas for the foreseeable future, a city that is anything but quiet, and they now precede the MLB Awards Show, a full-blown red-carpet affair. The Winter Meetings will be canceled if the league locks out the players, so teams are expected to meet with players in Las Vegas instead of waiting until December.
NOV. 17: DEADLINE TO ACCEPT QUALIFYING OFFERS
Eligible players have until 4 p.m. ET to accept or reject the qualifying offer.
NOV. 20: NON-TENDER DEADLINE
The final date for teams to offer a contract to all arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players on their 40-man roster for next season; this is where the Mets have some tough decisions to make. Their list of arbitration-eligible players is long: Mark Vientos, Brett Baty, Francisco Alvarez, Ronny Mauricio, Tylor Megill, Reed Garrett, Robert Stock and Austin Warren.
Vientos, Baty, Alvarez and Mauricio were once top prospects in the Mets’ system, but they aren’t prospects anymore.
Alvarez, a power-hitting catcher, was primarily the Mets’ full-time catcher until this season, when his defense was so poor the team had to use Luis Torrens as the main backstop. Injuries are also a concern for Alvarez, who has spent significant time on the injured list in each of the last three seasons. But he’s a well-liked, well-respected catcher, and it’s tough to let someone with his power go.
Though it’s clear the pop is still there, Vientos doesn’t have a full-time position, and he’s struggled as a platoon hitter over the last two seasons. The Mets converted Baty, a third baseman, to a super utility role this season, using him at first base and in the outfield in addition to second and third base. Though his outfield defense was particularly lacking, the Mets were happy with how he approached the season and the professionalism he showed in embracing a new challenge.
It’s tough to know what to do with Mauricio. The time he lost from his knee injury clearly stunted his development; he’s struggled to hit breaking balls at the big-league level, and he’s out of minor league options. But the switch-hitter can seriously impact the baseball and play multiple infield positions. Veteran infielders Lindor and Marcus Semien both spent time on the IL last season, and they aren’t getting any younger, so keeping him around next season might be beneficial.
DEC. 1: EXPIRATION OF THE CBA
For the second time in five years, the 30 club owners are expected to lock out their players. All activity involving players on 40-man rosters will halt. Players and teams cannot communicate until a new CBA is agreed upon and ratified.

item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays left it late, but they survived.
After falling behind in the 12th inning, Tampa’s relentless lineup clicked by hitting four straight singles following a leadoff error to scratch and claw their way to a 4-3 win to avoid a sweep.
The Rays are still alive, which is all that matters when facing elimination, but at what cost?
Tampa Bay used seven pitchers in Game 4, including assumed Game 5 starter Nick Martinez, leaving Kevin Cash with quite the puzzle to put together Wednesday night.
The Brewers, meanwhile, will be sending their ace, Jacob Misiorowski, to the bump.
Brewers vs. Rays prediction
With Tampa Bay’s pitching plans shrouded in mystery, we’ll instead focus on the star of the show Wednesday night.
The Rays did a decent job against Misiorowski in Game 1.
Tampa Bay struck out just three times in five innings against the MLB strikeout king, but the Rays still only managed to tag Misiorowski for one run in a 3-2 loss.
If you can’t do damage against Misiorowski when he has his B-stuff, what is to be expected if he has his A-stuff?
Misiorowski averaged nearly 13 strikeouts per nine innings in the 2026 campaign, and he struck out at least 10 batters in 10 of his 30 starts during the regular season.
There’s every chance he can bring those numbers to Game 5, as he will be given quite a long leash after the Brewers used eight pitchers Tuesday night.
The path is there for Misiorowski to do something historic.

Jackson Chourio is rightfully an odds-on favorite to be named World Series MVP, but Misiorowski has a real chance to close that gap if he goes out there and blows Tampa Bay away.
He’ll need to be sensational (and Chourio will need to have a rare quiet night), but Misiorowski has a real habit of doing remarkable things every time he steps out to the mound.
And if he does it in a clincher, it will be hard for the voters to ignore.

item.content:encoded:
Yordan Álvarez también registró hecho que no se veía desde 1970 al ganar el título de bateo con al menos 40 jonrones a su cuenta. Solo Aaron Judge y Miguel Cabrera han sido capaz de gestar esta hazaña.
Yordan Álvarez consolidó su 2026 ganando el título de bateo de la Liga Americana y se unió al pelotero venezolano José Altuve y Yuli Gurriel como los únicos peloteros de Houston Astros con esta distinción.
En medio de la jornada del 28 de octubre se logró conocer a través de un comunicado oficial de Houston Astros, el anuncio de la Asociación de Jugadores de Béisbol de Grandes Ligas (MLBPA) de los ganadores de los prestigiosos “Players Choice Awards” 2026, distinguiendo Yordan Álvarez, como el Regreso del Año de la Liga Americana y el Jugador Más Sobresaliente en la misma liga.
En este sentido, el antillano superó al lanzador de New York Yankees, Gerrit Cole, y al patrullero de Los Angeles Angels, Mike Trout, para adjudicarse el primer galardón mencionado. Asimismo, venció en la carrera a jugadores como Junior Caminero y Bobby Witt Jr., para llevarse la premiación como Jugador Más Sobresaliente.
Es importante resaltar que, los “Players Choice Awards” son elegidos directamente por los propios peloteros de la MLB.
El pelotero cubano se une a José Altuve y Yuli Gurriel dentro de la historia de Houston Astros
A sus 29 años y de acuerdo con el portal estadístico Baseball Reference, Yordan Álvarez cerró la temporada regular del 2026 con un promedio al bate de .316 con 179 imparables en 567 turnos al bate; además de ello conectó 42 cuadrangulares, remolcó 106 carreras al plato y anotó 105 carreras en un total de 158 juegos con su novena.
En consecuencia, el pelotero cubano se coronó campeón bate no solo en su liga, sino en todas las Grandes Ligas y se convirtió apenas en el tercer pelotero en la historia de Houston Astros en ganar un título de bateo, uniéndose a:
- Yuli Gurriel (2021)
- José Altuve (2014, 2016 y 2017)
Además de ello, lideró la Liga Americana en renglones como bases alcanzadas totales (341), boletos recibidos (109), boletos intencionales (33) y OPS (1.033).
Yordan Álvarez logró hecho que no se veía desde 1970
De igual forma, el poderoso toletero se erigió como el tercer jugador desde 1970 en conquistar el título de bateo de la Liga Americana conectando al menos 40 jonrones, uniéndose al jardinero de New York Yankees, Aaron Judge (2025) y al pelotero venezolano Miguel Cabrera (2012-2013).
Como punto a resaltar, Yordan Álvarez obtuvo tres distinciones de Jugador de la Semana de la Liga Americana, dos premios de Jugador del Mes y fue seleccionado a su cuarto Juego de Estrellas.
Luego de una zafra pasada colmada de lesiones, el resurgir del pelotero cubano fue notorio y por ende al contar con salud en su totalidad es capaz de desplegar todo su talento y poderío en el plato.

item.title: [NBC Sports Philadelphia] Zack Wheeler's remarkable return earns Players Choice Award from his peers
item.dc:creator: Cole Weintraub
item.description: Zack Wheeler's return to the mound was one of the Phillies' biggest success stories of 2026. Now, he's being recognized by the players who witnessed it firsthand. The Major League Baseball Players Association announced Wednesday that Wheeler was voted the National League Comeback Player of the Year as part of its annual Players Choice Awards. The 36-year-old right-hander received the honor after returning from venous thoracic outlet syndrome, which required surgery to remove a rib after doctors
item.content:encoded:
Zack Wheeler's return to the mound was one of the Phillies' biggest success stories of 2026. Now, he's being recognized by the players who witnessed it firsthand.
The Major League Baseball Players Association announced Wednesday that Wheeler was voted the National League Comeback Player of the Year as part of its annual Players Choice Awards.
The 36-year-old right-hander received the honor after returning from venous thoracic outlet syndrome, which required surgery to remove a rib after doctors discovered a blood clot near his right shoulder in August 2025.
Wheeler made his season debut April 25 and returned to form, posting a 14-5 record with a 3.00 ERA and 193 strikeouts across 162 innings in 28 starts.
In a video released by the MLBPA announcing the award, several pitchers around the league praised Wheeler's ability to overcome an injury that initially raised questions about his future.
"He's a special player. He's had a tremendous career," Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler said. "You see the injuries can be, you know, a setback and then rehab can be a tough process. I was very impressed."
Philadelphia Phillies
Find the latest Philadelphia Phillies news, highlights, analysis and more with NBC Sports Philadelphia.
Orioles pitcher Chris Bassitt recalled his initial reaction to Wheeler's diagnosis, believing the injury could potentially bring his career to an abrupt end.
"What I thought at the time was like he doesn't deserve to go out like this," Bassitt said. "He deserves to have a path where he can choose when he's done."
Wheeler also offered a glimpse into the uncertainty of his recovery, detailing the multiple procedures required to restore proper blood flow.
"This is one of these surgeries that, you know, just isn't really that common," Wheeler said. "So a lot of uncertainty around it. At the same time, you got to keep a positive mindset."
That mindset helped Wheeler return to the level of performance his peers had grown accustomed to seeing.
And for a pitcher who has spent more than a decade competing against some of baseball's best, the recognition carried particular significance.
"I always thought when we vote on these every year that this would be one of the cool awards to win," Wheeler said. "The ones that the players vote on is the guys that you're competing against, playing with, guys who know what it takes to be good day in and day out."
Wheeler could soon add another honor to his résumé.
He is also a leading candidate for MLB's separate NL Comeback Player of the Year Award, which will be announced Nov. 11. Unlike the Players Choice Awards, which are voted on by major league players, MLB's honor is determined by a vote of the 30 MLB.com club beat reporters.

item.content:encoded:
Tampa Bay Rays se negó a entregar la corona sin pelear hasta el último momento y encontró en el Juego 4 de la Serie Mundial una victoria que le permite mantenerse con vida. Con un triunfo de 4-3 sobre Milwaukee Brewers, la novena de Florida forzó un quinto encuentro y recuperó la esperanza de prolongar la batalla por el campeonato.
Tampa Bay Rays se niega a morir y convierte remontada épica en 12 entradas para vencer a Brewers
Al finalizar el emotivo encuentro, Jonathan Aranda habló sobre el carácter de su equipo y destacó que la confianza permanece intacta pese a la presión de disputar una serie en la que cada derrota puede resultar definitiva.
Jonathan Aranda destaca el espíritu de lucha de Tampa Bay
“Es parte del juego, nunca te tienes que rendir, hasta que no caiga el último out se define. Nos queda una vida todavía, este equipo está más motivado que nunca”, expresó Aranda.
El infielder mexicano también recordó que la novena ha demostrado capacidad para competir durante toda la temporada, por lo que confía en que esa misma mentalidad pueda marcar la diferencia en los encuentros restantes.
“Hay que seguir peleando, lo hemos venido haciendo todo el año, estamos en esta parte de la temporada, estamos nosotros aquí y bueno, ¿por qué no hacerlo una vez más?”, señaló.
“Nuestra confianza está hasta el tope”, advierte el mexicano
Aranda destacó que el ánimo dentro del vestidor se mantiene elevado y que el triunfo ante Milwaukee es una muestra de la energía con la que los Rays afrontan los momentos más complicados.
“Todos traemos la energía, traemos las ganas de hacer las cosas, de ganar, es lo que nos ha caracterizado a través del año y bueno, ahorita lo pudieron ver otra vez en el terreno”, comentó.
Finalmente, Jonathan Aranda resumió el sentimiento que domina a los Rays después de una victoria que les permitió evitar la eliminación y extender la lucha por el título. “Nuestra confianza está hasta el tope y así vamos a seguir”, sentenció el mexicano.

item.content:encoded:
今季終了後にカブスからフリーエージェント（FA）となる鈴木誠也外野手の去就が注目されている。米メディア『ジ・アスレチック』は26日（日本時間27日）、鈴木がカブスの想定を大きく上回る契約を手にする可能性を報道。チーム残留の難しさを指摘した。
■今季のQOは「2315万ドル」
『ジ・アスレチック』によると、今後カブスは鈴木に1年2315万ドル（約36億5千万円）のクオリファイングオファー（QO）を提示すると見られている。QOとはFAとなった選手に元所属球団が提示できる1年契約で、金額は今季年俸の上位125選手の平均と定められている。選手がQOを拒否して他球団と契約した場合、元所属球団には補償として条件に応じたドラフト指名権が与えられる。QOが拒否された元所属球団が、新たな複数年契約を提示することも可能だ。
鈴木は2022年からのメジャー5年間で、通算113本塁打を記録。今季は右翼手としての守備も評価を高め、ゴールドグラブ賞の最終候補にも入るなど、攻守で評価が急上昇している。
今オフのカブスは先発ローテーションの大幅な再編に加えて、捕手やブルペンも補強候補となっており課題が山積している。『ジ・アスレチック』は、人気銘柄の鈴木が「シカゴが快適に支払える金額を大きく超える契約を提示される」と分析。右の有力打者が少ないFA市場において、カブスが鈴木を引き留められない可能性が高まっていると見立てた。
同メディアは、現行の労使協定が12月1日（同2日）に失効するため、ロックアウト前の駆け込み需要でFA市場が一気に動く可能性もあると予想。鈴木の争奪戦は早期決着するのだろうか。

item.title: [Swing Completo] MLB: Yordan Álvarez conquista dos premios de la MLBPA tras brillar en la temporada 2026
item.dc:creator: Aylet Morales
item.description: El slugger cubano fue elegido Jugador Destacado y Jugador del Regreso de la Liga Americana, después de firmar una temporada de 42 jonrones y OPS de 1.033 con los Houston Astros. Yordan Álvarez ganó dos premios en los Players Choice Awards 2026, tras conectar 42 jonrones e impulsar 106 carreras con Houston. El cubano Yordan Alvarez volvió a situarse entre las grandes figuras de las Grandes Ligas al conquistar dos de los principales reconocimientos de los Players Choice Awards 2026. La Asociación
item.content:encoded:
El slugger cubano fue elegido Jugador Destacado y Jugador del Regreso de la Liga Americana, después de firmar una temporada de 42 jonrones y OPS de 1.033 con los Houston Astros.
Yordan Álvarez ganó dos premios en los Players Choice Awards 2026, tras conectar 42 jonrones e impulsar 106 carreras con Houston.
El cubano Yordan Alvarez volvió a situarse entre las grandes figuras de las Grandes Ligas al conquistar dos de los principales reconocimientos de los Players Choice Awards 2026. La Asociación de Jugadores de las Grandes Ligas (MLBPA) lo distinguió como Jugador Destacado y Jugador del Regreso de la Liga Americana, dos premios que destacan tanto su extraordinaria producción ofensiva como su capacidad para recuperarse de una campaña afectada por las lesiones.
La elección tiene un valor especial porque los ganadores son seleccionados mediante el voto de sus propios compañeros. Yordan Alvarez recibió el reconocimiento después de protagonizar una temporada en la que recuperó su mejor versión y volvió a demostrar por qué es uno de los bateadores zurdos más peligrosos del béisbol actual.
Since 1992, the Players Choice Awards have celebrated excellence across Major League Baseball, recognizing performance, leadership, perseverance, and impact on and off the field. The awards are especially meaningful to players, because they’re determined through a vote of their peers. Congratulations to the 2026 Players Choice Awards winners! https://t.co/f1YVWtFTdZ— MLBPA (@MLBPA)
October 28, 2026

¿Qué son los Players Choice Awards?
Los Players Choice Awards son unos premios organizados por la MLBPA desde 1992, con el objetivo de reconocer a los peloteros más destacados de cada temporada a partir de la votación de sus propios compañeros. A diferencia de otros galardones del béisbol, estos reconocimientos reflejan la valoración de quienes compiten directamente contra los candidatos y conocen de primera mano el nivel de exigencia de las Grandes Ligas.
Entre sus categorías figuran el Jugador del Año, los jugadores y lanzadores más destacados de cada liga, el Novato Destacado y el Jugador del Regreso, además de distinciones que reconocen el liderazgo, el compromiso social y las contribuciones al béisbol.
Yordan Alvarez firmó una temporada ofensiva de élite
El bateador designado de los Houston Astros terminó la campaña regular de 2026 con números que respaldan plenamente sus dos distinciones. De acuerdo con las estadísticas de Baseball-Reference, participó 158 encuentros y registró promedio de bateo de .316, porcentaje de embasado de .432 y slugging de .601, para un OPS de 1.033.
Su producción de poder también fue determinante. Conectó 42 cuadrangulares, impulsó 106 carreras y anotó otras 105, además de recibir 109 bases por bolas en 692 apariciones al plato.
El cubano encabezó las Grandes Ligas entre los bateadores calificados en promedio de bateo, porcentaje de embasado, slugging y OPS. En la Liga Americana terminó segundo en jonrones e impulsadas, mientras que sus 341 bases alcanzadas reflejaron el impacto de su ofensiva a lo largo de la temporada.
Estas cifras consolidaron una de las campañas más destacadas de su trayectoria en las Mayores. Su combinación de poder, capacidad para embasarse y producción de carreras lo convirtió en una pieza fundamental de la alineación de Houston.
De las lesiones al protagonismo: las razones del premio al regreso
Para comprender la dimensión del reconocimiento como Jugador del Regreso, resulta necesario mirar lo ocurrido en 2025. Durante aquella temporada, las lesiones limitaron a Yordan Alvarez a solamente 48 partidos, en los que bateó para .273, con seis jonrones y 27 carreras impulsadas.
La reducción de su participación representó un golpe importante para los Astros, que no pudieron contar regularmente con uno de sus principales referentes ofensivos. Las molestias físicas impidieron que el toletero mantuviera la continuidad necesaria para desarrollar una campaña a la altura de sus antecedentes.
En 2026, el panorama fue completamente diferente. El slugger cubano más acción en los terrenos y recuperó su capacidad para producir extrabases, conectar cuadrangulares y generar oportunidades de anotación.
El contraste entre ambas temporadas explica por qué sus compañeros lo eligieron en la categoría de regreso. No se trató únicamente de volver al terreno, sino de recuperar su protagonismo y alcanzar cifras que lo ubicaron entre los mejores bateadores de toda la MLB.
Pete Crow-Armstrong encabezó los premios de la Liga Nacional
Yordan Alvarez fue una de las grandes figuras de la ceremonia, superando en la categoría de Jugador Destacado de la Liga Americana a Junior Caminero y Bobby Witt Jr., y para el premio al Jugador del Regreso a Gerrit Cole y Mike Trout. Sin embargo, el principal reconocimiento individual de los Players Choice Awards 2026 correspondió a Pete Crow-Armstrong, jardinero de los Chicago Cubs.
El estadounidense fue elegido Jugador del Año de las Grandes Ligas y también Jugador Destacado de la Liga Nacional. Su producción de 45 jonrones y su capacidad para aportar tanto a la ofensiva como a la defensa fueron elementos importantes en una temporada sobresaliente.
La MLBPA anunció además los siguientes ganadores:
- Jugador Destacado de la Liga Americana: Yordan Álvarez, Houston Astros.
- Jugador Destacado de la Liga Nacional: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Chicago Cubs.
- Jugador del Año: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Chicago Cubs.
- Lanzador Destacado de la Liga Americana: Cam Schlittler, New York Yankees.
- Lanzador Destacado de la Liga Nacional: Jacob Misiorowski, Milwaukee Brewers.
- Novato Destacado de la Liga Americana: Kevin McGonigle, Detroit Tigers.
- Novato Destacado de la Liga Nacional: Sal Stewart, Cincinnati Reds.
- Jugador del Regreso de la Liga Americana: Yordan Álvarez, Houston Astros.
- Jugador del Regreso de la Liga Nacional: Zack Wheeler, Philadelphia Phillies.
- Marvin Miller Man of the Year: Chris Bassitt, Baltimore Orioles.
- Filántropo del Año: Jake Burger, Texas Rangers.
- Premio Curt Flood: David Cone.
¿Quién es Yordan Alvarez?
Yordan Alvarez nació el 27 de junio de 1997 en Las Tunas, Cuba. Batea a la zurda y se desempeña principalmente como bateador designado y jardinero izquierdo; debutó en las Grandes Ligas el 9 de junio de 2019 con los Houston Astros.
Desde su llegada a la MLB, ha destacado por su poder ofensivo y su capacidad para producir carreras. Fue una figura clave en la conquista de la Serie Mundial de 2022, temporada en la que también recibió el premio al Jugador Más Valioso de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Americana. Con sus reconocimientos de 2026, añadió otro capítulo importante a una trayectoria que lo mantiene entre los principales representantes cubanos del béisbol profesional.

Josh Inglis' expert pick: Jacob Misiorowski Under 15.5 outs
Price: 53¢ at Polymarket
I have this priced at 60%, and the odds are already dropping. The Tampa Bay Rays have seen Jacob Misiorowski once, and the 24-year-old might be running on fumes. He's thrown 13 1/3 postseason innings on top of 174 2/3 during the regular season after logging just 130 frames in 2025.
He's been laboring through his playoff starts and threw just 78 pitches in Game 1 of the World Series. He hasn't recorded more than 15 outs in any of his three postseason starts, and the familiarity edge now shifts toward Tampa.
Even with a good outing, I see five innings as his ceiling. At 53%, there's still value in backing the Under.
Joe Osborne's expert pick: Brewers moneyline
Price: 57¢ at Polymarket
The Milwaukee Brewers are 12-0 in Misiorowski’s last 12 starts and 23-4 since May 1.
Milwaukee also owns the bullpen edge this World Series: a 1.29 ERA compared to Tampa Bay’s 4.12, and another reliever-heavy night looms for the Rays after using six pitchers in Game 3 and seven in Game 4.
At the plate, Milwaukee’s .773 series OPS dwarfs Tampa’s atrocious .491.
With an elite starter, a stronger bullpen, and a more productive lineup, I’m backing the Brewers to finish the job tonight
Neil Parker's expert pick: William Contreras Over 1.5 hits + runs + RBI
Price: 51¢ at Polymarket
Even with a 0-for-5 night at the dish in Game 4, Milwaukee catcher William Contreras has gone 7-for-17 with a run and three RBI during the World Series.
He’s sporting a .454 wOBA for the postseason while hitting in the heart of the lineup, so I recommend this Over up to 55%. Contreras posted a nearly identical .760 OPS against left-handed pitchers and .756 OPS against righties during the regular season, too
Dustin Saracini's expert pick: Chandler Simpson Over 1.5 hits + runs + RBI

Chandler Simpson has been one of the Rays' most reliable bats throughout the World Series. He's recorded at least one hit in five of his last six postseason games, highlighted by a three-hit performance in Game 4.
He played a pivotal role in Tampa's two-run comeback in the 12th inning, continuing to deliver the goods for a team that's largely been counted out.

item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki could be in line for a massive payday this offseason, with at least one team already generating buzz as a potential landing spot.
Jim Bowden of The Athletic ranks Suzuki as the No. 6 overall free agent in his latest rankings and projects the 32-year-old outfielder to land a five-year, $120 million contract, averaging $24 million per season.
Suzuki is coming off the best season of his MLB career, batting .270 with 26 home runs, 86 RBIs and a .368 on-base percentage. He also posted a .473 slugging percentage, an .841 OPS and a 131 OPS+ while producing 5.1 WAR, according to Baseball-Reference.
While Suzuki has always been a productive offensive player, his improved defense in right field helped make 2026 his most complete season since arriving from Japan.
Rumors are growing that the Toronto Blue Jays will make Suzuki a priority this offseason as they look to strengthen their outfield and add lineup protection for superstar Vladimir Guerrero Jr.
Bowden lists Toronto and the Philadelphia Phillies as the two best potential landing spots for Suzuki.
The veteran outfielder has been one of Chicago's most consistent hitters since signing his original five-year, $85 million contract ahead of the 2022 season. Over his five seasons with the Cubs, Suzuki averaged more than 20 home runs per year and posted an OPS+ of at least 125 in each of the past four seasons.
His combination of offensive consistency, improved defense and experience makes him one of the more attractive position players available in free agency.
Bowden compared Suzuki's potential contract to several notable outfield deals, including Teoscar Hernández's three-year, $66 million agreement, Jung Hoo Lee's six-year, $113 million contract and Nick Castellanos' five-year, $100 million deal.
For the Cubs, Suzuki's projected price tag presents another difficult offseason decision.
Chicago already faces significant uncertainty in its outfield, with several players potentially departing through free agency. Losing Suzuki would create another hole in a lineup that ranked among baseball's most productive offenses in 2026.
At $24 million annually, bringing Suzuki back would require a big financial commitment from the Cubs, who also need to address their starting rotation and several other roster needs.

item.dc:creator: Mike Chiari

It's supposed to test you." Trailing by scores of 1-0 and 2-1, the Brewers twice battled back to tie things up in Game 4 th
item.content:encoded:
Outfielder and team captain Christian Yelich summed things up following the Milwaukee Brewers' heartbreaking, 4-3 loss in extra innings to the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday.
Speaking to reporters after the Brewers allowed a golden opportunity to close out the series to slip through their fingers, Yelich said, "This stuff is not supposed to be easy. It's supposed to test you."
Trailing by scores of 1-0 and 2-1, the Brewers twice battled back to tie things up in Game 4 thanks to an RBI double by Cooper Pratt and solo home run by David Hamilton.
That allowed Milwaukee to force extra innings, and after the teams failed to score in the 10th and 11th innings, Pratt smacked a solo homer in the top of the 12th to put the Brewers ahead 3-2.
Milwaukee entered the bottom of the 12th needing three outs to win the first World Series in franchise history, but things went awry from there.
After Junior Caminero began the inning by reaching first base on a throwing error by Joey Ortiz, Shane Drohan entered the game and allowed four consecutive singles.
An RBI single by Jonny DeLuca tied it, and a walk-off RBI single by Ben Williamson won it, thus giving the Rays new life.
The Brewers still have a huge advantage, up 3-2 with likely National League Cy Young Award winner Jacob Misiorowski set to take the mound in Game 5 on Wednesday, but it is fair to wonder if losing Game 4 in such dramatic fashion could potentially mess with the Brew Crew's psyche.

item.title: [PCMag] Milwaukee Brewers vs. Tampa Bay Rays Livestream: How to Watch The MLB World Series Game 5 for Free
item.dc:creator: Jason Cohen

item.content:encoded:
The MLB World Series is finally here after several weeks of intense playoff action. The Brewers swept the Dodgers to reach the World Series for the first time in 44 years. The Rays beat out the Guardians in six games to win the American League pennant for just the third time. Just like in this year's WNBA Finals, we're about to witness history: Whoever wins, this will be the franchise's first championship.
The Milwaukee Brewers are currently in the lead with three wins; they only need one more to win the entire World Series. But it's still anyone's game. Which team will come out on top? Here's how you can watch tonight's World Series game live, even for free.
What Time Is the Milwaukee Brewers vs. Tampa Bay Rays Game?
Game 5 of the World Series between the Rays and Brewers will take place on Wednesday, October 28, at 8:00 p.m. ET.
How to Watch the Milwaukee Brewers vs. Tampa Bay Rays?
This year, the World Series will be broadcast on Fox and the Fox One app. You can also watch it with a live TV or sports streaming subscription from DirecTV, Fubo, Hulu, Sling, Sportsnet+ (if you're in Canada), or YouTube TV.
How to Watch the Brewers vs. Rays for Free
If you don't want to subscribe to any of the above platforms, you may be able to sign up for a few free trials to gain access to the remaining games. Fox One and Hulu offer three-day trials, DirecTV and Fubo offer five days, and YouTube TV gives you 10 days for free.
2026 MLB World Series Game Schedule
MLB's expanded postseason means more teams on the playoff schedule. In the Wild Card round, the Braves beat the Phillies, the Padres beat the Cubs, the Yankees defeated the Red Sox, and the White Sox defeated the Astros. The winners advanced to the Division Series, where the Los Angeles Dodgers, Milwaukee Brewers, Tampa Bay Rays, and Cleveland Guardians beat their respective opponents.
For the Championship Series, the Brewers beat the Dodgers in four games to clinch the National League pennant. The Rays defeated the Guardians in six games to capture the American League pennant. Now, Milwaukee and Tampa Bay will face off in the best-of-seven World Series to begin on October 23. Who will get to raise the trophy?
World Series: Milwaukee Brewers vs. Tampa Bay Rays - MIL leads 3-1
- Game 5 on October 28 - Fox/Fox One*
- Game 6 on October 30 - Fox/Fox One*
- Game 7 on October 31 - Fox/Fox One*
*if necessary
How to Stream the 2026 MLB Playoffs
This year's MLB postseason is stretched across multiple networks and streaming services. All Wild Card Series games for the American League and National League were broadcast on NBC, NBCSN, and Peacock. ALDS and ALCS games were on TBS/TruTV and HBO Max, while NLDS and NLCS games were on Fox/FS1. For the World Series, all games will be broadcast on Fox and the Fox One streaming service.
- DirecTV: DirecTV's MySports base pack costs $45 per month for the first six months to see every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, and TBS/TruTV.
- Fox One: Fox's own streaming app lets you watch the NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox and FS1 for $20 per month.
- Fubo: Fubo's Sports plan costs $45.99 for the first month to watch the Wild Card Series, NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox, FS1, and NBC/NBCSN.
- HBO Max: If you pay for the $18.49-per-month HBO Max Standard, you'll be able to watch the ALDS and ALCS games on TBS/TruTV.
- Hulu: For $90 per month, you can watch every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, TBS, and TruTV.
- Peacock: Instead of a live TV service, you'd need to pay $10.99 per month for Peacock Premium to see the Wild Card Series games.
- Sling: The $60.99-per-month Sling Orange & Blue bundle will let you watch the ALDS and ALCS on TBS/TruTV and the NLDS and NLCS on FS1. Day Passes are also available for Sling Orange, allowing you to watch games on TBS for up to seven days.
- Sportsnet+ (Canada only): The $30-per-month Standard tier lets you watch every postseason game.
- YouTube TV: Though the standard plan for YouTube TV costs $83 per month, you can actually now pay for the cheaper $65 Sports package to see all games on Fox, FS1, NBC/NBCSN, and TBS/TruTV.
Can I Watch Postseason Games on MLB.TV?
Are you already an MLB.TV subscriber? You can watch the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series games through MLB's own streaming service—but there's a catch. To watch on MLB.TV, you'll first need to authenticate through a participating pay TV provider. It's such a sticking point that it makes the entire question moot. If you already have a TV provider, then you wouldn't need to use a streaming service. If you don't already have an MLB.TV subscription, don't pay for one now.
How can I listen to the 2026 postseason?
You can also listen to the games via ESPN Radio.
Which Teams Are In the Playoffs?
Since MLB expanded its postseason picture in 2022, a total of 12 teams make the playoffs each year. That includes six teams per league, including the three division winners and three Wild Card teams.
- American League Division Winners: Tampa Bay Rays (1), Cleveland Guardians (2), Houston Astros (3)
- American League Wild Card: New York Yankees (4), Boston Red Sox (5), Chicago White Sox (6)
- National League Division Winners: Milwaukee Brewers (1), Los Angeles Dodgers (2), Atlanta Braves (3)
- National League Wild Card: Chicago Cubs (4), Philadelphia Phillies (5), San Diego Padres (6)
Upgrade Your Streaming Experience
If you decide to watch the MLB postseason, there's still time to get a big-screen television for viewing this beautiful game. Pro tip: Turn on your TV's motion-smoothing option for the best picture while watching sports. Just remember to turn it off before watching other TV shows and movies to avoid the awful "soap opera" effect.
About Our Expert
As PCMag's editor of how to content, I have to cover a wide variety of topics and also make our stories accessible to everyday users. Considering my history as a technical writer, copywriter, and all-around freelancer covering baseball, comics, and more at various outlets, I am used to making myself into an expert.
I believe tech corporations are bad, but you might as well know how to use technology in everyday life. Want more how to content delivered right to your inbox? Sign up for the tips and tricks newsletter that I curate three times a week.
My job as how-to guru means I use just about every gadget under the sun, so I can figure out how everything works. I work from a Lenovo ThinkPad running Windows 11, but also have a very large Dell Inspiron 17 3000 and Apple silicon MacBook. I have a Google Pixel 6a for personal use and use a Galaxy Z Flip 4 for additional Samsung-related testing. For iOS coverage, an iPhone 13 mini works like a charm, though it's already becoming a little long in the tooth.
My desktop situation includes a dual monitor setup with a modest Acer monitor. I also use a Logitech vertical mouse (who can use these ThinkPad trackpads) and a Havit keyboard (my first mechanical keyboard; I love it but my wife hates it!). I'm a recent convert from wired headphones; I have Anker Soundcore Liberty Air wireless earbuds for personal use and have taken to the Sennheiser HD 450BT headphones for work.
Whenever I have a second to myself, I'm probably gaming on my Nintendo Switch 2, Steam Deck, or Xbox Series S. I also still have a bunch of classic consoles lying around as well.

item.dc:creator: Brady Farkas
item.description: In perhaps a precursor to the American League Cy Young Award voting, Toronto Blue Jays pitcher Dylan Cease was not named as the Most Outstanding American League Pitcher of the Year, falling in the voting to Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees. item.content:encoded:
In perhaps a precursor to the American League Cy Young Award voting, Toronto Blue Jays pitcher Dylan Cease was not named as the Most Outstanding American League Pitcher of the Year, falling in the voting to Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees.
The awards are voted on by the MLB Players Association.
Regardless of result, it was a great first season in Toronto for Cease, who signed a seven-year, $210 million deal last offseason.
The right-hander made 29 starts around two short injured list stints, going 11-6 with a 2.40 ERA. The Blue Jays had the fewest runs scored and fewest home runs in baseball this season, so Cease and the pitching staff were forced to carry the offense. And Cease certainly did his part.
He struck out 239 batters in just 169.0 innings, marking his sixth straight season of 200 strikeouts or more. He also led the American League in hits/9, strikeouts/9, and home runs/9.
An eight-year veteran of the Chicago White Sox, San Diego Padres and Blue Jays, he's 76-64 in his career with a 3.67 ERA.
He made the All-Star Game for the first time this season, earning the start for the American League, which was managed by Jays' skipper John Schneider.
He ended the year on the IL with shoulder inflammation but is expected to be healthy for spring training.
As for Cam Schlittler
The 25-year-old Massachusetts native made his major league debut in 2025 and has taken the league by storm ever since. Armed with a fastball in the upper-90s, he went 14-6 with a minuscule 1.95 ERA this season, also striking out 239 batters. In 193.2 innings, he had a WHIP of just 0.92. He was a major reason why the Yankees won the American League East and advanced to the American League Division Series, where they were beaten by the Tampa Bay Rays.
Elsewhere for the Blue Jays...
The Milwaukee Brewers currently lead the Rays 3-1 in the World Series with Game 5 set to come on Wednesday night.
If the Rays win, the series will shift back to Milwaukee for Game 6 on Friday, but if the Rays lose, the season is over.
Once the season ends, the pending free agents for the Blue Jays will officially exit the 40-man roster. The Blue Jays will then have five days to get their 40-man roster in compliance and free agency will begin.
However, it's unclear how active free agency will be in November as a result of the looming MLB lockout.

item.title: [CubsHQ] Pete Crow-Armstrong sweeps two major MLB Players Choice Awards
item.dc:creator: Tony Crumpton
item.description: Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong continues to add to his impressive awards after a historic 2026 season. The Major League Baseball Players Association announced Wednesday that Crow-Armstrong has won both the 2026 Players Choice Awards Player of the Year and National League Outstanding Player honors. Unlike awards voted on by baseball writers, the Players Choice Awards are determined exclusively by active MLB players, making the recognition even more meaningful for the 24-year-old
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong continues to add to his impressive awards after a historic 2026 season.
The Major League Baseball Players Association announced Wednesday that Crow-Armstrong has won both the 2026 Players Choice Awards Player of the Year and National League Outstanding Player honors.
Unlike awards voted on by baseball writers, the Players Choice Awards are determined exclusively by active MLB players, making the recognition even more meaningful for the 24-year-old Cubs star.
Crow-Armstrong put together one of the greatest individual seasons in franchise history, batting .280 with 45 home runs, 107 RBIs, 119 runs scored and 41 stolen bases. He also posted a .372 on-base percentage, .570 slugging percentage and .942 OPS while appearing in all 162 games.
His 45 home runs tied Philadelphia Phillies slugger Kyle Schwarber for the major league lead, while his 41 stolen bases made him just the seventh player in MLB history to record at least 40 home runs and 40 stolen bases in the same season. He also became the first Cubs player to accomplish the feat.
What makes Crow-Armstrong's season even more remarkable is his ability to impact games on both sides of the ball.
According to the MLBPA, Crow-Armstrong became the first player since Hall of Famer Cal Ripken Jr. in 1991 to finish among FanGraphs' top three players in both offensive and defensive value.
His combination of power, speed and elite defense in center field helped establish him as one of baseball's most complete players.
Crow-Armstrong was selected over fellow Player of the Year finalists Shohei Ohtani and Yordan Alvarez. He also beat out Ohtani and Schwarber for the NL Outstanding Player honor.
The latest recognition adds to an already impressive offseason for Crow-Armstrong, who has also received Player of the Year honors from Baseball America and Baseball Digest.

With the Rays down to their last three outs, Jonny DeLuca and Ben Williamson provided the heroics to alter the narrative after Tampa Bay had been stymied at every turn over the first three games by the Milwaukee Brewers.
