How to Stream the 2026 MLB Playoffs
This year's MLB postseason is stretched across multiple networks and streaming services. All Wild Card Series games for the American League and National League were broadcast on NBC, NBCSN, and Peacock. Additional rounds will be on other networks. ALDS and ALCS games are on TBS/TruTV and HBO Max, while NLDS and NLCS games are on Fox/FS1. For the World Series, all games will be broadcast on Fox and the Fox One streaming service.
- DirecTV: DirecTV's MySports base pack costs $45 per month for the first six months to see every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, and TBS/TruTV.
- Fox One: Fox's own streaming app lets you watch the NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox and FS1 for $20 per month.
- Fubo: Fubo's Sports plan costs $45.99 for the first month to watch the Wild Card Series, NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox, FS1, and NBC/NBCSN.
- HBO Max: If you pay for the $18.49-per-month HBO Max Standard, you'll be able to watch the ALDS and ALCS games on TBS/TruTV.
- Hulu: For $90 per month, you can watch every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, TBS, and TruTV.
- Peacock: Instead of a live TV service, you'd need to pay $10.99 per month for Peacock Premium to see the Wild Card Series games.
- Sling: The $60.99-per-month Sling Orange & Blue bundle will let you watch the ALDS and ALCS on TBS/TruTV and the NLDS and NLCS on FS1. Day Passes are also available for Sling Orange, allowing you to watch games on TBS for up to seven days.
- Sportsnet+ (Canada only): The $30-per-month Standard tier lets you watch every postseason game.
- YouTube TV: Though the standard plan for YouTube TV costs $83 per month, you can actually now pay for the cheaper $65 Sports package to see all games on Fox, FS1, NBC/NBCSN, and TBS/TruTV.
Can I Watch Postseason Games on MLB.TV?
Are you already an MLB.TV subscriber? You can watch the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series games through MLB's own streaming service—but there's a catch. To watch on MLB.TV, you'll first need to authenticate through a participating pay TV provider. It's such a sticking point that it makes the entire question moot. If you already have a TV provider, then you wouldn't need to use a streaming service. If you don't already have an MLB.TV subscription, don't pay for one now.
How can I listen to the 2026 postseason?
You can also listen to the games via ESPN Radio.
Which Teams Are In the Playoffs?
Since MLB expanded its postseason picture in 2022, a total of 12 teams make the playoffs each year. That includes six teams per league, including the three division winners and three Wild Card teams.
- American League Division Winners: Tampa Bay Rays (1), Cleveland Guardians (2), Houston Astros (3)
- American League Wild Card: New York Yankees (4), Boston Red Sox (5), Chicago White Sox (6)
- National League Division Winners: Milwaukee Brewers (1), Los Angeles Dodgers (2), Atlanta Braves (3)
- National League Wild Card: Chicago Cubs (4), Philadelphia Phillies (5), San Diego Padres (6)
Upgrade Your Streaming Experience
If you decide to watch the MLB postseason, there's still time to get a big-screen television for viewing this beautiful game. Pro tip: Turn on your TV's motion-smoothing option for the best picture while watching sports. Just remember to turn it off before watching other TV shows and movies to avoid the awful "soap opera" effect.
About Our Expert
As PCMag's editor of how to content, I have to cover a wide variety of topics and also make our stories accessible to everyday users. Considering my history as a technical writer, copywriter, and all-around freelancer covering baseball, comics, and more at various outlets, I am used to making myself into an expert.
I believe tech corporations are bad, but you might as well know how to use technology in everyday life. Want more how to content delivered right to your inbox? Sign up for the tips and tricks newsletter that I curate three times a week.
My job as how-to guru means I use just about every gadget under the sun, so I can figure out how everything works. I work from a Lenovo ThinkPad running Windows 11, but also have a very large Dell Inspiron 17 3000 and Apple silicon MacBook. I have a Google Pixel 6a for personal use and use a Galaxy Z Flip 4 for additional Samsung-related testing. For iOS coverage, an iPhone 13 mini works like a charm, though it's already becoming a little long in the tooth.
My desktop situation includes a dual monitor setup with a modest Acer monitor. I also use a Logitech vertical mouse (who can use these ThinkPad trackpads) and a Havit keyboard (my first mechanical keyboard; I love it but my wife hates it!). I'm a recent convert from wired headphones; I have Anker Soundcore Liberty Air wireless earbuds for personal use and have taken to the Sennheiser HD 450BT headphones for work.
Whenever I have a second to myself, I'm probably gaming on my Nintendo Switch 2, Steam Deck, or Xbox Series S. I also still have a bunch of classic consoles lying around as well.

item.content:encoded:
Los Los Angeles Dodgers afrontan el Juego 4 de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional con la obligación de vencer a los Milwaukee Brewers para evitar la eliminación en los MLB Playoffs 2026. Tras caer en los tres primeros encuentros, la novena angelina regresa al Dodger Stadium sin margen de error, ante un rival que ha capitalizado su ventaja y está a un triunfo de conquistar el banderín de la Liga Nacional. Los Brewers buscarán cerrar la serie como visitantes, mientras que los Dodgers necesitan una actuación contundente para extender la eliminatoria y mantener sus aspiraciones de alcanzar la Serie Mundial.
En Estados Unidos, el cuarto partido se transmitirá por FS1 y FOX Deportes, con FOX One como alternativa para seguirlo por streaming. Los aficionados podrán elegir la señal en inglés o la cobertura en español para acompañar un encuentro que puede definir el futuro de los Dodgers en la postemporada. El primer lanzamiento está programado para las 8:00 p. m. ET (5:00 p. m. PT) de este jueves 15 de octubre.
En México, la transmisión de Dodgers vs. Brewers estará disponible a través de FOX Plus y FOX One. El encuentro comenzará a las 6:00 p. m., tiempo del centro de México, y los aficionados podrán seguir el desarrollo del Juego 4 por las señales y plataformas correspondientes a este mercado.
En el resto de Latinoamérica, los seguidores de las Grandes Ligas podrán ver el partido por ESPN 3 y Disney+ Premium. En Venezuela, la cobertura estará a cargo de Televen e IVC, mientras que MLB.TV ofrecerá una alternativa para los aficionados de otros países. Los horarios varían según el territorio: en Perú, Colombia, Ecuador y Panamá el encuentro comenzará a las 7:00 p. m.; en Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, Uruguay y Brasil, a las 9:00 p. m.; y en Bolivia, República Dominicana y Puerto Rico, a las 8:00 p. m.

item.content:encoded:
カブスとの５年契約が今季限りで満了となる鈴木誠也外野手（３２）に熱視線だ。安定した打撃に加え、守備力の向上でヤンキースのアーロン・ジャッジ外野手（３４）に代わる右翼のレギュラー候補として期待されている。
今季の鈴木は１４３試合の出場で打率２割７分、２６本塁打、８６打点、ＯＰＳ０・８４１の好成績。４年連続で２０発超えを果たしただけでなく、１４日（日本時間１５日）に発表されたゴールドグラブ賞の右翼手部門で初めて最終候補に選出された。以前は守備に対するチーム内の評価を得られず、ＤＨ専任となる時期もあったことを考えれば大躍進だ。
こうした攻守にわたる活躍があるからこそ他球団も放ってはおかない。米老舗誌「スポーツ・イラストレイテッド」の電子版「ＯＮ ＳＩ」は、ヤンキースの外野手の補強候補の一人として鈴木の名前を挙げた。しかもメジャー屈指の強打者・ジャッジの〝後釜〟という位置づけだ。
同誌は今季の鈴木を「彼のすべてが結実した年だった」と絶賛した上で「ケガに悩まされたシーズンを経て、ジャッジは今後、必然的に指名打者（ＤＨ）としての役割に限定されるだろう。２０２６年の鈴木がどれほど素晴らしい活躍を見せたかを考えれば、ヤンキースがこの日本人強打者を獲得できれば、ジャッジが去った後の外野陣は極めて充実した布陣となるだろう」と占った。
今季のジャッジは４月に右肋骨を疲労骨折。長期離脱を経て復帰したものの、９月に今度は右ふくらはぎの筋損傷で離脱した。そしてポストシーズンでは戦列に戻れないまま、チームは地区シリーズで敗退。ジャッジ自身にとって出場が６６試合にとどまったのは１年目の２０１６年、新型コロナの影響でシーズンが短縮された２０年を除いて最も少なく、来季はＤＨに転向すべきとの論調が強まっている。
ジャッジがＤＨで打撃に専念する代わりに右翼に空く穴を鈴木が埋めるという算段だ。その場合、「スペンサー・ジョーンズとコディ・ベリンジャーが中堅手と左翼手を務めることになる」とし「トレード期限直前に獲得した２選手（ルイス・ガルシアとエリオト・ラモス）と、ジアンカルロ・スタントンの全員を放出することになるだろう」と大胆な動きが必要との見方も示した。
年々進化を続ける鈴木の需要は高まるばかりとなりそうだ。

item.title: [si.com] Brewers Are Using Postseason Stage to Showcase MLB’s New Era
item.dc:creator: Tom Verducci
item.description: Los Angeles — When dynasties fall, it is not insurrection, nor jealousy, nor sloth that bring them down. It is the undefeated champion of the world, Father Time. We are watching the Los Angeles Dodgers age out. The Milwaukee Brewers proved for a third time in the National League Championship Series they are the better (and younger) team, completing a beautiful triptych of comebacks with a 6-2 win in Game 3 on Wednesday. In three successive games, the Dodgers had Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles — When dynasties fall, it is not insurrection, nor jealousy, nor sloth that bring them down. It is the undefeated champion of the world, Father Time. We are watching the Los Angeles Dodgers age out.
The Milwaukee Brewers proved for a third time in the National League Championship Series they are the better (and younger) team, completing a beautiful triptych of comebacks with a 6-2 win in Game 3 on Wednesday. In three successive games, the Dodgers had Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Blake Snell on the mound with a lead and lost all three. Ninety-five million dollars, four Cy Young awards and a World Series MVP worth of pitching and they could not hold back Milwaukee any more than you can hold back water with your hands.
But the most obvious reason why the Brewers have put the Dodger dynasty on the brink of extinction is this: the youngest pitching staff in baseball—and the hardest throwing staff in postseason history—has smothered the oldest team in baseball. Milwaukee is pushing around the aging Dodgers lineup with a barrage of fastballs in three versions, especially power sinkers. They are shoving 66.8% fastballs at the Dodgers at an average velocity of 97.9 mph. The Dodgers’ only path to victory is to slug and the Brewers simply won’t allow it.
“I just think they’re really good pitchers,” Dodgers infielder Miguel Rojas said. “A lot of their pitchers throw three different fastballs. They throw hard, and they’ve been locating the ball really well. They haven’t really given us too much of an opportunity to kind of build momentum.
“They’ve been attacking the zone. They throw their stuff in the zone—and with all three fastballs. A lot of guys have a cutter, a sinker and a four-seam fastball. It’s really hard to put barrels on the ball.
“At the end of the day, it’s just the velocity of their stuff. They throw the ball really hard. And we all know when you throw that hard, it’s really hard.”
The Brewers knew coming into the series that in today’s game older players don’t hit elite fastballs as well as younger players, and so the matchup was to their liking. But this? Who could have seen this in the NLCS? The Dodgers:
- Have two extra-base hits in 105 plate appearances
- Have been outhomered, 5-0
- Are the first team in franchise history to lose three straight games in one postseason with no home runs and no attempted stolen bases
- Are hitting .228 against fastballs
- Are 2-for-16 with runners in scoring position, part of a 3-for-32 postseason disaster in those spots
This has been the year in which baseball made a sharp turn when it comes to the speed of the game. Younger players thrive. Velocity, and the widespread adoption of the family of three fastballs, changed everything. You need fast-twitch athleticism, youthfulness. You need this generation of players who know velocity as a first language. You need rangy players on defense. The numbers bear out that younger players are the preferred way to go.
Players 30 and younger this year hit .247. Players in the 31-35 year-old demographic hit 10 points worse, .237, their worst showing ever. There was a time when front offices valued those 31-35 players because it seemed to be the peak intersection of experience and physical tools. Front offices were afraid to commit to younger players because of the lack of reps and track records. Those days are over.
The difference on the field in NLCS Game 3 was striking. The Brewers are the fastest team in baseball, as measured by sprint speed. The Dodgers are 24th.
The Brewers started a lineup and a pitcher with an average age of 26.1. They became the first team in history with a second postseason game starting three players 22 and younger: leftfielder Jackson Chourio, shortstop Cooper Pratt and rightfielder Luis Lara. Chourio opened the game with a first-pitch homer. Pratt smacked three hits, stole a base and scored a run. Lara flew around rightfield like a bird of prey, snaring anything that dared enter his airspace.
Watching Chourio, 22, Garrett Mitchell, 28, and Lara, 21, patrol the outfield was like watching an Olympic sprint relay team.
On the other side of the field, the Dodgers, especially their bats, looked old and slow. The average age of their starting 10 was 32.3 years old—more than six years older than Milwaukee’s fearless group. Only two starting Dodgers were in their 20s: centerfielder Andy Pages, 25, and Kyle Tucker, 29, who with his diminished range and baserunning has been trending older than his age.
By starting eight players 31 and older, these Dodgers joined the 2023 Dodgers, who got bounced by the Diamondbacks, as the only teams in the past 19 postseasons to trot out so many starting players that old in a game.
Fittingly, the old team played an outdated style of baseball, one from a generation ago. The ninth-place hitter, Tommy Edman, twice batted after the leadoff runner reached first base. Twice manager Dave Roberts did not ask him to bunt.
“I thought about it, but it’s just, he had a good pitch to hit. Flew out,” Roberts said. “I just didn’t feel giving up an out right there. Early in the game, I wanted Tommy to hit ...
“We haven’t been getting hits with runners in scoring position. To give up an out, to bank on getting a hit with runners in scoring position, I’d rather just try to maybe slug, hit a double.”
Edman was a below average hitter (97 OPS+) with a .385 slug this season.
Roberts and the Dodgers keep waiting for slug to show up at the expense of forfeiting the situational baseball as deployed by the other three remaining teams, the youthful Brewers, Guardians and Rays. The Dodgers still may be waiting Thanksgiving morning.
For instance, the Dodgers were down 1-0 in the sixth when Roberts sent 36-year-old Max Muncy to hit for Pages with runners on first and second and no outs. In that situation, the Brewers are bunting. Milwaukee plays get-em-over, get-em-in ball. The Dodgers? No way. Muncy is a three-true outcome guy. He is not going to bunt. Again, the Dodgers played for slug and got nothing. Muncy struck out. Will Smith, 31, did save the rally with a two-run double. But the Dodgers would go 1-for-12 after that against hard-throwing relievers D.L. Hall and Trevor Megill.
The lineup remained cold. Shohei Ohtani, 32, cannot pull a baseball because of lower-half injuries that won’t allow him to properly turn his hips and get to a firm front side. Freeman, 37, has three extra-base hits since Aug. 31.
“[Our] pitching staff has been great, to be honest,” Rojas said. “It’s really hard to put it into context when you have to pitch and have to play defense with a one run lead every single time. It’s like asking these guys to just throw a perfect inning every single time. It’s not sustainable. So, the blame is on the offense. We all know we could’ve done better, but nothing we can do now.”
How in the world has Milwaukee made Los Angeles look so bad?
“It’s pretty simple,” Muncy said. “We’ve played like [poop]. They’ve played great.”
Occam’s razor (or commode) aside, the one-sided NLCS is bigger than that. It stands as a changing of the guard, recalling the 1964 World Series, when the St. Louis Cardinals, emblematic of the National League embracing Black and Latin American players, ended the dynasty of an aging New York Yankees team, then the second oldest team in baseball. The younger, faster, harder-throwing, more creative team has been, beyond doubt, the better team.
Tom Verducci is a senior writer for Sports Illustrated who has covered Major League Baseball since 1981. He also serves as an analyst for FOX Sports and the MLB Network; is a New York Times best-selling author; and cohosts The Book of Joe podcast with Joe Maddon. A five-time Emmy Award winner across three categories (studio analyst, reporter, short form writing) and nominated in a fourth (game analyst), he is a three-time National Sportswriter of the Year winner, two-time National Magazine Award finalist, and a Penn State Distinguished Alumnus Award recipient. Verducci is a member of the National Sports Media Hall of Fame, Baseball Writers Association of America (including past New York chapter chairman) and a Baseball Hall of Fame voter since 1993. He also is the only writer to be a game analyst for World Series telecasts. He lives in New Jersey with his wife, with whom he has two children.

item.content:encoded:
Alejandro Kirk gave the Toronto Blue Jays a rare bright spot on an offense that struggled all season.
The catcher hit .278 with a .351 on-base percentage and a .415 slugging percentage. Kirk hit 10 home runs, drove in 43 runs and scored 26 times in 79 games. He collected 77 hits, including eight doubles and drew 33 walks against 38 strikeouts.
Injuries limited Kirk to 79 of Toronto’s 162 games. After a long season, Kirk is spending the offseason with his family.
He reposted photos from a Disney World trip on his Instagram story. The trip included his wife, Sofia Castañeda and their daughter, Emilia. The couple welcomed their daughter on Feb. 28, 2023.
Amid that news, what made headlines was trade chatter surrounding him.
Alejandro Kirk Labelled as a Trade Chip
Trade talk about Kirk surfaced Oct. 11. The Blue Bird Territory podcast posted a clip that day on X. The show features The Athletic’s Mitch Bannon, former Blue Jays outfielder Kevin Pillar and former pitcher Ricky Romero.
The post called Kirk “one of Toronto’s most VALUABLE trade chips.” In the clip, Pillar wondered about Kirk’s market value after injuries cost him much of the season. The clip spread online and some fans took it as a trade pitch.
Should Alejandro Kirk Be Traded?
The short answer is absolutely not. Bannon backed that view on X the same day. He wrote that he, Pillar and Romero all agreed Toronto should keep Kirk.
“This clip has gained some misguided traction, so to be clear, Kevin, Ricky and I all agreed the Jays shouldn’t trade Kirk,” he said. “We were more discussing why there’s been trade talk about him. In fact, I said he’s the exact mold of hitter the Jays covet, not a potential trade guy.”
The case against a trade starts with the contract. Toronto signed Kirk to a five-year, $58 million extension in March 2025. The deal covers 2026 through 2030 and averages $11.6 million per year.
Kirk also produces. His 114 wRC+ in 2026 topped his career mark of 111. He posted that mark despite missing more than two months. He walked in 10.5 percent of his plate appearances and struck out in 12.1 percent.
His defense adds to the case. In 2025, Kirk tied for third in MLB in fielding run value, with 21. He led all catchers in blocks above average and finished as a Gold Glove finalist.
Kirk also delivers in October. The two-time All-Star hit five home runs in the 2025 postseason. That ties the most by a catcher in one postseason. One was a go-ahead, three-run homer in World Series Game 3.
Toronto cannot afford to lose a productive bat. The Blue Jays’ offense was one of baseball’s worst this year. Trading a 27-year-old catcher on a long-term deal would deepen that problem.

item.content:encoded:
Get to Know Milwaukee Brewers Pitcher Jacob Misiorowski’s Fiancée
The Milwaukee Brewers are making a big postseason run, currently leading the Los Angeles Dodgers 3-0 in the National League Championship Series. If they win on October 15, they’ll head to the World Series for the first time since 1982.
The 24-year-old professional baseball team has a lot of players contributing to their success this season, including pitcher Jacob Misiorowski. This is just Jacob’s second season in the MLB and he’s having quite an incredible run.
Off the field, Jacob got engaged during his time off between the 2025 and 2026 baseball seasons. While he is mostly private about his relationship, we gathered everything we know so far. Scroll down for more.
Who is Jacob Misiorowski’s fiancée?
Since Jacob and Elle are so private about their relationship, very little is known about her. In a July 2026 interview, Jacob revealed that Elle played softball in high school and had an impressive arm.
“Jacob Misiorowski and his fiancé, Elle, might be the hardest throwing couple in baseball,” the reporter wrote on X. “He told me she was hitting the low 70s while playing softball as a catcher when they were in high school. Talk about a power couple!”
View this post on Instagram
Jacob follows one Elle on Instagram, Elle Nicas, but her profile is private. She became a fifth grade teacher at Matthews Elementary School in Grain Valley, Missouri, where Jacob is from, in July 2024.
Her employment was announced on the school’s Instagram with the following caption: “Ms. Nicas is excited to build relationships with students and to help them learn and grow. She is also excited to develop her skills and become the best teacher possible for her students. Ms. Nicas loves working in education because she loves seeing students grow throughout the year and creating activities tailored to her student’s interests.”
The pro athlete announced his engagement to Elle on January 12 with an Instagram post of her left hand showing off the engagement ring. He captioned it with a red heart emoji.
Of his proposal, Jacob told WISN it was “nothing too crazy” and that he “just asked the question.”
How did Jacob Misiorowski meet his fiancée?
Jacob and Elle seemingly met in high school. He attended Grain Valley High School in Missouri, and there was an Elle Nicas who played on the school’s softball team until she graduated in 2020. Jacob also graduated that year.
When is Jacob Misiorowski getting married?
When Jacob spoke to WISN in February 2026, he said his wedding to Elle was still “an offseason or two away,” which means he’ll likely get married in winter 2027 or winter 2028.

item.title: [Heavy.com] 2 Reasons for Bo Bichette to Reach Free Agency 1 Year After Blue Jays Departure
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: Bo Bichette was a free agent last offseason, and he used that opportunity to leave the Toronto Blue Jays and sign a three-year deal with the New York Mets. item.content:encoded:
Bo Bichette was a free agent last offseason, and he used that opportunity to leave the Toronto Blue Jays and sign a three-year deal with the New York Mets.
Despite that contract, though, Bichette could be a free agent again this offseason.
That deal signed by Bichette was technically for three years and $126 million, but it really functions as three one-year deals with options in between.
That’s because there is an opt-out built in between each season.
So Bichette just played the first season of his deal with the Mets for $42 million, but he doesn’t have to continue the deal if he doesn’t want to.
The Mets don’t have any power in the situation. It’s a player decision whether to opt-out or not.
In an MLB.com article on Thursday, Anthony DiComo broke down the two sides of the coin for Bichette’s decision.
And it certainly sounds like there are at least a few reasons that the former Blue Jays star could return right to free agency.
2 Reasons for Bo Bichette to Opt-Out
DiComo listed two reasons that he thinks Bichette could choose to opt-out of his contract after just one season.
“There are two primary reasons why Bichette might want to opt out of his deal,” DiComo writes. “One is lifestyle; if he wishes to move on from New York, Bichette could chalk his move from Toronto up to an error in judgment and simply tear it to pieces. Another is competitiveness; if he believes the Mets won’t be a playoff team in 2027, Bichette could look elsewhere.”
DiComo goes on to point out that Bichette hasn’t actually given off any concerns about the lifestyle — just that it can be a change for players who are in New York City for the first time.
Bichette got some big city life in Toronto, but nothing compares to the Big Apple.
The Mets’ competitiveness is another question altogether — they missed the playoffs by daylight in 2026 despite being immensely expensive. It’s fair to be uncertain about what the future might hold there.
The Money Question
Bichette left Toronto in part because of the money New York was offering.
Coming off a less-than-optimal season, Bichette has to decide where the money looks best now.
“Outside of lifestyle or competitive factors, Bichette’s only reason for tearing up his contract would be if he believes he can find significantly more money on the open market,” DiComo writes. “There’s some merit to that argument, with a significant caveat. If Bichette opts out, he will become arguably the best infielder available.”
Still, Bichette is due to get more than $80 million over the next two seasons — and if he does better in 2027, he can always opt-out next year.
Bichette likely wouldn’t return to the Blue Jays either way, but plenty of fans in Toronto are certainly curious about what he might do.

item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies were eliminated from the MLB playoffs by the Atlanta Braves in the National League Wild Card Series.
The Braves won Games 1 and 3, and the Phillies won Game 2.
The Braves have since been eliminated. Four teams remain in the playoffs. The Milwaukee Brewers have a 3-0 lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS, and the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays are tied 1-1 in the ALCS.
During the Championship Series, the Phillies announced news involving shortstop Trea Turner.
Philadelphia Phillies’ Dave Dombrowski Announces Trea Turner News After Early Playoff Exit
ATLANTA, GEORGIA – SEPTEMBER 30: Trea Turner #7 of the Philadelphia Phillies runs the bases during the first inning against the Atlanta Braves in game two of the National League Wild Card Series at Truist Park on September 30, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)
“He did not have a good year. He needs to fix things with his swing. He knows he has to be better at shortstop. I told him that is mandatory. I told him he cannot play shortstop like he did in 2026, going into 2027.”
Dave Dombrowski told him if he plays shortstop like he did in 2026, then he won’t be playing shortstop. Trea will be working with Carlos Mendoza.
Dave says Turner prefers the infield.
Sounds like Turner will be moved from shortstop if it is not going well in spring training
Trea Turner does not think he had a good season. He takes complete accountability. He is already working on his swing.
Turner flew back into town to speak with Dave Dombrowski for a few hours
Looking at Trea Turner
PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – SEPTEMBER 25: Trea Turner #7 of the Philadelphia Phillies reacts after a strikeout in the fourth inning during a game against the Tampa Bay Rays at Citizens Bank Park on September 25, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images)
Turner arguably had the worst season of his career in 2026.
The shortstop hit .242/.297/.378 with 19 home runs and 58 RBI over 157 games. He recorded -17 Defensive Runs Saved and -8 Outs Above Average over 1,343 1/3 innings at shortstop.
PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – SEPTEMBER 24: Trea Turner #7 of the Philadelphia Phillies looks on during a game against the Milwaukee Brewers at Citizens Bank Park on September 24, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images)
Turner signed an 11-year, $300 million contract with the Phillies in the 2022-23 offseason.
He accumulated 14.4 fWAR in his first three seasons with the Phillies. This year, he posted just 1.1 fWAR.
Turner began his career with the Washington Nationals in 2015.
The Nationals traded Turner to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the 2021 trade deadline. He played for Los Angeles through the 2022 season then signed his deal with Philadelphia.
Throughout his MLB career, Turner has posted 48.4 fWAR. He is a World Series Champion and a three-time All-Star.

item.dc:creator: Sportsnet Staff
item.description: After the worst statistical season of his MLB career, Trea Turner drew the ire of his general manager on Thursday. "He needs to fix things with his swing. He knows he has to be better at shortstop. I told him that is mandatory. I told him he cannot play shortstop like he did in 2026, going into 2027.” Turner, 33, posted a career-low minus-0.1 bWAR. He slashed .242/.297/.378 with 19 home runs and 58 RBIs. However, his defensive work was far worse. Turner graded out as a minus-nine by Statcast's f
item.content:encoded:
After the worst statistical season of his MLB career, Trea Turner drew the ire of his general manager on Thursday.
"He needs to fix things with his swing. He knows he has to be better at shortstop. I told him that is mandatory. I told him he cannot play shortstop like he did in 2026, going into 2027.”
Turner, 33, posted a career-low minus-0.1 bWAR. He slashed .242/.297/.378 with 19 home runs and 58 RBIs.
However, his defensive work was far worse. Turner graded out as a minus-nine by Statcast's fielding run value and tied for an MLB low with minus-17 defensive runs saved.
Dombrowski added that Turner will start the season at shortstop, but must play well defensively to continue at the position.
If not, the Phillies GM implied that changes will be made.
According to Dombrowski, Turner agreed that he had a bad season, took full accountability, and is already working on his swing.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Phillies get honest with Trea Turner about future at shortstop after bad 2026 season
item.dc:creator: Matt Sullivan

After a turnaround with Don Mattingly in charge, the Phillies ran out of gas, and nearly had an all-time collapse to miss the playoffs. But once they got there, they lost in three to the Atlanta Braves and were fa
item.content:encoded:
Phillies get honest with Trea Turner about future at shortstop after bad 2026 season originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Philadelphia Phillies' 2026 season was a disaster. They started horribly, firing Rob Thomson. After a turnaround with Don Mattingly in charge, the Phillies ran out of gas, and nearly had an all-time collapse to miss the playoffs.
But once they got there, they lost in three to the Atlanta Braves and were facing another long climb back to the postseason in 2027. However, Dave Dombrowski and the Phillies are not heading into next year so passively.
John Clark of NBC Sports Philadelphia shared that the Phillies and Dombrowski got honest with Trea Turner this offseason and told him that if he doesn't improve, the Phillies are going to take him off his shortstop position this upcoming season.
Phillies get brutally honest with Trea Turner, threaten to move him off SS position
"He did not have a good year," Dombrowski said of Turner. "He needs to fix things with his swing. He knows he has to be better at shortstop. I told him that is mandatory. I told him he cannot play shortstop like he did in 2026, going into 2027."
While that is quite the harsh quote from Dombrowski, will the Phillies actually do anything if Turner doesn't improve at shortstop this offseason?
Well, Clark shared that Dombrowski told Turner, "If he plays shortstop as he did in 2026, then he won't be playing shortstop."
If Turner were to continue to struggle defensively in the offseason and spring training, then the Phillies plan to move him to a new position next year.
That could mean Turner is playing second base with Bryson Stott manning third base, as he did after the Luis Arraez trade this past season.
He could also move to the outfield, but with Dombrowski revealing that Turner would prefer to stay in the infield, a move to second base, and Stott going to shortstop or third, would make sense.
Aidan Miller is getting close to making his MLB debut, so the Phillies could pencil him into the infield at either shortstop or third base, with Stott taking up the other spot and Turner manning shortstop with Bryce Harper back at first base.
Turner himself knows he didn't have a good season, and Clark shared that Turner "takes complete accountability" for his struggles and that he's "already working on his swing."
It's going to take more than just fixing his offense to stay at shortstop, however, as he'll need to play much better defense. With new infield coach Carlos Mendoza joining the club, the hope is that Turner can improve defensively and return to his 2025 form.
If he can do that, and also have a much better offensive season at the plate, the Phillies' lineup could be in a much better spot than it was last season, given how badly Turner struggled all year.
But Turner has an ultimatum. If he can't improve defensively, he'll be playing at a new position next year. The Phillies got honest with Turner and aren't going to be afraid of change this offseason.

item.content:encoded:
Trea Turner News: Staying at shortstop next season
Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski said Thursday that he plans to have Turner open next season at shortstop, Todd Zolecki of MLB.com reports.
Turner had a bounce-back season defensively in 2025, but he regressed in 2026 with a minus-10 Outs Above Average, per Statcast, which was the worst mark of his career. The Phillies don't plan to have Turner change positions, but Dombrowski noted Thursday that he told the player personally he'd have to play better defensively in order to remain at shortstop. Turner had a down year offensively, as well, slashing .242/.297/.378 in 157 regular-season contests.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees would be wasting Cody Bellinger at first base
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: Seventeen home runs aren't enough to make everyone happy with a $162.5 million contract. Cody Bellinger's glove deserves a much fairer hearing than his power total, though, especially when the Yankees start moving names around their 2027 lineup. I'd keep him in left field. Making Bellinger part of a first-base reshuffle might solve a daily playing-time headache, but it would also remove him from the position where he provided his clearest advantage this season. Bellinger gave the Yankees real va
item.content:encoded:
Seventeen home runs aren't enough to make everyone happy with a $162.5 million contract. Cody Bellinger's glove deserves a much fairer hearing than his power total, though, especially when the Yankees start moving names around their 2027 lineup.
I'd keep him in left field. Making Bellinger part of a first-base reshuffle might solve a daily playing-time headache, but it would also remove him from the position where he provided his clearest advantage this season.
Bellinger gave the Yankees real value in left
Wednesday's Gold Glove finalist announcement supplies a timely reminder. Bellinger led left fielders with 21 Defensive Runs Saved and finished with six Outs Above Average. Those measures use different methods and shouldn't be added together. Both, however, describe a useful defender rather than an expensive bat the club needs to hide.
The actual assignments matter. Bellinger started 112 games in left and logged 1,008 2/3 innings there. He made one start at first base. Moving him across the diamond would be a meaningful change to how the Yankees used him, not a harmless continuation of the same role.
New York can still want more offense. Bellinger hit .264/.338/.429 with 17 homers and 73 RBI in 132 games. A .767 OPS doesn't settle whether the five-year investment was wise, and a defensive award nomination certainly doesn't settle it either.
There isn't an obvious platoon problem to solve
His season wasn't built on one comfortable matchup. Bellinger had a .755 OPS against left-handed pitching and .775 against right-handers. Neither number makes him indispensable, but they don't suggest a player who needs to be pulled out of the lineup whenever the opposing starter throws with the wrong hand.
0What do you think?Post a comment.
Moving him would create another assignment
First-base flexibility has uses. On a day when Bellinger needs less running, or when another outfielder offers a clear matchup advantage, the occasional move can help. Committing him there for long stretches would be a different decision, because somebody else would have to handle those left-field innings.
I'd want the Yankees to compare the entire defensive arrangement before making that call. How much better is the new first baseman than the existing option? How much weaker does left field become? A more convenient lineup card can still produce a worse team if those costs are ignored.
There are limits to this argument. Defensive estimates vary, Bellinger's future health can't be assumed, and a genuinely superior outfield addition could change the calculation. The Yankees should remain open to those possibilities instead of treating one position as permanently reserved.
For now, the evidence favors leaving his main job alone. Bellinger can improve at the plate without the Yankees sacrificing what he already does well. Their offseason should be about adding strengths, not moving one of the existing ones to a position where it matters less.

item.title: [MLB.com] Rays-Guardians ALCS Game 3 FAQ, lineups (1 ET, TBS/HBO Max)
item.dc:creator: Tim Stebbins; Keegan Matheson; Adam Berry
item.description: CLEVELAND -- It’s a new day in the ALCS, as the Rays and Guardians have shifted their matchup back to Cleveland tied up at 1-1. The Rays' 3-1 win in Game 2 shifted this series back into focus after the Guardians pulled off a 7-3 come-from-behind win in the opener. We’ve seen each team’s best, and as these pitching staffs get stretched even thinner as the series wears on, they’ll need to lean on the identities they’ve built in 2026. “It’s going to be a challenging place to play,” said Rays manage
item.content:encoded:
CLEVELAND -- It’s a new day in the ALCS, as the Rays and Guardians have shifted their matchup back to Cleveland tied up at 1-1.
The Rays' 3-1 win in Game 2 shifted this series back into focus after the Guardians pulled off a 7-3 come-from-behind win in the opener. We’ve seen each team’s best, and as these pitching staffs get stretched even thinner as the series wears on, they’ll need to lean on the identities they’ve built in 2026.
“It’s going to be a challenging place to play,” said Rays manager Kevin Cash. “We played there not too long ago in the postseason. That's as good an atmosphere as you're going to see. They've got a great fan base that's going to be behind their team. I'd like to think we can carry our momentum into there and just play good baseball for Game 3.”
Step back a few feet for a wider view, and this Guardians team has still won four of its past five games. The club ran into a Game 2 buzzsaw named Freddy Peralta, whose fastball was nearly unhittable, but Cleveland is still in an excellent spot after stealing Game 1.
“We feel great. Obviously we would have loved to have taken [Game 2],” Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. “That would have been really big. And we had our position and our opportunities to do that. But going home 1-1, to go have three games in front of our fans in Cleveland, we feel really good about that. And we're excited to get it going.”
The pitching matchup has the potential to lean in the Guardians’ favor, too, with Gavin Williams starting on regular rest, fresh off a dominant outing against the White Sox to clinch the ALDS. For the Rays, Griffin Jax has been officially named the starter, and while he spent the majority of the season working in a true starter’s role, he pitched two innings of relief against the Yankees in Game 3 of the ALDS, throwing just 32 pitches.
This series is still waiting for its first show-stopping moment, too, with all eyes on José Ramírez for the Guardians and Junior Caminero for the Rays. Ramírez's series has been up-and-down so far, from a solid Game 1 to a crucial error that opened the door in Game 2, while Caminero is still searching for his first career postseason home run.
There’s history on the line here, too, for whichever team advances to represent the American League in the World Series. The Rays haven’t won the World Series since entering the league in 1998 and have only reached the big stage twice (2008, 2020). The Guardians, on the other hand, still carry the weight of the longest World Series drought in the big leagues at 77 seasons, stretching all the way back to 1948.
When is the game and how can I watch it?
First pitch for Game 3 of the Rays-Guardians American League Championship Series is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on Thursday at Progressive Field. Due to inclement weather in the forecast, the original start time of 6 p.m. was moved up. The game will be broadcast on TBS and HBO Max. 
Spanish-language game broadcasts will be available on UniMas for the ALCS, and Spanish-language radio broadcasts will be available on Univision’s TUDN Radio.
Who are the starting pitchers?
Rays: Griffin Jax, RHP
Key Stats: 0.90 ERA over his past five appearances
Nick Martinez started ALDS Game 3 for the Rays, but they will turn to Jax this time after using him as a reliever against the Yankees, with Martinez likely in line to pitch Game 4 on Friday. Jax has been excellent since a rough return from the injured list on Sept. 2 after a bout of right elbow discomfort, permitting only two runs on 10 hits and four walks while striking out 19 in 20 innings over his last four regular-season starts and his Game 3 relief outing at Yankee Stadium. Jax is presumably prepared for Cleveland’s inclement weather, having pitched for Minnesota for most of his career, and he’s put up impressive numbers (including a 2.19 ERA, 0.89 WHIP and 20 strikeouts) in 13 relief appearances at Progressive Field.
Guardians: Gavin Williams, RHP
Key Stats: 1.54 ERA, 24 strikeouts in 11 2/3 innings in ALDS
The Guardians officially named Williams their Game 3 starter on Wednesday afternoon, setting the 27-year-old up for a start on normal rest following his heroic performance in the ALDS, when he made two starts and an emergency relief appearance against the White Sox. After he recorded the final three outs of Game 4, Williams came back on one day’s rest in Game 5 and tied a franchise postseason record in strikeouts (12) to help Cleveland beat Chicago, 2-0, to advance. Williams starting Game 3 also positions him to start a potential Game 7 of this series on Tuesday, on normal rest.
What are the starting lineups?
Rays: With Williams on the mound, the Rays are going with their standard lineup against right-handers, with the “Big Three” followed by their other left-handed hitters. They're staying with Jonny DeLuca, who’s started every postseason game so far, over Cedric Mullins in center field.
Guardians: Patrick Bailey is back behind the plate in Game 3. He and Williams have been a customary battery this season, and Bailey is swinging a hot bat this postseason. The Guards are sticking with the standard lineup they’ve had in this series.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
Guardians: Vogt will have a full bullpen at his disposal after the off-day, and will work getting the ball to closer Cade Smith. He and Hunter Gaddis did not appear in Game 2, after both pitched in each of the Guardians’ first six contests this postseason. Setup man Erik Sabrowski also did not pitch in Game 2 and will be working off two days’ rest.
Rays: The Rays should be in good shape after Wednesday’s off-day, although this will be the first time since the regular season that they’ve played three consecutive days in a row. Left-hander Ian Seymour has clearly established himself as a top setup option in front of closer Bryan Baker, and lefty Cam Booser has also been tasked with getting big outs against left-handed hitters. Right-hander Kevin Kelly and Tyler Wells are also setup options in front of Baker, who has recorded the save in each of Tampa Bay’s four wins this postseason.
Any injuries of note?
Guardians: None.
Rays: Caminero and DeLuca said they were fine after a nasty collision while chasing a foul ball in Game 1. Left-hander Shane McClanahan, who finished the regular season on the injured list due to left forearm tightness, was shut down for the rest of the postseason, Cash said on Sunday. Otherwise, nothing new.
Who is hot and who is not?
Guardians: Shawn Armstrong has allowed just one hit and struck out five batters in 5 1/3 scoreless innings over four postseason appearances. It’s been an impressive comeback after he missed two months with a left calf strain, before returning the final week of the regular season. DeLauter is hitting .346 (9-for-26) with just one strikeout in seven postseason games.
Rocchio is hitting .091 (2-for-22) in seven games.
Rays: Pretty much everyone who touched the mound for Tampa Bay in the ALDS and Game 2 of this series performed well, which is certainly promising for the team moving forward, even after some shaky bullpen work in Game 1. The Rays are starting to find some rhythm at the plate, too, with Caminero leading the way despite not yet having the big moment everyone’s expecting. Hicks drove in a couple runs in Game 2, and DeLuca had his second straight multihit game. Díaz is just 5-for-21 in the playoffs, and Mesa is only 3-for-18.
Anything else fans might want to know?
• Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell will throw the ceremonial first pitch before Game 3.
• With his fifth-inning single in Game 2, Ramírez moved into second place in franchise history in postseason hits (49), breaking a tie with Kenny Lofton. Omar Vizquel (57) ranks first.
• Game 2 of the ALCS was Díaz’s 30th postseason game with the Rays, matching Evan Longoria for the most in franchise history. Game 3 should give Tampa Bay’s DH the club record.
• The Rays are 89-0 this year, including the regular season and postseason, when leading after eight innings. The last team to go a full year with a 1.000 winning percentage and at least 89 wins when leading after eight innings? The 2022 Mets, who went 90-0. The last team to do so in the AL was the 2002 Athletics (93-0).

item.content:encoded:
人気ランキング
コラム一覧
ポストシーズン リーグチャンピオンシップシリーズ
『MLB.com』は現地10月14日（日本時間15日）付で、同賞の最終候補に選出された選手を紹介する記事を掲載。鈴木について、「2025年から2026年にかけて、スズキほど守備を大きく向上させた選手はほとんどいない」と評価している。
同記事では「メジャーリーグでの最初の4シーズンはいずれもFRV（フィールディング・ラン・バリュー）はマイナスだったが、32歳のベテランは、今季は+8を記録した」と、守備指標の大幅な改善を紹介。
さらに、「スズキのDRS（守備防御点）は+14を数え、これは全右翼手の中で2番目に高い数字である」と、数字を挙げて最終候補入りの根拠を示した。
一方、ベンジについては、「23歳のベンジは、卓越した守備を武器に、ナ・リーグの新人王候補として一躍脚光を浴びた」と紹介。さらに、「彼は10補殺以上を記録した7人の外野手の1人であり、送球による守備貢献度を示すスタットキャストの指標『Arm Value』では、メジャーリーグ全体でトップだった」と、その強肩を評価している。
また、同記事では「ベンジは送球速度の指標『Arm Strength』で96.6マイル（約155.5キロ）を記録し、MLB全体で5位にランクインしている」と、強肩を裏付ける数字も紹介。新人ながら優れた守備力を発揮し、ナ・リーグ右翼手部門の最終候補に選出されたベンジの特徴にスポットを当てている。
キャロルについては、「肩の強さは平均以下であるものの、驚異的な守備範囲の広さでそれを補っている」と特徴を説明。さらに、「持ち前の卓越したスピードを生かして広範囲をカバーし、OAA（平均的な野手と比較してどれだけ多くのアウトを奪ったかを表す指標）は+10を記録した」と伝えている。
このOAAはMLB全体の95パーセンタイル（上位5％）に相当する。また、同記事は「昨季『ゴールドグラブ賞』の最終候補にも選出されたキャロルが、OAAで2桁の数値を記録するのはこれで3年連続となる」と紹介し、守備範囲の広さを継続して示している点を評価した。
『ゴールドグラブ賞』の受賞者は、現地11月1日に発表される。発表はアメリカ東部時間午後8時30分（日本時間2日午前10時30分）から、スポーツ専門局『ESPN』で行われる予定だ。

item.content:encoded:
An Outstanding first year as a Blue Jay 👨🏻 Dylan Cease is a Finalist for the @MLBPA’s Outstanding Pitcher Award!
Blue Jays’ Dylan Cease nominated for MLBPA’s outstanding pitcher award
Photo credit: John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images
Dylan Cease’s 2026 greatness has been recognized among his peers. 
On Wednesday, Cease was recognized as one of three American League finalists for outstanding pitcher in Major League Baseball Players Association’s Players Choice Awards. Cease was nominated alongside New York Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler and Boston Red Sox right-hander Sonny Gray. 
Signed by the Toronto Blue Jays to a seven-year, $210-million contract on December 2, 2025, Cease did nothing but impress in his first season north of the border. Cease made 29 starts and went 11-6 with a 2.40 ERA and a 1.10 WHIP. 
Cease struck out 239 batters – tied for third-most with Schlittler in Major League Baseball – and held opponents to a sparkling .180 average. The only pitcher in the majors who beat Cease’s mark of .180 was Milwaukee Brewers right-hander Jacob Misiorowski, who held opponents to a .157 average. 
The 30-year-old’s best month of the season came during July, when the right-hander made five starts and went 3-1 with a 1.00 ERA and 0.72 WHIP. Cease threw 36 innings and, during that span, struck out 46 batters and held opponents to a .125 average. 
Cease spent the month flirting with no-hitters, as on July 8, during a 10-0 win over the San Francisco Giants, the right-hander was three outs away from history before outfielder Heliot Ramos opened the bottom of the ninth with a leadoff single. 
Two starts later, on July 25, Cease turned in a pitching line of 9.0 IP, 1 H, 0 R, 0 ER, 3 BB, 12 K during a 6-0 win over the Boston Red Sox. Cease threw 120 pitches in the outing, in what could be one of MLB’s best pitching performances of the 2026 campaign. 
Unfortunately for Cease, he appeared to run out of gas in September. Following a start against the Texas Rangers on September 18, in which Cease allowed four runs (one earned) across 2.2 innings, it was announced he would head for imaging on his right shoulder. Five days later, Cease was placed on the 15-day injured list, ultimately ending his season. 
With no structural damage, Cease is expected to enter spring training healthy as he prepares for his second season with the Blue Jays.

item.title: [newstribune.com] Late-game homers send Brewers past Dodgers, into 3-0 NLCS lead | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla; Field Level Media
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Jake Bauers put his team’s determination on full display, getting the Milwaukee Brewers within one victory of their first World Series appearance in 44 years. Bauers turned an 11-pitch at-bat into a go-ahead two-run homer in the seventh inning as the Brewers took a commanding 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series with a 6-2 victory Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Dodgers. Milwaukee will aim for a sweep of the best-of-7 series tonight at Dodger Stadium. Garret
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Jake Bauers put his team’s determination on full display, getting the Milwaukee Brewers within one victory of their first World Series appearance in 44 years.
Bauers turned an 11-pitch at-bat into a go-ahead two-run homer in the seventh inning as the Brewers took a commanding 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series with a 6-2 victory Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Milwaukee will aim for a sweep of the best-of-7 series tonight at Dodger Stadium.
Garrett Mitchell followed Bauers with a homer of his own as the Southern California natives put on a show in front of family and friends in a ballpark where the home team has played the bully for more than a decade.
“We play for each other. It’s as simple as that, man,” Bauers said. “Any time there’s a mistake, an error, a walk, pitchers give up runs, hitters strike out in a big spot, the only thing anybody’s thinking about is how can I help pick that guy up? How can I help pick that guy up and do my part to win this game?”
Rookie left-hander Robert Gasser gave up three hits over five scoreless innings as the Brewers moved closer to the franchise’s second trip to the World Series. The Brewers made their lone Fall Classic appearance in 1982 as an American League team, losing in seven games to the St. Louis Cardinals.
Jackson Chourio led off the game with a first-pitch homer off Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell as Milwaukee showed its power capabilities after finishing last in the National League in homers during the regular season with 154.
“Job’s not finished yet,” Mitchell said. “Just got to take it a day at a time, not really worried about what’s happened today, what happened yesterday or what’s coming tomorrow. We’ve just got to show up and continue to play our brand of baseball and continue doing it for one another.”
Will Smith hit a two-run double for the Dodgers, who won the past two World Series titles. Los Angeles is trying to become the first National League club to win three consecutive Fall Classic championships.
Los Angeles manager Dave Roberts moved Shohei Ohtani to sixth in the batting order with the superstar in a postseason slump. Ohtani went 1-for-2 with a walk and a hit-by-pitch. The Dodgers’ offense was held to five hits in Game 3 after collecting three in Game 2.
“I haven’t digested this one,” Roberts said when asked about potential lineup changes for Game 4. “They’re going to run a bullpen game. Just trying to figure out which guys we want to be in there, how you kind of construct the lineup, but I haven’t thought about that one yet.”
Snell appeared to recover from Chourio’s ambush home run before he was rocked by consecutive home runs with no outs in the seventh. Snell (0-1) allowed four runs on four hits in six-plus innings with two walks and nine strikeouts.
“I just left the fastball over the middle to Bauers,” said Snell, who was in the Tampa Bay Rays organization with Bauers from 2015-18. “… I’ve seen the ups and downs he’s been through, and it’s been a lot of downs. So for him to go through this right now, he’s earned it. Hats off to him. What an at-bat.”
Trailing 1-0 from the jump, the Dodgers managed to put their leadoff batter on base in four of the first six innings before finally breaking through.
Gasser was replaced by right-hander Abner Uribe to open the sixth inning, and the reliever walked three of the first four batters he faced to load the bases, including a walk to Ohtani. Smith delivered a double off the wall in left-center field for a 2-1 lead after entering the game in a 1-for-25 slump.
Los Angeles failed to add onto the lead in the inning against left-hander DL Hall (3-0) when Enrique Hernandez and Tommy Edman struck out to end the threat.
Milwaukee responded immediately when Andrew Vaughn walked to open the seventh before Bauers’ epic at-bat. Two pitches later, Mitchell went over the wall in right-center field for a 4-2 advantage to end Snell’s outing.
Bauers had a similar plate appearance in Game 2 when he worked a 12-pitch walk with two outs in the third inning and Christian Yelich followed with a two-run single.
“Yeah, there was for sure a moment where I thought to myself like, ‘Oh, you’re in it again,’” Bauers said. “As far as the approach for the at-bat, I didn’t want to miss a fastball.”
The Brewers added to their lead in the eighth when Brice Turang scored on a Justin Wrobleski wild pitch, and Joey Ortiz tacked on an RBI single in the ninth.
Hall threw 2⅓ scoreless innings. Brewers closer Trevor Megill got the last four outs, striking out the final two batters, for his fourth save of the postseason.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers' Kyle Tucker makes 1 thing clear with LA facing NLCS elimination appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are one loss away from having their season end, but Kyle Tucker is not ready to write them off just yet. Los Angeles fell 6-2 to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series on Wednesday at Dodger Stadium, falling into a 3-0 series hole.
After the game, the star outfielder made it clear he still believes the Dodgers have what it takes to dig out of it.
"This team has won four games before, so that's what we're going to have to do," Tucker said. "I believe in this group, the staff, the clubhouse and guys in here. I think if there's a team to do it, it's this team, but it's not going to come easy, obviously."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"If there's a team to do it, it's this team."
Kyle Tucker on the #Dodgers facing a 3-0 series deficit in the #NLCS @CBSLosAngeles pic.twitter.com/45mwbGZhpU
— Sports Central LA (@SportsCentralLA) October 15, 2026
He also knows the Brewers are just as hungry. "They want to win as well, so we've just got to come out and get after it tomorrow," he said.
History is not on Los Angeles' side. The 2004 Boston Red Sox remain the only team in MLB history to win a best-of-seven postseason series after falling behind 3-0, rallying past the New York Yankees in the American League Championship Series. The Dodgers themselves have trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series only once before, when the Baltimore Orioles swept them in the 1966 World Series.
Still, there is a reason Tucker has faith in this group. The Dodgers are the two-time defending World Series champions, and they swept these same Brewers in four games in last year's NLCS. Tucker joined the club this past offseason on a four-year, $240 million deal.
To keep that run alive, the offense will have to wake up quickly. The Dodgers have scored only seven runs in three games, have yet to hit a home run in the series, and have struggled badly with runners in scoring position all postseason.
Milwaukee, meanwhile, has done almost everything right. Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back home runs in the seventh inning to flip Game 3, and the Brewers' bullpen has been nearly untouchable throughout October.
The Dodgers will try to stave off elimination in Game 4 on Thursday at Dodger Stadium, with the Brewers aiming to clinch their first National League pennant.
Related: Dodgers' Miguel Rojas calls out glaring culprit behind LA's 3-0 NLCS hole

item.content:encoded:
The 2026 MLB playoffs are in full swing!
The 12-team postseason began with an action-packed wild-card round that featured eight teams battling for four spots to advance to the eight-team division series.
The Chicago White Sox became the first team to win a series this postseason with a wild-card round sweep of the Houston Astros. Then the New York Yankees swept the Boston Red Sox in two routs, recording the highest series run differential in the history of the current wild-card format. The San Diego Padresalso sealed their spot in the NLDS with a sweep of the Chicago Cubs. In the only wild-card series to go the distance, the Atlanta Braves held off the Philadelphia Philliesto move on.
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Braves to nab the first spot in the championship series, where they are facing the Milwaukee Brewers after they beat the Padres.
The Tampa Bay Rays swept the Yankees to clinch the first spot in the ALCS and face the Cleveland Guardians, who mounted a stunning comeback against the White Sox after dropping the first two games of the ALDS.
From the first pitch of the wild-card games to the last out of the World Series, we've got you covered with the postseason bracket, schedules, results and how to watch every game this October.

item.dc:creator: Michael DeRosa

Due to this, New York should be aiming to strengthen their roster this offseason. One major need that the Yankees have heading into the offseason is another impactful power hitter. Because of this, they are now being urged to sign one of this year's top free agents from the C
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees once again failed to win the World Series this year after having high expectations.
After sweeping the Boston Red Sox in the AL Wild Card series, the Yankees got swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. Due to this, New York should be aiming to strengthen their roster this offseason.
One major need that the Yankees have heading into the offseason is another impactful power hitter. Because of this, they are now being urged to sign one of this year's top free agents from the Chicago Cubs.
New York Yankees Urged to Sign Cubs Star
Joe Najarian of SI.com urged the Yankees to sign Cubs star outfielder Seiya Suzuki this offseason in a recent article.
"But after his injury-plagued season, Judge will inevitably be limited to DH duties in the future. And given how good Suzuki was in 2026, the Yankees' post-Judge outfield would be in very good shape if they sign the Japanese slugger," Najarian wrote.
With the Yankees needing another star outfielder, it is understandable that they are being linked to him. He would certainly be a big addition to the Yankees' roster if signed. This is because he has shown throughout his career that he is a star.
Suzuki just had an impressive season with the Cubs, too. In 143 games in 2026, he recorded 26 home runs, 86 RBI, and a .270 batting average. This is after he had 32 home runs and 103 RBI in 2025 with Chicago. With numbers like these, he certainly would give New York's roster more pop if signed.
Should the Yankees Make This Move?
With Suzuki being a star, it would make a lot of sense for New York to sign Suzuki. Landing Suzuki would be massive for a Yankees club that wants to have better success in 2027. This is because he is a very impactful player when playing at his best and could thrive in New York.
Suzuki is exactly the kind of player that a contender like the Yankees should be adding, too. He has been consistently good at the plate and would simply make New York a more difficult team to go up against.
The Yankees will have a ton of competition to land Suzuki, though. This is because he is not only coming off a great season but is one of this year's top pending free agents. Thus, he will generate a lot of interest around the league. This will only heighten his value.
Although this is the case, it still makes sense for the Yankees to sign Suzuki. They need to win a World Series during the Judge era. Due to this, they are in a position to make a splash for Suzuki.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post New York Yankees Urged to Add Cubs Star in Massive Offseason Move appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
After setting a franchise record with an MLB-best 103 wins in the 2026 regular season, the Brewers are vying for their first World Series appearance since 1982, which remains the only trip to the fall classic in franchise history.
Chourio pounced on the first pitch of Game 3 of the National League Championship Series from Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell, parking it over the right-center-field fence for a home run. It was his sixth career postseason dinger at just 22 years old, breaking a tie with Contreras -- who has three long balls in the 2026 playoffs -- for the most in Brewers postseason history.
With both in mind, who is each team’s all-time postseason home run king? Here’s a breakdown of the players who hold a franchise’s playoff home run record.
American League East
Blue Jays: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. -- 8
Vladdy put together one of the single greatest individual postseason performances we’ve ever seen in 2025, leading the Blue Jays all the way to Game 7 of the World Series. After starting his postseason career with six homer-less games, Guerrero hit all eight of his October long balls in ‘25. He surpassed José Bautista (six) for the most home runs in Blue Jays playoff history. The dinger that earned Guerrero the franchise lead came off of Shohei Ohtani in the World Series, no less.
Orioles: Frank Robinson -- 9
The Hall of Famer had a knack for the clutch. Robinson's 26 career walk-off hits (regular season and postseason) are the most by any player since RBI became official in 1920. That knack extended to the playoffs, where Robinson posted an .887 OPS and slammed 10 total homers, including a franchise-best nine with the Orioles. Robinson won World Series MVP in 1966 after hitting go-ahead home runs in Games 1 and 4 of a Baltimore sweep over the Dodgers.
Rays: Randy Arozarena -- 11
Arozarena put the Rays on his back in the 2020 postseason, recording 29 hits -- at the time the most in a single postseason. Ten of those hits were home runs, giving Arozarena another single-postseason record and pulling him ahead of Evan Longoria (nine) for the most playoff homers in Rays franchise history. Oh, and Arozarena did all of this as a rookie. He tagged one more postseason big fly with the Rays in '21 before joining the Mariners via trade in 2024.
Red Sox: David Ortiz -- 17
Big Papi was an October legend in the truest sense of the phrase. His walk-off heroics helped the Red Sox overcome a 3-0 series deficit in the 2004 ALCS, paving the way for a curse-breaking World Series title. Ortiz’s 17 playoff home runs included two walk-offs and six with the Red Sox facing elimination.
Yankees: Bernie Williams -- 22
Williams played in the postseason in 12 consecutive years from 1995-2006, with huge moments at several turns. His 1996 performance -- an 1.142 OPS with six homers -- is one of the best postseasons of all time. Overall, his 22 long balls are fifth most by any player in playoff history, sharing a list with other Yankees legends like Derek Jeter (20) and Mickey Mantle (18).
AL Central
Guardians: Jim Thome -- 17
Thome hit all 17 of his postseason homers with Cleveland. He’s one of three players with multiple postseason grand slams, along with Francisco Lindor and Jason Varitek. Thome's grand slams came in Game 6 of the 1998 ALCS against the Yankees and Game 2 of the 1999 ALDS against the Red Sox.
Royals: George Brett -- 10
Brett is one of just 12 players who have hit three home runs in a single postseason game. His herculean effort came in Game 3 of the 1978 ALCS against the Yankees. Even though in defeat, Brett memorably whacked three pitches over the fence, one out to left field, one over the center-field fence, and one to right field.
Tigers: Miguel Cabrera -- 9
Cabrera’s most memorable postseason may have come as a rookie with the championship-winning Marlins in 2003 (more on that soon). But his most impactful playoff performance happened in 2011, when he launched four home runs with a 1.261 OPS in 11 games for the Tigers. He later passed Delmon Young’s eight career playoff home runs as a Tiger with a solo shot in Game 1 of the 2014 ALDS.
Twins: Kirby Puckett -- 5
Goose Goslin is the Twins' franchise leader in postseason home runs with seven, but Puckett holds the record since the club moved to Minnesota in 1961. Puckett took two trips to the postseason with the Twins, winning the World Series both times (1987 and 1991). The Hall of Famer was particularly impactful in ‘91, when he hit four dingers on an overall .333/.396/.667 slash line. That included an iconic 11th-inning walk-off homer in Game 6 of the Fall Classic.
White Sox: Paul Konerko -- 7
Konerko mashed five of his seven postseason homers during Chicago's 2005 title run, narrowly besting teammate Paul Crede (four HR) for the franchise lead. Konerko hit two of his long balls while earning ALCS MVP honors, then later launched a go-ahead grand slam in Game 2 of the World Series to down the Astros.
AL West
Angels: Troy Glaus -- 9
Glaus hit seven of his nine postseason homers with the Angels during the club's World Series campaign in 2022. Three of those were go-ahead long balls in the sixth inning or later, which is tied with the Astros' Yordan Alvarez (2022) for the most such home runs in a single postseason.
Athletics: José Canseco -- 7
In addition to holding the club's all-time postseason home run record, Canseco holds a share of the record for the most homers in a single postseason by an A's player. He slugged four big flies in 1988, helping lead the Athletics to the AL Pennant. Two years later, Canseco passed Al Simmons for the most postseason home runs in A's franchise history with a dinger in Game 2 of the 1990 World Series.
Astros: Jose Altuve -- 28
Altuve added to his stature as one of baseball's best postseason hitters in 2026. He clubbed a solo shot in Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series against the White Sox, putting him one home run behind Manny Ramirez for most all-time. And Altuve tends to meet the moment, too: A whopping 14 of his playoff homers have been of the game-tying or go-ahead variety, the most such homers in postseason history.
Mariners: Jay Buhner and Edgar Martinez -- 8
Buhner and Martinez each starred for the Mariners during the most successful era in franchise history, as the club made the playoffs four times between 1994 and 2001. Buhner took the early lead in career postseason homers, hitting four in ‘95 and two more in ‘97. But Martinez caught up to his longtime teammate in 2001 with a pair of long balls in the 2001 ALDS.
Rangers: Nelson Cruz -- 14
Cruz authored a historic postseason moment when he hit the first walk-off grand slam in postseason history in Game 2 of the 2011 ALCS against the Tigers. It remains one of just two walk-off postseason slams after Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman also accomplished the feat in Game 1 of the 2024 World Series. Cruz, the owner of 464 regular-season home runs, hit his last postseason homer at age 41 with the Rays, becoming the second-oldest player to go yard in a playoff game.
National League East
Braves: Chipper Jones -- 13
Jones starred for an Atlanta team that made 11 consecutive postseason appearances from 1995-2005. The eight-time All-Star broke onto the October stage in a big way in ‘95, slugging two home runs -- including the game-winning shot in the ninth inning -- in a 5-4 win over the Rockies in Game 1 of the NLDS. Jones and Austin Riley are the only two players in Braves history with multiple go-ahead homers in the eighth inning or later of a postseason game.
Marlins: Miguel Cabrera -- 4
A 20-year-old, baby-faced Cabrera looked at home in his first postseason in 2003, steering the Florida Marlins to the franchise’s second World Series title. Cabrera launched four home runs in the ‘03 playoffs -- his only with the Marlins -- which stands as the most home runs in a single postseason at age 20 or younger in MLB history. With a long ball off Yankees right-hander Roger Clemens in Game 4 of the World Series, Cabrera became the second youngest player to go yard in the Fall Classic.
Mets: Daniel Murphy -- 7
All seven of Murphy’s playoff home runs with the Mets came during a magical two-week stretch in 2015. The second baseman homered in six straight postseason games -- spanning Game 4 of the NLDS through Game 4 of the NLCS -- to steer the Mets to the NL Pennant. That’s the longest streak in a single postseason in MLB history. Even more impressive, Murphy homered off three former Cy Young winners: Clayton Kershaw, Zack Greinke and Jake Arrieta.
Nationals: Bryce Harper, Juan Soto, Anthony Rendon and Ryan Zimmerman -- 5
Four of the most iconic players in Nationals franchise history (since the team moved from Montreal to Washington) share this distinction. Youth is a popular theme here. At 19 years old and 362 days, Harper became the second-youngest player in MLB history to homer in a postseason game when he went deep in Game 5 of the 2012 NLDS. Seven years later, Soto (20 years, 346 days) became the sixth-youngest player to homer in the playoffs, teeing off for a two-run shot in Game 3 of the 2019 NLDS.
Phillies: Kyle Schwarber -- 13
Schwarber is one of the most prolific power hitters in playoff history: His 24 career playoff home runs rank third most all time, trailing only Ramirez and Altuve. He’s crushed 15 homers in a Phillies uniform, the latest being a 447-foot shot in Game 2 of the 2026 NL Wild Card Series against the Braves. In 2022, Schwarber keyed a stirring run to the World Series with three home runs in the NLCS against the Padres and three more dingers in the Fall Classic against the Astros.
NL Central
Brewers: Jackson Chourio -- 6
Chourio tattooed a pair of home runs to help the Brewers stave off elimination in Game 2 of the 2024 NL Wild Card Series, becoming the second-youngest player in postseason history with a multi-HR game (20 years & 205 days). He’s the only player in postseason history with a leadoff home run under age 22 -- which he’s done three times -- and the only player in MLB history with six playoff home runs before turning 23. Chourio's leadoff dinger off Blake Snell in Game 3 of the NLCS against the Dodgers as his latest feat of strength.
Cardinals: Albert Pujols -- 13
Who else but The Machine? Pujols slugged 19 career playoff home runs -- T-7th most all time -- including 13 with the Cardinals. The future Hall of Famer tagged Randy Johnson for his first career playoff homer in Game 2 of the 2001 NLDS, a surefire sign of things to come. Pujols is one of just 12 players to go deep three times in a postseason game, doing so in Game 3 of the 2011 World Series. He also launched one of the most iconic home runs in franchise history with a go-ahead, three-run shot onto the train tracks in Houston off All-Star closer Brad Lidge in Game 5 of the 2005 NLCS.
Cubs: Kris Bryant, Anthony Rizzo and Kyle Schwarber -- 6
Talk about a fitting trio: These three All-Stars propelled the Cubs to a curse-breaking, legacy-defining World Series title in 2016. Bryant (2) and Rizzo (1) each launched home runs in the Fall Classic, keying victories in Games 5 and 6 to spur a historic 3-1 series comeback. Schwarber, one of the best postseason power hitters of all time, launched six of his 24 playoff homers with the Cubs, including five dingers in his introduction to playoff baseball in 2015.
Pirates: Willie Stargell -- 7
The Hall of Fame slugger managed just two home runs while hitting .217 across his first 26 postseason games, spanning five different playoff appearances. But Stargell flipped the script in his age-39 season in 1979, smashing five home runs while earning NLCS and World Series MVP honors. Stargell’s two-run blast in the sixth inning of Game 7 of the ‘79 World Series proved to be the World Series-winning hit.
Reds: Johnny Bench -- 10
Bench played in 10 postseason series across his illustrious 17-year career and, rather remarkably, homered in all but one of them -- only going without a long ball in the 1975 NLCS. The Hall of Fame catcher’s only multi-HR playoff series came in the 1976 Fall Classic, when he swatted a pair of homers, posted a 1.667 OPS and took home World Series MVP honors for the Big Red Machine.
NL West
D-backs: Chris Young -- 5
Young only played in 12 postseason games for Arizona, but that was plenty of time to rewrite the franchise record books. His leadoff home run in Game 3 of the 2007 NLDS against the Cubs’ Rich Hill accounts for the only leadoff home run in D-backs franchise history. Four years later, Young slammed a pair of long balls in Game 4 of the NLDS against the Brewers. It remains the only multi-HR game by a Diamondbacks’ hitter in franchise history.
Dodgers: Max Muncy -- 19
Muncy homered three times in the 2026 NLDS against the Braves, pushing his total to 19 playoff home runs and extending the most in Dodgers postseason history. It’s a remarkable record for Muncy to hold, given his journey: He first joined the Dodgers organization on a Minor League contract in 2017, after he was released by the Athletics. The three-time All-Star owns some of the most important home runs in Dodgers history. That includes his 18th-inning walk-off in Game 3 of the 2018 World Series and his eighth-inning home run in Game 7 of the 2025 Fall Classic, which set the stage for a stirring late-game comeback.
Giants: Barry Bonds -- 8
Bonds made the postseason only four times in 15 seasons with the Giants. And while he launched more home runs (756) than anyone in baseball history, Bonds actually was held without a home run in three of those four trips to October. All eight of his playoff home runs with San Francisco came in 2002, when he posted a 1.559 OPS in 17 games while leading the Giants to the NL Pennant. The most memorable occurred in the ninth inning of Game 2 of the World Series, when he clobbered a blast to right field off closer Troy Percival. Arozarena (10, 2020 Rays) is the only player with more home runs in a single postseason.
Padres: Manny Machado -- 9
Machado extended his own franchise record in his first at-bat of the 2026 postseason, launching a home run in the first inning of Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series against the Cubs’ Matthew Boyd. Machado ushered in a new era of baseball in San Diego when he signed a 10-year deal ahead of the 2019 season, and the Padres have made the playoffs in five of the eight years since. The seven-time All-Star was at his best in the 2022 playoffs, helping San Diego win a pair of postseason series thanks to four home runs in 12 games.
Rockies: Matt Holliday -- 5
Holliday is responsible for one of the defining moments in Rockies history, although it has nothing to do with a home run: He belly-flopped into home plate to score the game-winning run in Game 163 in 2007, giving Colorado the Wild Card tiebreaker over San Diego. That mad dash set the stage for Holliday's only postseason stint with the club, which was wildly successful. The seven-time All-Star homered in each of his first two playoff games in the NLDS against the Phillies, and wound up with five long balls as the Rockies earned the franchise’s first World Series berth.
