item.content:encoded:
Brandon Valenzuela, el hermosillense finalista por el Guante de Oro de MLB en su año de novato: ¿contra quién compite?
El receptor sonorense de los Blue Jays de Toronto figura entre los tres mejores defensivos de su posición en la Liga Americana. Conoce a sus rivales y la lista completa de los 60 finalistas.
El beisbol mexicano tendrá representación en la disputa por el reconocimiento defensivo más importante de las Grandes Ligas. El receptor hermosillense Brandon Valenzuela, de los Blue Jays de Toronto, fue anunciado este miércoles 14 de octubre como uno de los finalistas al Guante de Oro 2026, después de destacar detrás del plato durante su primera temporada en MLB.
El sonorense, de 26 años, competirá por el reconocimiento al mejor receptor defensivo de la Liga Americana contra Dillon Dingler, de los Tigres de Detroit, y Austin Wells, de los Yankees de Nueva York.
La empresa Rawlings presentó a los 60 finalistas, distribuidos en 10 categorías por cada liga, incluyendo la posición de jugador utility. Los ganadores serán anunciados el próximo domingo 1 de noviembre.
¿Por qué Brandon Valenzuela fue nominado al Guante de Oro 2026?
La nominación del hermosillense representa uno de los logros más importantes de su joven trayectoria, especialmente porque llegó a las Grandes Ligas apenas el 5 de abril de 2026 y rápidamente logró establecerse como uno de los receptores defensivos más destacados.
Durante su temporada de novato, Valenzuela disputó 91 encuentros con Toronto y se ubicó entre los cinco mejores receptores de MLB en métricas defensivas avanzadas.
De acuerdo con Statcast y FanGraphs, sus números fueron los siguientes:
- +11 carreras de valor defensivo (Fielding Run Value), según Statcast.
- +13.6 en calificación defensiva, de acuerdo con FanGraphs.
- +8 carreras mediante el enmarcado de lanzamientos, una habilidad que ayuda a convertir pitcheos cercanos a la zona en strikes.
- +5 carreras por sus tiros a las bases, reflejando su capacidad para controlar los intentos de robo.
- 19 corredores retirados en intento de robo, con una efectividad aproximada del 30.2%.
- 1.88 segundos de tiempo promedio de tiro a segunda base, desde la recepción de la pelota hasta su llegada a la almohadilla.
El mexicano también aportó ofensivamente, al registrar un promedio de bateo de .222, nueve cuadrangulares y 23 carreras impulsadas.
Su rendimiento le permitió formar una destacada dupla de receptores mexicanos con Alejandro Kirk, otro de los jugadores de Toronto reconocidos por su capacidad defensiva.
¿Quiénes compiten contra Brandon Valenzuela por el Guante de Oro?
El camino del hermosillense hacia el premio no será sencillo, pues deberá superar a dos receptores con números defensivos sobresalientes.
- Dillon Dingler (Tigres de Detroit): Es el actual ganador del Guante de Oro de la Liga Americana. Terminó la temporada con +17 en valor defensivo y una calificación defensiva de +22.1, liderando ambas métricas entre los receptores.
- Austin Wells (Yankees de Nueva York): Destacó por su capacidad para recibir lanzamientos y bloquear pelotas en la tierra. Registró +10 carreras de valor defensivo durante 2026.
- Brandon Valenzuela (Blue Jays de Toronto): Se colocó entre los mejores receptores defensivos pese a disputar menos encuentros que varios de sus competidores.
Dingler buscará conquistar su segundo Guante de Oro consecutivo, mientras que Valenzuela y Wells aspiran a obtener el primero de sus carreras.
¿En qué equipo de la LMP juega Brandon Valenzuela?
Aunque Brandon Valenzuela es originario de Hermosillo, Sonora, actualmente sus derechos en la Liga Mexicana del Pacífico (LMP) pertenecen a los Águilas de Mexicali, organización que lo adquirió mediante un intercambio con los Naranjeros de Hermosillo.
El movimiento se hizo oficial el 17 de junio de 2025, cuando los Naranjeros enviaron al receptor sonorense a Mexicali a cambio del infielder Milán Tolentino, hijo del exbeisbolista naranjero José Tolentino. El acuerdo fue de carácter definitivo entre ambas organizaciones.
Antes de su salida, Valenzuela había tenido actividad con los Naranjeros durante la temporada 2024-25, en la que disputó 28 encuentros, conectó 21 imparables, incluidos ocho extrabases, produjo 10 carreras y terminó con un promedio de bateo de .259.
El cambio se concretó cuando el catcher todavía pertenecía a la organización de los Padres de San Diego en el beisbol estadounidense. Posteriormente, el 31 de julio de 2025, pasó a los Blue Jays de Toronto en otro intercambio, esta vez a nivel de Grandes Ligas, por el infielder Will Wagner.
¿Quiénes son todos los finalistas al Guante de Oro 2026 de la Liga Americana?
Además de Brandon Valenzuela, entre los candidatos de la Liga Americana aparecen figuras como Bobby Witt Jr., Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Jacob deGrom y Cody Bellinger.
| Posición | Finalistas |
|---|---|
| Lanzador | Tanner Bibee (Guardians), Jacob deGrom (Rangers), José Soriano (Blue Jays) |
| Receptor | Brandon Valenzuela (Blue Jays), Dillon Dingler (Tigres), Austin Wells (Yankees) |
| Primera base | Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (Blue Jays), Vinnie Pasquantino (Reales), Christian Walker (Astros) |
| Segunda base | Michael Massey (Reales), Chase Meidroth (White Sox), Cole Young (Marineros) |
| Tercera base | Caleb Durbin (Red Sox), Brooks Lee (Mellizos), Nick Loftin (Reales) |
| Campocorto | Andrés Giménez (Blue Jays), Taylor Walls (Rays), Bobby Witt Jr. (Reales) |
| Jardinero izquierdo | Cody Bellinger (Yankees), Wyatt Langford (Rangers), Chandler Simpson (Rays) |
| Jardinero central | Evan Carter (Rangers), Steven Kwan (Guardians), Ceddanne Rafaela (Red Sox) |
| Jardinero derecho | Wilyer Abreu (Red Sox), Nathan Lukes (Blue Jays), Cam Smith (Astros) |
| Utility | José Caballero (Yankees), Ezequiel Durán (Rangers), Zach McKinstry (Tigres) |
Los Blue Jays de Toronto encabezan la Liga Americana con cinco finalistas, incluyendo al hermosillense, Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Andrés Giménez, Nathan Lukes y José Soriano, quien también jugó para los Angelinos durante 2026.
¿Quiénes son todos los finalistas al Guante de Oro 2026 de la Liga Nacional?
En el Viejo Circuito, los Cachorros de Chicago también consiguieron cinco nominaciones, mientras que peloteros reconocidos como Chris Sale, Matt Olson, Dansby Swanson y Pete Crow-Armstrong buscarán sumar otro reconocimiento a sus trayectorias.
| Posición | Finalistas |
|---|---|
| Lanzador | Michael McGreevy (Cardenales), Nolan McLean (Mets), Chris Sale (Bravos) |
| Receptor | Freddy Fermín (Padres), Gabriel Moreno (Diamondbacks), Luis Torrens (Mets) |
| Primera base | Ty France (Padres), Matt Olson (Bravos), TJ Rumfield (Rockies) |
| Segunda base | Brandon Lowe (Piratas), Brice Turang (Cerveceros), JJ Wetherholt (Cardenales) |
| Tercera base | Alex Bregman (Cachorros), Max Muncy (Dodgers), Javier Sanoja (Marlins) |
| Campocorto | Geraldo Perdomo (Diamondbacks), Dansby Swanson (Cachorros), Masyn Winn (Cardenales) |
| Jardinero izquierdo | Jackson Chourio (Cerveceros), Ian Happ (Cachorros), Daylen Lile (Nacionales) |
| Jardinero central | Pete Crow-Armstrong (Cachorros), Michael Harris II (Bravos), Andy Pages (Dodgers) |
| Jardinero derecho | Carson Benge (Mets), Corbin Carroll (Diamondbacks), Seiya Suzuki (Cachorros) |
| Utility | Mauricio Dubón (Bravos), Jared Triolo (Piratas), Ildemaro Vargas (Diamondbacks) |
¿Cuándo se anunciarán los ganadores del Guante de Oro 2026 de MLB?
Los ganadores serán revelados el domingo 1 de noviembre de 2026, durante una edición especial de Baseball Tonight, transmitida por ESPN.
En las nueve posiciones tradicionales, los premios se determinan mediante dos componentes:
- 75%: Votación de los managers y entrenadores de Grandes Ligas, quienes no pueden seleccionar a jugadores de sus propios equipos.
- 25%: Índice Defensivo de la Sociedad para la Investigación del Beisbol Estadounidense (SABR), que utiliza estadísticas para evaluar el rendimiento defensivo.
La categoría de utility cuenta con una fórmula especializada desarrollada por Rawlings y SABR.
Posteriormente también se realizará la elección de los Guantes de Platino, que distinguen al mejor jugador defensivo de cada liga mediante una combinación de estadísticas y votaciones de los aficionados.
Para Brandon Valenzuela, la nominación representa una oportunidad de conquistar uno de los premios individuales más importantes de MLB en apenas su primera temporada, llevando el nombre de Hermosillo y Sonora a la élite defensiva del beisbol de Grandes Ligas.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Pat Murphy 'ticked' catcher William Contreras not a Gold Glove finalist
item.dc:creator: Todd Rosiak; Milwaukee Journal Sentinel
item.description: LOS ANGELES – Pat Murphy clearly had bigger fish to fry on Wednesday, Oct. 14 with his Milwaukee Brewers preparing to face the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series at Dodger Stadium. But there was some Brewers-adjacent news that broke earlier in the day that irked Murphy – one of his best players had seemingly been disrespected. William Contreras, whose 1,085 ⅔ innings and 9.064 pitches caught led the major leagues, was not among the three finalists at catcher
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES – Pat Murphy clearly had bigger fish to fry on Wednesday, Oct. 14 with his Milwaukee Brewers preparing to face the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series at Dodger Stadium.
But there was some Brewers-adjacent news that broke earlier in the day that irked Murphy – one of his best players had seemingly been disrespected.
William Contreras, whose 1,085 ⅔ innings and 9.064 pitches caught led the major leagues, was not among the three finalists at catcher in the National League for the Rawlings Gold Glove Award.
Those catchers were Freddy Fermin of the San Diego Padres, Gabriel Moreno of the Arizona Diamondbacks and Luis Torrens of the New York Mets.
"Contreras, he wasn't in there? Contreras?" said Murphy when asked initially for his reaction both to Brice Turang and Jackson Chourio being named finalists at second base and in left field, respectively, as well as any Brewers players he thought might have been snubbed.
"I'm biased. I get to see him 100-plus games catching. I think he caught the most games in the major leagues this year, and he was so important to us. They should come up with another award for William, because he's been incredible.
"So, if he's not on that list, ask for a redo."
The criteria is listed by Rawlings as the following:
To determine the winners of the 18 defensive position Awards, each team's manager and up to six coaches on his staff vote from a pool of qualified players in their League and cannot vote for players from their own team. In 2013, Rawlings added the SABR Defensive Index™ (SDI) to the Rawlings Gold Glove Award selection process, which comprises approximately 25 percent of the overall selection total, with the managers' and coaches' votes continuing to carry the majority.
To identify the utility Award winners, Rawlings collaborated with the Society for American Baseball Research (SABR) to create a specialized defensive formula separate from the traditional selection process for the Rawlings Gold Glove Award position winners. Utilizing the SABR formula and additional defensive statistics, Rawlings will select one utility winner from each League.
Looking at metrics, Contreras did rate out poorly in areas like framing (minus-6, 53rd out of 56 qualified catchers) and blocks above average (minus-7 on 4,361 opportunities). But with Contreras behind the plate, Brewers pitchers threw to a 3.32 ERA with the team ultimately going 80-41.
Contreras also threw out 28.4% of would-be basestealers (19 of 67).
Joey Ortiz also failed to make the cut as a utility player despite finishing 15th in the major leagues with 15 outs above average and also logged eight total defensive runs saved between third base and shortstop.
"Joey's a great defender," said Murphy. "I don't know the other guys in the league, but Joey, if given the chance to play every day on a team, you'd be hard-pressed to find a better defender. I don't know how all the voting takes place and everything. I know I vote, but I don't remember who was on there and who wasn't. You can't vote for your own players anyway.
"I try to just really vote for who I think is the best. I think you're doing a disservice if you try to like, 'Well, I don't want to vote for this guy because my guy's in competition.' I just voted for the guys that I think are the best. But for Contreras not to be on there, I don't know what it's based on. There's so many things in the catching position that you can't measure.
"So, now I'm kind of ticked about it now that you brought it up."
This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Pat Murphy 'ticked' catcher William Contreras not a Gold Glove finalist

item.content:encoded:
Technically speaking, this game is not a "must win" for the Los Angeles Dodgers. Down 2-0 in a best-of-seven gives, the back-to-back champs still have a tiny room for error, and they are back in the friendly confines of Chavez Ravine, where they went 51-33 during the regular season. No one is going to be putting them out to pasture just yet.
That said, it is entirely possible that they have simply come up against MLB's best team in the 2026 Milwaukee Brewers. The Brewers led the league in wins, runs scored, and run differential this season. The Dodgers were close behind in each of those metrics, but just like they were chasing the Brewers for the NL's number one seed during the final two months of the season, they seem to be a beat behind in the first two games of this series.
Shohei Ohtani's struggles are not a small part of the story here. He's 1-for-7 with three strikeouts in this series. This follows a nightmarish September for him in which he was injured and then underperforming. He is probably still hurt quite badly. At the same time, the rest of the lineup has also struggled. They have one extra-base hit through two games, and have gone 1-f0r-10 with runners in scoring position.
Brewers at Dodgers, 8:00 p.m., FS1
Brewers lead series 2-0
LHP Robert Gasser (5-5, 3.87 ERA) vs. LHP Blake Snell (4-1, 1.90 ERA)
How long will Snell stick around in this game? As long as he is effective. He last pitched on October 4 against the Braves. That day he worked 3.2 innings and allowed one run while walking five and striking out five. The lefty has never been known for his longevity, so if he gets through the order twice the Dodgers have to consider it a win.
Gasser worked four innings and allowed one run to the Padres in Game 4 of the NLDS, his most recent outing. He ended the regular season on a run of allowing four earned runs over his final four starts (22.2 innings). Similar to Snell, they will hope to get him through an order twice, and then turn to the bullpen.

Well, well, well. The Los Angeles Dodgers now have their backs against the wall and are starting off the Dodger Stadium portion of the 2026 National League Championship Series down 2-0 to the Milwaukee Brewers. Can Blake Snell and Shohei Ohtani figure it out? Will Robert Gasser, old friend William Contreras and the rest of the Brewers really put LA's attempt at a three-peat in serious jeopardy by taking a 3-0 win tonight? It's time to find out.
In case you're not here for the baseball and you just want to hang out, let us know what you've got going on tonight. We'd love to hear about it.
Anyways, the floor is now yours. Here's a clip of Walt Weiss (with hair) hitting a dinger back in the 1989 World Series.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Milwaukee Brewers Announce Sudden Christian Yelich Move Before NLCS Game 3
item.dc:creator: Cole Sullivan
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers hold a 2-0 series lead in the NLCS against the Los Angeles Dodgers entering Wednesday night as the series shifts to L.A. Left-hander Robert Gasser will take the mound for the Brewers, while the Dodgers will send out lefty Blake Snell. With Snell on the mound, Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy has made a sudden change to his starting lineup from Game 2. item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers hold a 2-0 series lead in the NLCS against the Los Angeles Dodgers entering Wednesday night as the series shifts to L.A.
Left-hander Robert Gasser will take the mound for the Brewers, while the Dodgers will send out lefty Blake Snell.
With Snell on the mound, Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy has made a sudden change to his starting lineup from Game 2.
Brewers Announce Christian Yelich Move
While most of the lineup will remain similar to what’s been working for them, Murphy has elected not to start veteran Christian Yelich.
Yelich has been a major part of the Brewers’ success this season and so far in October. However, he’s taken on more of a platoon role when left-handed pitchers take the mound.
We saw that in Game 1 when the Dodgers sent out Tarik Skubal. Yelich didn’t start that game. However, he hit fifth in the lineup in Game 2 and recorded two hits and two RBIs in the team’s 7-4 win.

Yelich’s 2026 Season With Brewers
In his 14th MLB season, Yelich has had to take a step back from being a surefire everyday player.
He rarely plays the field anymore, and that honestly fits the Brewers’ current roster.
Milwaukee has a plethora of players who fill different roles, which is a big reason the team finished the regular season with the best record in baseball and sits just two wins away from winning the National League and reaching the World Series.
Yelich has appeared in 118 games and is hitting .235 with 69 runs, 104 hits, 12 home runs and 59 RBIs.
In the postseason, he’s recorded at least one hit in every game, going 8-for-19 at the plate with two walks.

item.title: [NBC Sports] Brewers start Andrew Vaughn, sit Christian Yelich
item.dc:creator: Matthew Pouliot; Andrew Vaughn
item.description:
The Brewers have Andrew Vaughn batting cleanup and Christian Yelich out of the lineup for NLCS Game 3 against the Dodgers.
With a lefty back on the mound in Blake Snell, the Brewers are using the same nine they did in Game 1 versus Tarik Skubal. The lineup: LF Jackson Chourio, 2B Brice Turang, C William Contreras, DH Vaughn, 1B Jake Bauers, CF Garrett Mitchell, SS Cooper Pratt, RF Luis Lara, 3B Joey Ortiz.

item.title: [NBC Sports] Kyle Tucker takes over cleanup spot in NLCS Game 3
item.dc:creator: Matthew Pouliot; Kyle Tucker
item.description:
After four straight games of batting eighth, Kyle Tucker has been inserted into the cleanup spot for Game 3 against the Brewers.
Tucker hadn’t hit higher than sixth in the postseason. Tonight, Shohei Ohtani has been dropped to sixth, and Max Muncy is sitting initially against left-hander Robert Gasser. The lineup: SS Mookie Betts, 1B Freddie Freeman, LF Teoscar Hernández, RF Tucker, CF Andy Pages, DH Ohtani, C Will Smith, 3B Miguel Rojas, 2B Tommy Edman.
